options: Protect|Secure|Endanger|Guard
rubric: Jeopardize means to put at risk; endanger is the closest synonym.

subject: English Language
stem: The synonym for AUSTERE is ___
options: Luxurious|Severe|Soft|Comfortable
rubric: Austere means severe or strict; severe is its synonym.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the word nearest in meaning to QUERULOUS.
options: Cheerful|Happy|Complaining|Content
rubric: Querulous means complaining in a petulant or whining manner.

subject: English Language
stem: The word nearest in meaning to OBSCURE is ___
options: Clear|Famous|Unclear|Bright
rubric: Obscure means not easily understood or known; unclear is its synonym.

subject: English Language
stem: Select the synonym for FRUGAL.
options: Wasteful|Extravagant|Economical|Generous
rubric: Frugal means careful with money and resources; economical is the closest synonym.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of ANCIENT.
options: Historical|Old|Modern|Traditional
rubric: Ancient means very old; its antonym is Modern.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to BRAVE.
options: Courageous|Bold|Fearless|Cowardly
rubric: Brave means showing courage; its antonym is cowardly.

subject: English Language
stem: The antonym of ABUNDANT is ___
options: Many|Plentiful|Scarce|Much
rubric: Abundant means existing in large amounts; its antonym is scarce.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to CONSTRUCT.
options: Build|Create|Destroy|Repair
rubric: Construct means to build; its antonym is destroy.

subject: English Language
stem: The antonym of DILIGENT is ___
options: Busy|Hard-working|Lazy|Active
rubric: Diligent means hard-working and careful; its antonym is lazy.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of GENEROUS.
options: Helpful|Kind|Stingy|Giving
rubric: Generous means willing to give; its antonym is stingy.

subject: English Language
stem: The word most OPPOSITE in meaning to HUMBLE is ___
options: Modest|Quiet|Arrogant|Reserved
rubric: Humble means having a modest view of oneself; its antonym is arrogant.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of INNOCENT.
options: Pure|Blameless|Guilty|Honest
rubric: Innocent means not guilty; its antonym is guilty.

subject: English Language
stem: The antonym of OPTIMISTIC is ___
options: Hopeful|Cheerful|Pessimistic|Happy
rubric: Optimistic means hopeful about the future; its antonym is pessimistic.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to LENIENT.
options: Easy|Forgiving|Strict|Gentle
rubric: Lenient means tolerant and not strict; its antonym is strict.

subject: English Language
stem: The antonym of EXPAND is ___
options: Grow|Increase|Spread|Contract
rubric: Expand means to get bigger; its antonym is contract.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of SUPERIOR.
options: Better|Higher|Greater|Inferior
rubric: Superior means higher in rank or quality; its antonym is inferior.

subject: English Language
stem: The word most OPPOSITE in meaning to JOVIAL is ___
options: Happy|Funny|Cheerful|Gloomy
rubric: Jovial means cheerful and friendly; its antonym is gloomy.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of PRUDENT.
options: Wise|Careful|Sensible|Reckless
rubric: Prudent means acting with care; its antonym is reckless.

subject: English Language
stem: The antonym of RELUCTANT is ___
options: Hesitant|Unwilling|Eager|Slow
rubric: Reluctant means unwilling; its antonym is eager.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the word most OPPOSITE in meaning to TIMID.
options: Shy|Fearful|Bold|Nervous
rubric: Timid means shy and fearful; its antonym is bold.

subject: English Language
stem: The antonym of FORGIVE is ___
options: Pardon|Excuse|Blame|Release
rubric: Forgive means to pardon someone; its antonym is blame.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of NAIVE.
options: Innocent|Simple|Sophisticated|Trusting
rubric: Naive means lacking experience; its antonym is sophisticated.

subject: English Language
stem: The word most OPPOSITE in meaning to MODEST is ___
options: Quiet|Simple|Boastful|Reserved
rubric: Modest means having a low opinion of one's abilities; its antonym is boastful.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the antonym of KIND.
options: Nice|Good|Cruel|Helpful
rubric: Kind means being caring and gentle; its antonym is cruel.

subject: English Language
stem: Identify the noun in this sentence: 'The teacher praised the hardworking student.'
options: teacher|praised|hardworking|praised and teacher
rubric: A noun names a person, place or thing. 'teacher' and 'student' are nouns; 'teacher' is the first one.

subject: English Language
stem: In the sentence 'She runs every morning' the word 'runs' is a ___
options: Noun|Adjective|Verb|Adverb
rubric: A verb expresses action. 'runs' describes what she does — it is a verb.

subject: English Language
stem: In the sentence 'The beautiful garden attracts visitors' 'beautiful' is a ___
options: Noun|Verb|Adjective|Adverb
rubric: An adjective describes a noun. 'beautiful' describes the garden.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'He walked slowly' the word 'slowly' is a ___
options: Noun|Verb|Adjective|Adverb
rubric: An adverb modifies a verb. 'slowly' describes how he walked.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these is a collective noun?
options: Flock|Bird|Fly|Run
rubric: A collective noun names a group. A flock (of birds) is a collective noun.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these is an abstract noun?
options: Stone|River|Honesty|Teacher
rubric: An abstract noun names a quality or idea that cannot be physically touched.

subject: English Language
stem: In the sentence 'We went to Lagos' the word 'We' is a ___
options: Noun|Pronoun|Adjective|Verb
rubric: A pronoun replaces a noun. 'We' is a personal pronoun replacing a group of people.

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence uses a preposition correctly?
options: She sat on the chair.|The chair sat she on.|On the she sat chair.|She the chair on sat.
rubric: A preposition shows the relationship between a noun and other words. 'on' correctly shows where she sat.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'Wow! That was amazing!' the word 'Wow' is a ___
options: Noun|Verb|Interjection|Conjunction
rubric: An interjection expresses sudden emotion. 'Wow!' is an exclamation.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is a conjunction in this sentence: 'I was tired but I kept working.'?
options: tired|kept|but|working
rubric: A conjunction joins clauses. 'but' joins 'I was tired' and 'I kept working'.

subject: English Language
stem: A noun that can be counted is called a ___
options: Abstract noun|Proper noun|Countable noun|Collective noun
rubric: Countable nouns can have singular and plural forms and can be counted.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these is a proper noun?
options: city|country|Nigeria|river
rubric: A proper noun is the specific name of a person, place or thing and begins with a capital letter.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'She sang beautifully at the concert' identify the adverb.
options: sang|beautifully|concert|she
rubric: Adverbs modify verbs. 'beautifully' describes how she sang.

subject: English Language
stem: The plural of 'child' is ___
options: childs|childes|children|childre
rubric: Child has an irregular plural: children.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these is a possessive pronoun?
options: He|We|Their|Them
rubric: Possessive pronouns show ownership. 'Their' shows possession.

subject: English Language
stem: The superlative form of 'good' is ___
options: Gooder|Goodest|Better|Best
rubric: Good — comparative: better; superlative: best (irregular).

subject: English Language
stem: In 'The children played noisily in the park' identify the adjective.
options: noisily|played|park|The
rubric: 'The' is the definite article, which functions as an adjective modifying 'children'.

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
options: Amaka baked the cake.|The cake was baked by Amaka.|She is baking.|They bake cakes.
answer: The cake was baked by Amaka.
rubric: In passive voice the subject receives the action: 'the cake' is acted upon.

subject: English Language
stem: The comparative form of 'bad' is ___
options: Badder|Baddest|Worse|Worst
rubric: Bad — comparative: worse; superlative: worst (irregular).

subject: English Language
stem: A noun formed from a verb is called a ___
options: Adjective|Gerund|Pronoun|Adverb
rubric: A gerund is a verb form used as a noun (e.g. 'Swimming is fun').

subject: English Language
stem: In 'Neither Emeka nor Ada was present' the verb agrees with ___
options: Emeka|Ada|both Emeka and Ada|the teacher
rubric: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the noun closest to it — 'Ada'.

subject: English Language
stem: The plural of 'sheep' is ___
options: Sheeps|Sheepen|Sheep|Sheepes
rubric: Sheep is an invariant noun — its plural form is the same as its singular.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is a demonstrative pronoun?
options: Who|This|What|Which
rubric: Demonstrative pronouns point to specific things. This, that, these, these are demonstrative.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'The tall man entered the room quickly' how many adjectives are there?
options: One|Two|Three|Four
rubric: Only 'tall' is an adjective describing the man. 'quickly' is an adverb.

subject: English Language
stem: The word 'beautiful' becomes a noun when you add ___
options: -ly|-ness|-er|-est
rubric: Adding '-ness' to adjectives forms nouns: beautiful → beauty (or beautifulness).

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct verb form: 'Each of the students ___ a book.'
options: have|has|are having|had have
rubric: 'Each' is singular and takes a singular verb 'has'.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct form: 'Neither of the boys ___ ready.'
options: are|were|is|be
rubric: 'Neither' takes a singular verb: 'is'.

subject: English Language
stem: The sentence 'She has eaten the food' is in which tense?
options: Simple past|Present continuous|Present perfect|Past perfect
rubric: Present perfect uses 'has/have + past participle'. 'has eaten' is present perfect.

subject: English Language
stem: Change to past tense: 'He writes a letter.'
options: He write a letter.|He written a letter.|He wrote a letter.|He was writing a letter.
rubric: The simple past of 'writes' is 'wrote'.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct form: 'The news ___ good today.'
options: are|were|is|be
rubric: 'News' is uncountable and always takes a singular verb.

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: He don't know the answer.|He doesn't knows the answer.|He doesn't know the answer.|He do not knows the answer.
rubric: With he/she/it we use 'doesn't' (not 'don't') and the base verb 'know' (not 'knows').

subject: English Language
stem: The future tense of 'She runs' is ___
options: She ran|She has run|She will run|She is running
rubric: Simple future uses 'will + base verb'.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct verb: 'A number of students ___ absent today.'
options: is|was|are|has
rubric: 'A number of' takes a plural verb: 'are'.

subject: English Language
stem: Complete correctly: 'If I ___ a bird I would fly home.'
options: am|was|were|is
rubric: In subjunctive mood for unreal conditions we use 'were': 'If I were...'

subject: English Language
stem: Which is the correct form? 'The teacher as well as the students ___ present.'
options: were|are|is|have been
rubric: When 'as well as' joins subjects the verb agrees with the first subject 'teacher' — singular.

subject: English Language
stem: 'She had finished before he arrived.' This is in which tense?
options: Present perfect|Past perfect|Simple past|Past continuous
rubric: 'Had + past participle' is the past perfect tense showing one past action before another.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct form: 'Five thousand naira ___ a lot of money.'
options: are|were|is|be
rubric: Amounts of money are treated as singular even with plural-sounding numbers.

subject: English Language
stem: 'They are playing football now.' This sentence is in which tense?
options: Simple present|Present perfect|Present continuous|Past continuous
rubric: Present continuous = am/is/are + verb-ing; shows an action in progress now.

subject: English Language
stem: Change to reported speech: He said 'I am hungry.'
options: He said he is hungry.|He said he was hungry.|He said I was hungry.|He said he will be hungry.
rubric: In reported speech the pronoun changes to 'he' and the tense shifts back: 'am' → 'was'.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct form: 'The jury ___ divided in their opinion.'
options: is|was|are|were
rubric: When members of a group act individually 'jury' takes a plural verb.

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence uses the conditional correctly?
options: If she studies she will pass.|If she will study she will pass.|If she studied she will pass.|If she study she will pass.
answer: If she studies she will pass.
rubric: First conditional: if + present simple → will + base verb.

subject: English Language
stem: He ___ there for ten years before he left.
options: lived|has lived|had lived|was living
rubric: Past perfect shows an action completed before another past event.

subject: English Language
stem: The verb in 'It is raining heavily' is in which form?
options: Simple present|Present continuous|Present perfect|Past perfect
rubric: Am/is/are + verb-ing = present continuous; 'is raining' is present continuous.

subject: English Language
stem: Choose the correct form: 'Neither the manager nor the workers ___ informed.'
options: was|is|were|has
rubric: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearest subject 'workers' (plural).

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence is in simple present tense?
options: She was singing.|She sings every day.|She has sung.|She sang yesterday.
rubric: Simple present uses base verb + s/es for third person: 'sings'.

subject: English Language
stem: Identify the type of sentence: 'Open the door!'
options: Declarative|Interrogative|Imperative|Exclamatory
rubric: An imperative sentence gives a command or instruction.

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence is a compound sentence?
options: She ran.|She ran and he walked.|Because she ran she was tired.|She ran quickly.
rubric: A compound sentence joins two independent clauses with a conjunction.

subject: English Language
stem: Identify the type: 'I went home because I was tired.'
options: Simple|Compound|Complex|Compound-complex
rubric: A complex sentence has one independent clause and at least one dependent clause.

subject: English Language
stem: What is the direct object in: 'Amaka bought mangoes at the market.'?
options: Amaka|bought|mangoes|market
rubric: The direct object receives the action of the verb. Amaka bought what? Mangoes.

subject: English Language
stem: Identify the type: 'What a beautiful day!'
options: Declarative|Interrogative|Imperative|Exclamatory
rubric: An exclamatory sentence expresses strong emotion and ends with an exclamation mark.

subject: English Language
stem: A phrase that functions as a noun is called a ___
options: Noun clause|Adjective clause|Adverb clause|Relative clause
rubric: A noun clause performs the same function as a noun in a sentence.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'The boy who won the prize is my brother' the clause 'who won the prize' is a ___
options: Noun clause|Adjectival clause|Adverbial clause|Main clause
rubric: The relative clause 'who won the prize' modifies the noun 'boy'.

subject: English Language
stem: What is the subject in: 'The long distance running champions were honoured.'?
options: long|distance|running champions|The long distance running champions
rubric: The subject is the noun phrase that performs the action of the verb.

subject: English Language
stem: A sentence with only one main clause is called ___
options: Complex|Simple|Compound|Compound-complex
rubric: A simple sentence has one independent (main) clause with a subject and verb.

subject: English Language
stem: In the sentence 'He arrived before I finished' which is the main clause?
options: before I finished|He arrived|arrived before|finished and arrived
rubric: The main clause can stand alone as a complete sentence: 'He arrived'.

subject: English Language
stem: What punctuation mark ends an imperative sentence?
options: Full stop or exclamation mark|Comma|Question mark|Semicolon
rubric: Imperative sentences can end with a full stop or exclamation mark depending on urgency.

subject: English Language
stem: Identify the indirect object: 'The teacher gave the pupils a test.'
options: teacher|gave|pupils|test
rubric: The indirect object is the person/thing that receives the direct object — the pupils received the test.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these is NOT a sentence?
options: She cried.|Run!|In the morning sun.|They came.
rubric: A sentence must have a subject and a verb. 'In the morning sun' is only a phrase.

subject: English Language
stem: A conjunction that shows contrast is ___
options: And|Because|But|So
rubric: 'But' is an adversative conjunction showing contrast between two ideas.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'She dances when she is happy' identify the adverbial clause.
options: She dances|when|when she is happy|is happy
rubric: The adverbial clause 'when she is happy' tells the time/condition under which she dances.

subject: English Language
stem: Read: 'Chidi always woke up at 5 a.m. to study before school.' What does this tell us about Chidi?
options: He is lazy.|He is playful.|He is diligent.|He is sick.
rubric: Waking up early to study shows dedication and hard work — characteristics of a diligent person.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The sky darkened and thunder rumbled.' What is about to happen?
options: It will snow.|It will rain.|The sun will shine.|It will become windy only.
rubric: Dark skies and thunder are signs of an approaching rainstorm.

subject: English Language
stem: 'She bit her lip and stared at the ground.' What does this suggest?
options: She is happy.|She is nervous or uncomfortable.|She is hungry.|She is laughing.
rubric: Biting lips and avoiding eye contact are signs of nervousness or discomfort.

subject: English Language
stem: If a passage says a character 'beamed with pride' it means the character ___
options: Was sad|Was angry|Was very happy|Was surprised
rubric: Beaming means smiling broadly and radiating happiness or pride.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Despite the hardship he never gave up.' The word 'despite' shows ___
options: Reason|Result|Contrast|Addition
rubric: 'Despite' introduces a concessive clause showing that something happened contrary to expectation.

subject: English Language
stem: The title of a passage is most likely to be found ___
options: At the end of the passage|After the questions|At the beginning of the passage|In a footnote
answer: At the beginning of the passage
rubric: The title introduces the passage and is placed at the top.

subject: English Language
stem: To make an inference from a passage means to ___
options: Copy out the exact words|List all the characters|Draw conclusions from clues given|Count the number of paragraphs
rubric: Inference involves reading between the lines to understand implied meanings.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The vendor's wares were spread across the dusty road.' The word 'wares' means ___
options: Clothes|Goods for sale|Vehicles|Books
rubric: Wares refer to goods or commodities offered for sale.

subject: English Language
stem: A word or phrase that has the same meaning as another in the passage is its ___
options: Antonym|Synonym|Homonym|Acronym
rubric: Synonyms are words with similar or identical meanings.

subject: English Language
stem: When answering a comprehension question you should ___
options: Use only your own ideas|Copy the passage entirely|Use evidence from the passage|Guess randomly
rubric: Good comprehension answers are always supported by textual evidence.

subject: English Language
stem: 'He walked like a man carrying the weight of the world.' This is an example of ___
options: Alliteration|Personification|Simile|Hyperbole
rubric: This comparison uses 'like' making it a simile.

subject: English Language
stem: The main idea of a passage is ___
options: Found only in the last paragraph|The central message the writer wants to convey|A minor detail|Always stated in the first sentence
answer: The central message the writer wants to convey
rubric: The main idea is the overall message or argument of the entire passage.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The old woman's hands were gnarled like the roots of an ancient oak.' 'Gnarled' most likely means ___
options: Smooth|Young|Twisted and knobbly|Soft
rubric: The comparison to oak roots indicates twisted and rough hands.

subject: English Language
stem: In a comprehension exercise a summary requires you to ___
options: Retell every detail|State only opinions|Give the key points in fewer words|Copy all direct speech
answer: Give the key points in fewer words
rubric: A summary condenses the main points into a shorter form.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The scholar's demeanour commanded respect.' 'Demeanour' means ___
options: Clothing|Manner of behaving|Intelligence|Voice
rubric: Demeanour refers to the outward behaviour or conduct of a person.

subject: English Language
stem: What does it mean when a question asks for the 'tone' of a passage?
options: The loudness of the writer's voice|The writer's attitude or feeling|The length of the passage|The number of characters
rubric: Tone refers to the writer's attitude toward the subject or reader.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The village was a stone's throw away.' This expression means the village is ___
options: Far away|Very close|Behind a stone|Hard to find
rubric: 'A stone's throw away' is an idiom meaning very nearby.

subject: English Language
stem: To 'paraphrase' a sentence means to ___
options: Translate it|Write it backwards|Express it in different words|Add more sentences
rubric: Paraphrasing means rewording a passage while keeping the same meaning.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The politician's speech was full of rhetoric but lacked substance.' This suggests ___
options: The speech was excellent.|The speech sounded good but had little real content.|The politician was honest.|The speech was too short.
answer: The speech sounded good but had little real content.
rubric: Rhetoric without substance means impressive-sounding words with little meaningful content.

subject: English Language
stem: A word that imitates a sound is called ___
options: Simile|Onomatopoeia|Metaphor|Hyperbole
rubric: Onomatopoeia refers to words that imitate the sounds they describe (e.g. buzz, crash, sizzle).

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
options: its a fine day.|It's a fine day.|Its' a fine day.|Its a fine day.
rubric: 'It's' is a contraction of 'it is'. An apostrophe shows the omitted letter.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
options: Recieve|Beleive|Achieve|Peice
rubric: The rule is 'i before e except after c'. Achieve is correctly spelled.

subject: English Language
stem: A comma is used to ___
options: End a sentence|Show possession|Separate items in a list|Show a question
rubric: Commas separate items in a series and also separate clauses.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
options: Accomodation|Accommodation|Acomodation|Accomadation
rubric: Accommodation has double 'c' and double 'm': Accommodation.

subject: English Language
stem: The punctuation mark used at the end of a question is called a ___
options: Full stop|Comma|Question mark|Exclamation mark
rubric: All direct questions end with a question mark.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
options: Embarass|Embarrass|Embarras|Embaras
rubric: Embarrass has double 'r' and double 's': Embarrass.

subject: English Language
stem: Apostrophes are used to show ___
options: Plurals only|Possession and contraction|Questions|Exclamations
rubric: Apostrophes mark possessives (boy's) and contractions (don't = do not).

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is spelled correctly?
options: Necesary|Necessary|Necesasary|Neccessary
rubric: Necessary has one 'c' and double 's': Necessary.

subject: English Language
stem: Which sentence has the correct use of capital letters?
options: she lives in lagos.|She lives in Lagos.|she Lives in Lagos.|She lives In Lagos.
rubric: Sentences begin with capital letters and proper nouns (Lagos) are always capitalised.

subject: English Language
stem: A semicolon (;) is used to ___
options: End a sentence|Join two related independent clauses|Show possession|Separate letters
rubric: A semicolon links two closely related independent clauses without a conjunction.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is correctly spelled?
options: Goverment|Govenment|Government|Governmet
rubric: Government is spelled with 'ern': Government.

subject: English Language
stem: Which punctuation mark introduces a list or explanation?
options: Comma|Apostrophe|Colon|Hyphen
rubric: A colon (:) introduces a list, explanation or quotation.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is correctly spelled?
options: Seperate|Separate|Seprate|Seperrate
rubric: Separate is spelled: S-E-P-A-R-A-T-E.

subject: English Language
stem: In 'The children's books were on the shelf' the apostrophe shows ___
options: Contraction|Plural|Possession|Omission
rubric: Children's = belonging to the children — this is a possessive apostrophe.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word is correctly spelled?
options: Occured|Occurred|Ocurred|Ocured
rubric: Occurred doubles the 'r' when adding '-ed': Occurred.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Life is a journey' is an example of ___
options: Simile|Metaphor|Personification|Hyperbole
rubric: A metaphor directly compares two unlike things without using 'like' or 'as'.

subject: English Language
stem: 'She ran as fast as a cheetah' is an example of ___
options: Metaphor|Personification|Simile|Alliteration
rubric: A simile compares using 'as' or 'like'. 'as fast as a cheetah' is a simile.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The trees danced in the wind' is an example of ___
options: Simile|Hyperbole|Personification|Metaphor
rubric: Personification gives human qualities to non-human things. Trees cannot literally dance.

subject: English Language
stem: 'I have told you a million times!' is an example of ___
options: Metaphor|Simile|Hyperbole|Personification
rubric: Hyperbole is deliberate exaggeration for emphasis or effect.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers' contains ___
options: Rhyme|Hyperbole|Alliteration|Personification
rubric: Alliteration is the repetition of the same initial consonant sound in nearby words.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The thunder clapped' is an example of ___
options: Simile|Onomatopoeia|Metaphor|Alliteration
rubric: Onomatopoeia uses words that imitate sounds. 'Clapped' imitates the sound of thunder.

subject: English Language
stem: In the expression 'hit the nail on the head' the figure of speech used is ___
options: Simile|Metaphor|Personification|Idiom
rubric: An idiom is a phrase whose meaning differs from the literal meanings of its words.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The news was a dagger to his heart' uses which figure of speech?
options: Simile|Metaphor|Alliteration|Onomatopoeia
rubric: This is a metaphor — directly comparing news to a dagger without 'like' or 'as'.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Fair is foul and foul is fair' is an example of ___
options: Simile|Antithesis|Hyperbole|Alliteration
rubric: Antithesis places contrasting ideas in parallel structures for effect.

subject: English Language
stem: 'He is as brave as a lion' uses which figure of speech?
options: Metaphor|Personification|Simile|Irony
rubric: The comparison uses 'as... as' making it a simile.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The silence screamed at him' uses which figure of speech?
options: Simile|Hyperbole|Personification|Rhyme
rubric: Silence is given the human quality of screaming.

subject: English Language
stem: When a writer says the opposite of what is meant it is called ___
options: Metaphor|Hyperbole|Alliteration|Irony
rubric: Irony occurs when words are used to imply the opposite of their literal meaning.

subject: English Language
stem: 'She has a heart of gold' is an example of ___
options: Simile|Metaphor|Personification|Hyperbole
rubric: 'Heart of gold' directly compares the heart to gold without 'like' or 'as'.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Sweet smell of success' uses which figure of speech?
options: Alliteration|Synesthesia|Metaphor|Simile
rubric: Synesthesia applies one sense to another (smell applied to success).

subject: English Language
stem: The repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words is called ___
options: Alliteration|Assonance|Rhyme|Onomatopoeia
rubric: Assonance is the repetition of vowel sounds in closely placed words.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Kill two birds with one stone' is a ___
options: Simile|Metaphor|Idiom|Personification
rubric: This is a well-known idiom meaning to accomplish two things with one action.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The boy was a lion in battle' is an example of ___
options: Simile|Metaphor|Hyperbole|Alliteration
rubric: The boy is directly compared to a lion — no 'like' or 'as' so it is a metaphor.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Buzz, crack, hiss, splash' — these words are examples of ___
options: Metaphors|Alliteration|Onomatopoeia|Hyperbole
rubric: These words imitate the sounds they describe — this is onomatopoeia.

subject: English Language
stem: A statement that seems contradictory but contains truth is called ___
options: Simile|Paradox|Metaphor|Hyperbole
rubric: A paradox is a self-contradictory statement that reveals a deeper truth.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Break a leg!' before a performance is an example of ___
options: Metaphor|Simile|Idiom|Hyperbole
rubric: 'Break a leg' is an idiom meaning 'good luck' — its meaning is not literal.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word has the stress on the FIRST syllable?
options: Record (noun)|Record (verb)|Produce (verb)|Export (verb)
rubric: Nouns like 'REcord' are stressed on the first syllable; verbs 'reCORD' on the second.

subject: English Language
stem: How many syllables does the word 'BEAUTIFUL' have?
options: Two|Three|Four|Five
rubric: Beau-ti-ful = 3 syllables.

subject: English Language
stem: The vowel sound in 'SEAT' is ___
options: Short i|Long e|Short e|Long a
rubric: 'Seat' contains the long /iː/ vowel sound as in 'see', 'feet'.

subject: English Language
stem: Which pair of words are HOMOPHONES?
options: Bear and Bare|Bear and Beer|Bare and Beer|Bear and Pear
rubric: Homophones sound the same but are spelled differently. 'Bear' and 'Bare' both sound like /bɛr/.

subject: English Language
stem: The silent letter in 'KNIGHT' is ___
options: K|N|G|H
rubric: The 'k' in 'knight' is silent: it is pronounced 'nite'.

subject: English Language
stem: In the word 'PHOTOGRAPH' where does the primary stress fall?
options: pho|TO|graph|PHO
rubric: PHOtograph — stress on the first syllable: PHO-to-graph.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word rhymes with 'MOVE'?
options: Love|Cove|Groove|More
rubric: Groove rhymes with move — both end in the /uːv/ sound.

subject: English Language
stem: The consonant sound at the beginning of 'PHONE' is ___
rubric: 'Ph' in 'phone' makes the /f/ sound.

subject: English Language
stem: How many syllables are in 'INFORMATION'?
options: Three|Four|Five|Six
rubric: In-for-ma-tion = 4 syllables.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these words has the stress on the second syllable?
options: Table|Garden|Begin|Open
rubric: be-GIN — the stress is on the second syllable.

subject: English Language
stem: The silent letter in 'WRAP' is ___
options: W|R|A|P
rubric: In 'wrap' the 'w' is silent; it is pronounced 'rap'.

subject: English Language
stem: A falling intonation at the end of a sentence usually indicates ___
options: A question|A statement or command|Surprise|Uncertainty
rubric: Falling intonation shows finality — typical of statements and commands.

subject: English Language
stem: The vowel sound in 'HOT' is ___
options: Long o|Short o|Long a|Short a
rubric: 'Hot' contains the short /ɒ/ vowel sound.

subject: English Language
stem: In connected speech the linking of the final consonant of one word to the initial vowel of the next is called ___
options: Assimilation|Elision|Liaison|Intonation
rubric: Liaison (or linking) occurs when a final consonant connects to the next vowel: 'an apple'.

subject: English Language
stem: Which word has a silent 'B'?
options: Bomb|Rabbit|About|Rubber
rubric: In 'bomb' the 'b' at the end is silent: /bɒm/.

subject: English Language
stem: The word 'ACCENT' as a noun has stress on which syllable?
options: First|Second|Third|Last
rubric: As a noun: AC-cent. As a verb: ac-CENT.

subject: English Language
stem: How many syllables does 'EDUCATION' have?
options: Three|Four|Five|Six
rubric: Ed-u-ca-tion = 4 syllables.

subject: English Language
stem: Which of these is a diphthong?
options: The sound in 'sat'|The sound in 'sit'|The sound in 'say'|The sound in 'set
rubric: A diphthong is a gliding vowel that moves from one position to another. The /eɪ/ in 'say' is a diphthong.

subject: English Language
stem: Rising intonation at the end of a sentence usually indicates ___
options: A definite statement|A yes/no question|A command|A greeting
rubric: Yes/no questions typically end with rising intonation.

subject: English Language
stem: The number of phonemes in the word 'CHURCH' is ___
rubric: Church = /tʃ/ + /ɜː/ + /tʃ/ = 3 phonemes.

subject: English Language
stem: 'To bite the bullet' means ___
options: To eat bullets|To endure a painful situation bravely|To shoot someone|To bite food hastily
answer: To endure a painful situation bravely
rubric: This idiom means to endure a difficult situation with courage.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Barking up the wrong tree' means ___
options: Trying to climb a tree|Pursuing the wrong course of action|Making loud noises|Barking like a dog
answer: Pursuing the wrong course of action
rubric: This idiom means to make a false assumption about someone or something.

subject: English Language
stem: 'A stitch in time saves nine' means ___
options: Sewing is important|Learning to sew|Dealing with a problem early prevents bigger problems|Time is very valuable
answer: Dealing with a problem early prevents bigger problems
rubric: This proverb advises prompt action to prevent a small problem from becoming larger.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The ball is in your court' means ___
options: You are playing tennis|It is your turn to take action|The ball rolled away|You must buy a ball
answer: It is your turn to take action
rubric: This idiom means the responsibility or decision now lies with the other person.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Burning the midnight oil' means ___
options: Setting things on fire|Cooking late at night|Working or studying late into the night|Wasting oil
answer: Working or studying late into the night
rubric: This idiom refers to working very late when others are asleep.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Every cloud has a silver lining' means ___
options: Clouds are made of silver|There is always something good in bad situations|It will rain soon|Clouds are useful
answer: There is always something good in bad situations
rubric: This proverb means that even in difficult situations there is hope or something positive.

subject: English Language
stem: 'To have a bone to pick with someone' means ___
options: To share a meal|To have a complaint or dispute to settle|To pick up bones|To cook together
answer: To have a complaint or dispute to settle
rubric: This idiom means having a grievance to discuss with someone.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Spill the beans' means ___
options: To knock over a pot|To cook beans|To reveal a secret|To eat beans
rubric: This idiom means to accidentally or deliberately reveal confidential information.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The grass is always greener on the other side' means ___
options: Other places have better grass|People always think others have it better|Grass grows everywhere|You should travel more
answer: People always think others have it better
rubric: This proverb warns against envying others because their situation may not be as good as it seems.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Hit the nail on the head' means ___
options: To hammer correctly|To wound someone|To describe something exactly accurately|To fail a task
rubric: This idiom means to describe exactly what is correct or true.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Let sleeping dogs lie' means ___
options: Do not wake dogs|Avoid bringing up old problems|Allow dogs to sleep|Be kind to animals
rubric: This proverb advises against stirring up old conflicts or troubles.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Once in a blue moon' means ___
options: During a full moon|Whenever the sky is blue|Very rarely|Once every month
rubric: This idiom means something that happens very infrequently.

subject: English Language
stem: 'At the drop of a hat' means ___
options: When it rains|Without hesitation|After picking up a hat|With careful thought
rubric: This idiom means to do something immediately or without needing persuasion.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Two heads are better than one' means ___
options: Having two leaders is bad|Having two brains|Cooperation leads to better results|Two people always disagree
rubric: This proverb means that working together produces better results than working alone.

subject: English Language
stem: 'When in Rome do as the Romans do' means ___
options: Travel to Rome|Visit Italy|Adapt to the customs of the place you are in|Always follow Roman customs
answer: Adapt to the customs of the place you are in
rubric: This proverb advises adapting to local customs when visiting new places.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Don't judge a book by its cover' means ___
options: Read every book|Books have good covers|Do not judge things by their appearance|Always buy books
answer: Do not judge things by their appearance
rubric: This proverb warns against making judgments based solely on outward appearance.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Under the weather' means ___
options: Outdoors|In a storm|Feeling ill or unwell|Watching the weather
rubric: This idiom describes feeling sick or not well.

subject: English Language
stem: 'It takes two to tango' means ___
options: Dancing requires two people|You need a partner to dance|Both parties are responsible for a situation|Tango is a difficult dance
answer: Both parties are responsible for a situation
rubric: This proverb means that both parties in a conflict or relationship share responsibility.

subject: English Language
stem: 'Bite off more than you can chew' means ___
options: To eat too much|To try to do more than you can manage|To be greedy|To chew food properly
answer: To try to do more than you can manage
rubric: This idiom means to take on a task that is too much for one to handle.

subject: English Language
stem: 'The early bird catches the worm' means ___
options: Birds wake up early|Worms come out in the morning|Those who start early achieve more success|Early mornings are good
answer: Those who start early achieve more success
rubric: This proverb rewards early action and initiative.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Matter is best defined as anything that ___
options: Has colour|Has mass and occupies space|Is alive|Can be seen
rubric: Matter is defined as anything that has mass and occupies space (volume).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is NOT a state of matter?
options: Solid|Liquid|Gas|Energy
rubric: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid, and gas. Energy is not a state of matter.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The process by which a solid changes directly into a gas without passing through liquid state is called ___
options: Melting|Sublimation|Evaporation|Condensation
rubric: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas (e.g. dry ice/iodine crystals).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which state of matter has a definite shape and definite volume?
options: Gas|Liquid|Solid|Plasma
rubric: Solids have a fixed shape and volume because particles are tightly packed.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The change of state from liquid to gas is called ___
options: Condensation|Solidification|Evaporation|Sublimation
rubric: Evaporation is the process by which a liquid changes into gas/vapour.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which property is used to separate iron filings from sand?
options: Sieving|Filtration|Magnetic separation|Evaporation
rubric: Iron is magnetic; a magnet can separate it from non-magnetic sand.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The process of changing water vapour back into liquid water is called ___
options: Evaporation|Sublimation|Condensation|Melting
rubric: Condensation is the change from gas to liquid — the reverse of evaporation.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A mixture of salt and water can be separated by ___
options: Filtration|Evaporation|Magnetic separation|Sieving
rubric: Evaporating the water leaves the salt behind — used to separate dissolved solids from liquids.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a pure substance?
options: Seawater|Air|Distilled water|Soil
rubric: Pure substances contain only one type of particle. Distilled water is a pure substance.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Atoms of the same element that have different numbers of neutrons are called ___
options: Ions|Isotopes|Molecules|Compounds
rubric: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same proton number but different neutron numbers.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which process is used to separate two miscible liquids with different boiling points?
options: Filtration|Distillation|Crystallisation|Decantation
rubric: Distillation separates miscible liquids by their different boiling points.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The mass of an object divided by its volume gives its ___
options: Weight|Density|Pressure|Area
rubric: Density = mass ÷ volume.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a physical change?
options: Burning wood|Rusting iron|Melting ice|Cooking food
rubric: Melting ice is a physical change; the water can be refrozen — no new substance is formed.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: An element is a substance that ___
options: Is made of two or more materials|Cannot be broken down by chemical means|Is always a metal|Dissolves in water
answer: Cannot be broken down by chemical means
rubric: An element is the simplest pure substance that cannot be broken down chemically.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The particle model of matter states that all matter is made up of tiny ___
options: Atoms|Cells|Electrons|Waves
rubric: The particle model states that all matter is composed of tiny particles called atoms (or molecules).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which gas makes up the largest percentage of the atmosphere?
options: Oxygen|Carbon dioxide|Nitrogen|Argon
rubric: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere; oxygen about 21%.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is a compound?
options: Iron|Oxygen|Water|Carbon
rubric: Water (H₂O) is a compound — it is made of hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A substance that dissolves in a solvent is called a ___
options: Solvent|Solute|Solution|Suspension
rubric: The solute dissolves in the solvent to form a solution.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Rusting of iron is an example of a ___
options: Physical change|Reversible change|Chemical change|State change
rubric: Rust (iron oxide) is a new substance — rusting is a chemical (irreversible) change.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The SI unit of mass is the ___
options: Newton|Gram|Kilogram|Pound
rubric: The SI (International System) unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is NOT a method of separating mixtures?
options: Filtration|Distillation|Sublimation|Combustion
rubric: Combustion is a chemical reaction (burning) — not a method of separating mixtures.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Water is a compound because ___
options: It is a liquid|It contains hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined|It can be boiled|It has no colour
answer: It contains hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined
rubric: A compound is formed when two or more elements are chemically combined.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The process by which liquids change to solid on cooling is called ___
options: Melting|Freezing|Evaporation|Condensation
rubric: Freezing is the change of state from liquid to solid.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: In a solution the liquid in which the solute dissolves is the ___
options: Solute|Mixture|Solvent|Compound
rubric: The solvent is the liquid that dissolves the solute to form a solution.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a mixture?
options: Pure water|Common salt|Air|Nitrogen gas
rubric: Air is a mixture of gases including nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, and others.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of living things?
options: Growth|Respiration|Rusting|Reproduction
rubric: Rusting is a chemical process of non-living iron. MRS NERG — Movement, Respiration, Sensitivity, Nutrition, Excretion, Reproduction, Growth — are life characteristics.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The basic unit of life is the ___
options: Tissue|Organ|Cell|System
rubric: The cell is the smallest and most basic unit of all living organisms.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which part of the plant cell is not found in animal cells?
options: Cell membrane|Nucleus|Cell wall|Cytoplasm
rubric: Plant cells have a rigid cell wall made of cellulose; animal cells do not.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Photosynthesis occurs mainly in the ___
options: Roots|Stem|Leaves|Flowers
rubric: Leaves contain chlorophyll and are the main site of photosynthesis.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which gas is released during photosynthesis?
options: Carbon dioxide|Nitrogen|Oxygen|Hydrogen
rubric: During photosynthesis plants absorb CO₂ and water, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Organisms that make their own food are called ___
options: Consumers|Decomposers|Producers|Scavengers
rubric: Producers (plants/algae) make their own food via photosynthesis — they are autotrophs.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The process by which plants lose water through their leaves is called ___
options: Respiration|Transpiration|Photosynthesis|Excretion
rubric: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from plant leaves through stomata.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is an invertebrate?
options: Fish|Frog|Earthworm|Lizard
rubric: An invertebrate lacks a backbone. Fish, frog, and lizard are vertebrates; earthworm is not.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The green pigment in leaves that absorbs sunlight is called ___
options: Carotene|Chlorophyll|Melanin|Haemoglobin
rubric: Chlorophyll is the green pigment in plant chloroplasts that absorbs light for photosynthesis.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which organ in humans is responsible for pumping blood?
options: Lung|Brain|Kidney|Heart
rubric: The heart is the muscular organ that pumps blood around the body.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a mammal?
options: Eagle|Crocodile|Dolphin|Tilapia fish
rubric: Dolphins are mammals — they breathe air, are warm-blooded, and nurse young with milk.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The process of releasing energy from food in cells is called ___
options: Photosynthesis|Transpiration|Respiration|Digestion
rubric: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose to release energy (ATP).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which part of a flower contains pollen?
options: Pistil|Sepal|Anther|Stigma
rubric: The anther is the male part of a flower that produces and releases pollen.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Bacteria belong to which kingdom?
options: Plantae|Animalia|Fungi|Monera
rubric: Bacteria belong to the kingdom Monera (or Prokaryota) — they are prokaryotic organisms.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is the correct order of a food chain?
options: Consumer → Producer → Decomposer|Producer → Consumer → Decomposer|Decomposer → Producer → Consumer|Consumer → Decomposer → Producer
rubric: Energy flows from producers (plants) to consumers (animals) to decomposers.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The tiny pores on the underside of leaves through which gas exchange occurs are called ___
options: Stomata|Chloroplasts|Lenticels|Vacuoles
rubric: Stomata are microscopic pores that allow CO₂ in and O₂ and water vapour out.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these nutrients provides the most energy per gram?
options: Carbohydrate|Protein|Fat|Vitamins
rubric: Fats provide 9 kcal per gram — more than carbohydrates (4 kcal/g) or proteins (4 kcal/g).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The function of the kidneys in the human body is to ___
options: Pump blood|Filter waste from blood|Digest food|Produce bile
rubric: The kidneys filter blood to remove urea and other waste products, excreting them as urine.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which disease is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C?
options: Rickets|Night blindness|Scurvy|Beri-beri
rubric: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, characterised by bleeding gums and poor wound healing.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: An organism that feeds on both plants and animals is called a ___
options: Herbivore|Carnivore|Omnivore|Decomposer
rubric: Omnivores eat both plant and animal matter.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which part of the human digestive system absorbs most nutrients?
options: Stomach|Large intestine|Small intestine|Oesophagus
rubric: The small intestine is where most digestion and nutrient absorption occurs.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Malaria is caused by ___
options: A virus|A bacterium|A protozoan parasite|A fungus
rubric: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium, a protozoan parasite transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is the main function of the lungs?
options: Pumping blood|Absorbing nutrients|Gas exchange|Filtering waste
rubric: Lungs exchange oxygen from air with carbon dioxide from the blood.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma is called ___
options: Fertilisation|Germination|Pollination|Dispersal
rubric: Pollination is the transfer of pollen to the stigma before fertilisation can occur.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The deficiency of iron in the diet leads to ___
options: Kwashiorkor|Anaemia|Rickets|Goitre
rubric: Iron is needed to make haemoglobin; iron deficiency causes anaemia (low red blood cell count).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
options: Coal|Petroleum|Solar energy|Natural gas
rubric: Solar energy comes from the sun and is inexhaustible — it is renewable.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Heat transfer through a vacuum (empty space) occurs by ___
options: Conduction|Convection|Radiation|Evaporation
rubric: Only radiation can transfer heat through a vacuum (e.g. from the sun to Earth).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The transfer of heat through direct contact between particles is called ___
options: Radiation|Convection|Conduction|Insulation
rubric: Conduction is heat transfer through direct molecular contact, mainly in solids.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Sound travels FASTEST through ___
options: Vacuum|Air|Water|Steel
rubric: Sound travels fastest through solids (like steel) because particles are closely packed.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The unit of electrical power is the ___
options: Ampere|Volt|Watt|Ohm
rubric: Power (rate of energy use) is measured in watts (W).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which colour of the visible spectrum has the longest wavelength?
options: Violet|Blue|Green|Red
rubric: In the visible spectrum ROY G BIV — red has the longest wavelength and violet the shortest.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: An echo is caused by the ___ of sound.
options: Absorption|Reflection|Refraction|Diffraction
rubric: An echo occurs when sound waves reflect off a hard surface back to the listener.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a good conductor of heat?
options: Wood|Plastic|Rubber|Copper
rubric: Metals — especially copper — are excellent conductors of both heat and electricity.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The change of energy from one form to another is called ___
options: Energy conservation|Energy transformation|Energy storage|Energy transfer
rubric: Energy transformation (or conversion) is the change of energy from one form to another.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which device converts electrical energy into sound energy?
options: Generator|Motor|Loudspeaker|Bulb
rubric: A loudspeaker converts electrical signals into sound waves.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Light travels at a speed of approximately ___ m/s in a vacuum.
rubric: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s (300,000 km/s).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: When light passes from one medium to another it bends — this is called ___
options: Reflection|Refraction|Diffraction|Dispersion
rubric: Refraction is the bending of light as it passes from one medium into another.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable energy source?
options: Wind|Solar|Crude oil|Hydropower
rubric: Crude oil is a fossil fuel — it takes millions of years to form and will eventually run out.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The loudness of sound is measured in ___
options: Hertz|Metres|Decibels|Watts
rubric: The decibel (dB) is the unit of sound intensity/loudness.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The heating coil in an electric kettle converts electrical energy into ___
options: Light energy|Sound energy|Heat energy|Kinetic energy
rubric: An electric kettle's heating element converts electrical energy into heat.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is the best insulator of electricity?
options: Copper|Iron|Rubber|Aluminium
rubric: Rubber is an electrical insulator — it does not allow electric current to pass through it.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The pitch of a sound depends on its ___
options: Amplitude|Frequency|Speed|Wavelength
rubric: Pitch is determined by frequency: high frequency = high pitch; low frequency = low pitch.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The bending of light when it passes through a prism to produce a spectrum is called ___
options: Reflection|Refraction|Dispersion|Diffraction
rubric: Dispersion occurs when white light splits into its component colours passing through a prism.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A solar cell converts ___ energy into electrical energy.
options: Heat|Sound|Light|Kinetic
rubric: Solar cells (photovoltaic cells) convert light (solar) energy directly into electrical energy.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Heat transfer through the movement of fluids (liquids and gases) is called ___
options: Conduction|Radiation|Convection|Absorption
rubric: Convection is heat transfer via the movement of heated fluid particles.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The primary colours of light are ___
options: Red, Yellow, Blue|Red, Green, Blue|Red, Green, Yellow|Cyan, Magenta, Yellow
rubric: The primary colours of light are Red, Green, and Blue (RGB).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: An object that emits its own light is called ___
options: Luminous|Transparent|Opaque|Translucent
rubric: A luminous object produces its own light (e.g. the sun, a candle, a lamp).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is an example of potential energy?
options: A moving car|A flowing river|A stretched spring|A burning candle
rubric: A stretched spring stores elastic potential energy — energy due to its position/deformation.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following appliances uses the MOST electrical energy?
options: Mobile phone charger|Electric fan|Electric cooker|LED bulb
rubric: Electric cookers have very high wattage (1000–3000W) compared to other household appliances.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Sound CANNOT travel through ___
options: Water|Steel|Air|A vacuum
rubric: Sound requires a medium (matter) to travel; it cannot travel through a vacuum.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The tendency of an object to remain in its state of rest or uniform motion is called ___
options: Momentum|Inertia|Friction|Gravity
rubric: Inertia is the resistance of an object to a change in its state of motion (Newton's First Law).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The SI unit of force is the ___
options: Kilogram|Joule|Newton|Watt
rubric: Force is measured in newtons (N), named after Isaac Newton.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact is called ___
options: Gravity|Friction|Tension|Upthrust
rubric: Friction is the force that resists the relative motion of surfaces in contact.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Weight is different from mass because weight ___
options: Cannot be measured|Is the same everywhere|Varies with gravitational field strength|Is measured in kilograms
rubric: Weight = mass × gravitational field strength; mass is constant but weight varies by location.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is an effect of a force on a body?
options: It makes it invisible|It changes its shape size or state of motion|It removes its colour|It changes its smell
answer: It changes its shape size or state of motion
rubric: Forces can cause acceleration, deceleration, changes in direction, or changes in shape.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The upward force exerted by a fluid on a submerged object is called ___
options: Weight|Gravity|Upthrust (Buoyancy)|Normal reaction
rubric: Upthrust (Archimedes' principle) is the upward force exerted by a fluid on a submerged object.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Speed is calculated as ___
options: Distance × Time|Distance ÷ Time|Time ÷ Distance|Distance + Time
rubric: Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The gravitational force of attraction between the Earth and an object gives the object its ___
options: Mass|Weight|Density|Pressure
rubric: Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object; W = mg.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Friction can be REDUCED by ___
options: Roughening surfaces|Adding more weight|Lubricating with oil|Increasing contact area
rubric: Lubricants (oil, grease) reduce friction by creating a thin film between surfaces.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which type of friction acts on a stationary object being pushed but not yet moving?
options: Kinetic friction|Rolling friction|Static friction|Fluid friction
rubric: Static friction acts when an object is at rest; it must be overcome to start motion.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The formula for pressure is ___
options: Pressure = Force × Area|Pressure = Force ÷ Area|Pressure = Area ÷ Force|Pressure = Force + Area
rubric: Pressure is defined as force per unit area: P = F/A.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A body moving in a circle at constant speed is said to have ___
options: Uniform velocity|Uniform acceleration|Variable speed|Constant angular velocity
rubric: Objects in uniform circular motion travel at constant speed but changing direction, with constant angular velocity.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Newton's Third Law states that for every action there is ___
options: A greater reaction|An equal and opposite reaction|A smaller reaction|No reaction
rubric: Newton's Third Law: every action force has an equal and opposite reaction force.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The product of mass and velocity is called ___
options: Force|Energy|Momentum|Acceleration
rubric: Momentum = mass × velocity.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A ball thrown upward eventually falls back due to ___
options: Air resistance|Friction|Gravity|Magnetism
rubric: Gravity (earth's gravitational pull) causes the ball to decelerate and fall back.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The unit for measuring pressure is the ___
options: Newton|Pascal|Joule|Watt
rubric: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa) where 1 Pa = 1 N/m².

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt one because ___
options: It is lighter|The sharp edge has a smaller area — creating more pressure|It is harder|It moves faster
answer: The sharp edge has a smaller area — creating more pressure
rubric: P = F/A; smaller area with same force = greater pressure.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of ___
options: Distance|Speed|Velocity|Displacement
rubric: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time taken.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is a scalar quantity?
options: Velocity|Force|Weight|Speed
rubric: Speed has only magnitude (no direction) so it is a scalar. Velocity has magnitude and direction.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: If a car travels 120 km in 2 hours its average speed is ___
options: 240 km/h|60 km/h|24 km/h|0.6 km/h
rubric: Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 km/h.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A simple machine is a device that ___
options: Generates electricity|Makes work easier|Stores energy|Converts mass to energy
rubric: Simple machines allow work to be done with less effort or at greater convenience.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A lever consists of a rigid bar resting on a ___
options: Wheel|Incline|Fulcrum|Pulley
rubric: A lever is a rigid bar that pivots around a fixed point called the fulcrum.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: In a first-class lever the fulcrum is ___
options: Between the effort and load|At the effort end|At the load end|Above the load
rubric: In a first-class lever the fulcrum lies between the effort and the load (e.g. a see-saw).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A wheelbarrow is an example of which class of lever?
options: First class|Second class|Third class|Fourth class
rubric: In a wheelbarrow the load is between the fulcrum (wheel axle) and the effort — second-class lever.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is an example of a first-class lever?
options: Wheelbarrow|Bottle opener|See-saw|Fishing rod
rubric: A see-saw has the fulcrum in the middle between load and effort — first-class lever.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Mechanical advantage of a machine is the ratio of ___
options: Work output to work input|Load to effort|Effort to load|Velocity to acceleration
rubric: Mechanical Advantage = Load ÷ Effort; it shows how much a machine multiplies force.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: An inclined plane reduces the effort needed by ___
options: Increasing the load|Decreasing the distance|Spreading the work over a longer distance|Removing friction
answer: Spreading the work over a longer distance
rubric: An inclined plane increases the distance over which a force acts — reducing the required effort.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A screw is an example of an inclined plane wrapped around a ___
options: Cylinder|Cube|Sphere|Cone
rubric: A screw is essentially an inclined plane (thread) wrapped around a cylindrical shaft.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A pulley helps to ___
options: Create energy|Change the direction of a force or multiply force|Increase weight|Destroy machines
answer: Change the direction of a force or multiply force
rubric: Pulleys redirect force (single fixed pulley) or multiply it (block and tackle systems).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which simple machine is used to split or cut objects?
options: Lever|Wedge|Pulley|Wheel and axle
rubric: A wedge (like an axe or chisel) is used to split, separate or cut objects.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A door knob is an example of a ___
options: Lever|Wedge|Wheel and axle|Inclined plane
rubric: A door knob is a wheel and axle — the knob acts as the wheel and the spindle as the axle.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The efficiency of a machine is always less than 100% because ___
options: Work output exceeds work input|Energy is lost through friction|Machines have no mechanical advantage|Load exceeds effort
rubric: No machine is 100% efficient because some energy is always lost as heat due to friction.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: In a third-class lever the effort is ___
options: Between the fulcrum and the load|At the fulcrum|Beyond the load|Above the fulcrum
answer: Between the fulcrum and the load
rubric: In a third-class lever the effort lies between the fulcrum and the load (e.g. tweezers, fishing rod).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is an example of a wedge?
options: See-saw|Staircase|Chisel|Bicycle wheel
rubric: A chisel has a wedge-shaped cutting edge used to split wood or stone.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The velocity ratio of a pulley system with 3 ropes supporting the load is ___
rubric: Velocity Ratio of a pulley system equals the number of rope segments supporting the load.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Work done is calculated as ___
options: Force ÷ Distance|Force + Distance|Force × Distance|Distance ÷ Force
rubric: Work = Force × Distance (in the direction of force). SI unit is the joule.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A pair of scissors is an example of which type of lever?
options: First class|Second class|Third class|Pulley
rubric: Scissors have the fulcrum (pivot) between the effort (handles) and the load (cutting point).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which simple machine is a ramp?
options: Wedge|Pulley|Inclined plane|Lever
rubric: A ramp is an inclined plane — it reduces the effort needed to raise objects vertically.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: When the mechanical advantage of a machine is greater than 1 it means ___
options: The effort is greater than the load|The load is greater than the effort|The machine is inefficient|No work is done
answer: The load is greater than the effort
rubric: MA = Load/Effort; if MA > 1, Load > Effort — the machine multiplies force.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A bicycle pedal and gear system is an example of ___
options: Lever|Pulley|Wheel and axle|Wedge
rubric: Bicycle pedals and gears use the wheel and axle principle to transmit and multiply force.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: First aid is defined as the immediate help given to ___
options: A doctor|An injured or sick person before professional medical care arrives|Only unconscious people|Hospital patients
answer: An injured or sick person before professional medical care arrives
rubric: First aid is the first immediate assistance given to an injured or sick person.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which action should you take FIRST when someone is injured?
options: Call for help|Give food|Ensure your own safety|Run away
rubric: The primary rule in first aid: always ensure the scene is safe before approaching.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The correct way to stop minor external bleeding is to ___
options: Apply heat|Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth|Remove the wound covering|Leave the wound open
answer: Apply direct pressure with a clean cloth
rubric: Direct pressure slows or stops bleeding from minor wounds.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: What should you do if someone is unconscious but breathing?
options: Give them water|Place them in the recovery position|Start CPR immediately|Leave them face-up
answer: Place them in the recovery position
rubric: The recovery position keeps the airway open and prevents choking for unconscious but breathing patients.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A burn caused by electricity should be treated by ___
options: Removing the power source before touching the victim|Pouring water immediately|Touching the victim to check|Leaving the victim in contact
answer: Removing the power source before touching the victim
rubric: With electrical injuries always disconnect the power source before helping — never touch the victim while connected.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is the PRIMARY aim of first aid?
options: To permanently cure the patient|To preserve life reduce harm and promote recovery|To replace hospital treatment|To give medication
answer: To preserve life reduce harm and promote recovery
rubric: The three goals of first aid: preserve life, prevent worsening, promote recovery.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Safety goggles in a science laboratory are worn to protect ___
options: The hands|The ears|The eyes|The feet
rubric: Safety goggles protect the eyes from chemicals, flying particles, and sparks.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: If someone has a minor burn you should ___
options: Apply toothpaste|Apply butter or oil|Cool it with running cold water for 10–20 minutes|Burst any blisters
answer: Cool it with running cold water for 10–20 minutes
rubric: Cooling a burn with running water reduces pain and tissue damage.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The internationally recognised symbol for a first-aid kit is ___
options: A red crescent|A white cross on a green background|A red star|A blue square
answer: A white cross on a green background
rubric: The standard first-aid symbol is a white cross on a green background.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is NOT a basic content of a first-aid box?
options: Bandages|Antiseptic cream|Thermometer|Stethoscope
rubric: A stethoscope is a clinical diagnostic instrument, not a standard first-aid box item.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is performed when a person ___
options: Has a headache|Has a cold|Has stopped breathing and has no heartbeat|Is bleeding slightly
answer: Has stopped breathing and has no heartbeat
rubric: CPR is performed when both breathing and heartbeat have stopped (cardiac arrest).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: In the laboratory the correct way to smell chemicals is to ___
options: Sniff directly from the container|Waft the vapour gently towards your nose|Pour it on your hand|Use a straw
answer: Waft the vapour gently towards your nose
rubric: Wafting prevents inhaling concentrated fumes directly which could be hazardous.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: If a chemical splashes into your eyes you should immediately ___
options: Rub your eyes|Rinse with plenty of water|Apply eye drops|Close your eyes
rubric: Immediate flushing with clean water dilutes and removes the chemical.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: What does DRABC stand for in first aid?
options: Danger Response Airway Breathing Circulation|Doctor Run Ambulance Bandage Cream|Danger Rest Aid Breathe Call|Drug Recovery Airway Bandage Care
rubric: DRABC is a first-aid assessment protocol for approaching emergencies.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The safest way to handle broken glass in a laboratory is to ___
options: Pick it up with bare hands|Use a brush and dustpan|Use your foot|Leave it on the bench
rubric: Broken glass should always be swept up with a brush and dustpan — never bare hands.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is the correct way to put out a small chemical fire in a lab?
options: Water|Sand|Burning another chemical|Blowing it out
rubric: A sand bucket or CO₂ extinguisher should be used for chemical fires — water can spread them.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Disinfectants used in first aid help to ___
options: Stop bleeding|Kill germs and prevent infection|Relieve pain|Remove bandages
rubric: Antiseptics/disinfectants destroy microorganisms and prevent wound infections.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: What protective gear should be worn when handling acids in the laboratory?
options: Hat and sunglasses|Gloves and apron|Raincoat and boots|No protection needed
rubric: Acid-resistant gloves and a laboratory apron protect against chemical spills.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A fracture is defined as a ___
options: Tear in muscle|Broken or cracked bone|Skin wound|Joint dislocation
rubric: A fracture is a complete or partial break in a bone.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The 'R' in RICE treatment for sprains stands for ___
options: Run|Rest|Rinse|Reverse
rubric: RICE = Rest, Ice, Compression, Elevation — used for sprains and soft tissue injuries.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The input device used to enter text and numbers into a computer is the ___
options: Mouse|Monitor|Keyboard|Printer
rubric: A keyboard is the primary input device for typing text and numbers into a computer.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: RAM in computing stands for ___
options: Read and Memory|Random Access Memory|Read Accessible Memory|Rapid Access Module
rubric: RAM (Random Access Memory) is the computer's temporary working memory.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is an OUTPUT device?
options: Keyboard|Scanner|Monitor|Microphone
rubric: A monitor displays information — it is an output device.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The 'brain' of a computer is the ___
options: Monitor|Keyboard|Central Processing Unit (CPU)|Hard Disk
rubric: The CPU processes all instructions and is often called the brain of the computer.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: What does ICT stand for?
options: International Communication Technology|Information and Communication Technology|Integrated Computer Technology|Internet Computer Tools
rubric: ICT stands for Information and Communication Technology.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which tool is used for measuring length accurately in a workshop?
options: Ruler|Tape measure|Try square|Spirit level
rubric: A tape measure is used for measuring lengths — particularly for longer distances in workshop settings.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is used to cut wood in a workshop?
options: Chisel|Saw|File|Drill
rubric: A saw (hand saw or hacksaw) is used to cut wood and other materials.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A file is a workshop tool used for ___
options: Drilling holes|Measuring angles|Smoothing rough surfaces|Cutting thick metal
rubric: Files are used to smooth, shape and remove material from metal and wood surfaces.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a storage device?
options: Monitor|USB flash drive|Keyboard|Printer
rubric: A USB flash drive stores digital data — it is a portable storage device.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The Internet is best described as ___
options: A single large computer|A worldwide network of connected computers|A type of software|A storage device
answer: A worldwide network of connected computers
rubric: The Internet is a global network linking millions of computers worldwide.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Software used for word processing includes ___
options: Adobe Photoshop|Microsoft Excel|Microsoft Word|VLC Media Player
rubric: Microsoft Word is word-processing software used for typing and formatting text.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a RENEWABLE material?
options: Plastic|Steel|Timber (wood)|Aluminium
rubric: Timber comes from trees which can be replanted — making it a renewable material.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A try square is a workshop tool used for ___
options: Measuring weight|Checking or marking right angles|Cutting metal|Tightening bolts
rubric: A try square is used to check or mark 90° angles on wood and metal.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is the correct sequence for the engineering design process?
options: Build → Test → Design → Identify|Identify → Design → Build → Test|Test → Identify → Build → Design|Design → Identify → Test → Build
rubric: The engineering design process follows: Identify problem, Design, Build/prototype, Test/evaluate.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A spreadsheet application is used mainly for ___
options: Drawing pictures|Storing videos|Organising and calculating numerical data|Browsing the internet
rubric: Spreadsheet applications (like Excel) are used for organising data and performing calculations.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a property of metals?
options: They are poor conductors of electricity|They are generally non-lustrous|They are good conductors of heat and electricity|They cannot be melted
answer: They are good conductors of heat and electricity
rubric: Metals are generally good conductors of both heat and electricity.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A drill is used to ___
options: Cut flat surfaces|Make holes in materials|Smooth rough edges|Tighten screws
rubric: A drill (hand or electric) is used to bore holes in wood, metal, or masonry.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The function of a virus in computing is to ___
options: Speed up the computer|Help manage files|Damage or disrupt the computer system|Create backups
answer: Damage or disrupt the computer system
rubric: A computer virus is malicious software designed to damage, corrupt or disrupt systems.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following best describes construction?
options: The process of mining|The art of making clothes|The process of building structures|Manufacturing electronics
rubric: Construction refers to the process of creating buildings, roads, bridges and other structures.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Corrosion of metals can be prevented by ___
options: Leaving metal exposed to air|Painting or galvanising|Heating the metal|Cooling the metal
rubric: Protective coatings (paint, zinc galvanising) prevent metals from being exposed to oxygen and moisture.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which safety device automatically stops electricity flow in a circuit when overloaded?
