options: Switch|Battery|Fuse|Resistor
rubric: A fuse melts and breaks the circuit when current exceeds the safe limit.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: In technology the word 'prototype' means ___
options: A finished product|A first model made to test a design|A list of tools|A technical drawing
answer: A first model made to test a design
rubric: A prototype is an early sample model built to test a concept or design.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is a natural material?
options: Plastic|Glass|Cotton|Nylon
rubric: Cotton comes from the cotton plant — it is a natural material. Plastic, glass and nylon are synthetic.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Technology can be described as ___
options: Only computers and phones|The application of scientific knowledge to solve human problems|Reading and writing|Only machinery
answer: The application of scientific knowledge to solve human problems
rubric: Technology is the practical application of science and knowledge to meet human needs.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The spirit level is a tool used for ___
options: Measuring length|Checking that a surface is horizontal (level)|Cutting wood|Measuring temperature
answer: Checking that a surface is horizontal (level)
rubric: A spirit level uses a bubble in liquid to indicate whether a surface is perfectly horizontal.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A homogeneous mixture is one in which the components ___
options: Are visible to the naked eye|Are uniformly distributed throughout|Can be easily separated|Have different colours
rubric: In a homogeneous mixture the composition is uniform throughout (e.g. salt solution).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Iron and sulphur can be separated from their mixture by ___
options: Distillation|Filtration|Using a magnet|Evaporation
rubric: Iron is magnetic; a magnet can extract it from non-magnetic sulphur.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The temperature at which a solid changes to liquid is its ___
options: Boiling point|Freezing point|Melting point|Dew point
rubric: The melting point is the temperature at which a solid becomes a liquid.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is a property of non-metals?
options: They are shiny|They are good conductors of electricity|They are poor conductors of heat|They are malleable
answer: They are poor conductors of heat
rubric: Non-metals are generally poor conductors (insulators) of heat and electricity.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Water boils at ___ degrees Celsius at sea level.
rubric: Water boils at 100°C (212°F) at standard atmospheric pressure (sea level).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The process by which organisms produce offspring is called ___
options: Respiration|Nutrition|Reproduction|Excretion
rubric: Reproduction is the biological process by which organisms generate new individuals.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which organ in plants stores food?
options: Leaves|Roots|Stem|Flower
rubric: Many plants store food (starch) in their roots (e.g. cassava, carrot, yam).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The virus that causes AIDS is called ___
options: Malaria parasite|HIV|Tuberculosis bacterium|Cholera bacterium
rubric: AIDS is caused by the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is an example of asexual reproduction in plants?
options: Pollination|Budding of yeast|Cutting and grafting|Fertilisation
rubric: Cuttings and grafts propagate plants vegetatively (asexually) without seeds or fertilisation.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The largest organ of the human body is the ___
options: Brain|Liver|Skin|Heart
rubric: The skin is the largest organ of the human body by surface area.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The unit of electrical energy consumed by appliances is the ___
options: Watt|Joule|Kilowatt-hour|Ampere
rubric: Electricity bills are calculated in kilowatt-hours (kWh) — the commercial unit of energy.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following converts chemical energy into electrical energy?
options: Motor|Generator|Battery|Transformer
rubric: A battery converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: When a ball rolls down a slope its potential energy is converted to ___
options: Chemical energy|Kinetic energy|Electrical energy|Nuclear energy
rubric: As the ball descends, gravitational potential energy converts to kinetic (motion) energy.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Hydroelectric power generates electricity using ___
options: Coal combustion|The energy of flowing water|Solar panels|Nuclear fission
rubric: Hydroelectric power stations use the kinetic/potential energy of water to spin turbines.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following best describes the law of conservation of energy?
options: Energy can be created from nothing|Energy can be created and destroyed|Energy can neither be created nor destroyed but only transformed|Energy increases over time
answer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed but only transformed
rubric: The law of conservation of energy states energy is always conserved — only its form changes.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A body is in equilibrium when the net force acting on it is ___
options: Maximum|Minimum|Zero|Equal to its weight
rubric: A body is in equilibrium when all forces balance and the resultant force is zero.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The distance covered by a body per unit time is its ___
options: Acceleration|Velocity|Speed|Force
rubric: Speed = distance ÷ time; it measures how fast a body moves without regard to direction.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A car slows down gradually. This is an example of ___
options: Positive acceleration|Negative acceleration (deceleration)|Uniform velocity|Zero force
rubric: Slowing down means velocity is decreasing — this is negative acceleration or deceleration.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The force of attraction between any two masses in the universe is called ___
options: Magnetic force|Electrostatic force|Gravitational force|Frictional force
rubric: Newton's law of universal gravitation describes the attraction between any two masses.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Stretching of a spring obeys Hooke's Law which states that extension is ___ to the force applied.
options: Inversely proportional|Not related|Directly proportional|Equal
rubric: Hooke's Law: extension ∝ force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The work input of a machine is always ___ its work output.
options: Less than|Greater than or equal to|Equal to|Half of
rubric: Due to friction and other energy losses, work input is always ≥ work output.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Bottle openers work on the principle of a ___
options: Pulley|First-class lever|Second-class lever|Third-class lever
rubric: A bottle opener has the fulcrum at one end (tip) and load (bottle cap) in the middle — second-class lever.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Tweezers picking up objects are an example of a ___
options: First-class lever|Second-class lever|Third-class lever|Pulley
rubric: Tweezers have the effort between the fulcrum and the load — third-class lever.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A flagpole uses a ___
options: Wedge|Single movable pulley|Single fixed pulley|Lever
rubric: A flagpole rope runs over a fixed pulley which changes the direction of force (pull down to raise flag).

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The efficiency of a machine is calculated as ___
options: (Work input / Work output) × 100%|(Work output / Work input) × 100%|Work input − Work output|(Work output × Work input) × 100%
rubric: Efficiency = (Useful Work Output / Work Input) × 100%.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is the CORRECT way to remove a splinter from skin?
options: Pull with your teeth|Use clean tweezers sterilised with alcohol|Use dirty scissors|Squeeze hard
answer: Use clean tweezers sterilised with alcohol
rubric: Sterilised tweezers minimise infection risk when removing splinters.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Triangular bandages in a first-aid kit are used to ___
options: Clean wounds|Make slings for arm injuries|Take temperature|Record pulse rate
rubric: Triangular bandages are folded and used as slings to support injured arms.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A person who has fainted should be ___
options: Given water immediately|Left standing up|Laid flat with legs raised slightly|Put in a sitting position
answer: Laid flat with legs raised slightly
rubric: Raising the legs increases blood flow to the brain in a person who has fainted.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of these is a sign of a fracture?
options: Itching|Pain swelling and inability to move the limb|Sneezing|Blurred vision
answer: Pain swelling and inability to move the limb
rubric: Classic signs of fracture include localised pain, swelling, deformity and loss of function.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Mouth-to-mouth resuscitation helps a victim by ___
options: Warming their body|Providing oxygen to their lungs|Stopping bleeding|Providing food
rubric: Rescue breathing delivers air (oxygen) into the victim's lungs when they cannot breathe independently.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: An email is a method of ___
options: Video editing|Printing documents|Sending messages electronically|Storing music
rubric: Email (electronic mail) is used to send and receive messages electronically over the internet.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following is an example of open-source software?
options: Microsoft Windows|Adobe Photoshop|LibreOffice|Apple macOS
rubric: LibreOffice is free open-source office software; the others are proprietary.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The hacksaw is used to cut ___
options: Wood only|Metals and plastic|Cloth|Stone
rubric: A hacksaw has a fine-toothed blade designed for cutting metals and plastic.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A centre punch is used in workshop to ___
options: Smooth surfaces|Mark a starting point for drilling|Measure thickness|Tighten bolts
answer: Mark a starting point for drilling
rubric: A centre punch makes a small indentation to guide a drill bit so it doesn't slip.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which of the following best describes automation in technology?
options: Doing work manually|Using machines to perform tasks automatically|Reading books|Writing letters
answer: Using machines to perform tasks automatically
rubric: Automation is the use of technology to carry out processes with minimal human intervention.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: A paint finish on metal surfaces prevents ___
options: Conduction of heat|Rusting and corrosion|Magnetism|Hardness
rubric: Paint seals metal from air and moisture — the main causes of corrosion.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: Which computer component permanently stores the operating system?
options: RAM|CPU|ROM|Monitor
rubric: ROM (Read-Only Memory) permanently stores the firmware/operating system and cannot be easily changed.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The sandpaper used in woodwork is for ___
options: Cutting|Drilling|Smoothing surfaces|Measuring
rubric: Sandpaper (abrasive paper) is used to smooth wood and remove surface imperfections.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: In a workshop a mallet is different from a hammer because a mallet has a ___
options: Metal head|Heavy metal face|Wooden or rubber head|Sharp edge
rubric: A mallet has a softer head (wood or rubber) to avoid damaging surfaces when striking chisels.

subject: Basic Science & Technology
stem: The abbreviation 'PDF' stands for ___
options: Portable Document Format|Personal Data File|Printed Data Form|Page Document File
rubric: PDF stands for Portable Document Format — a widely used file format for documents.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The smallest and most basic unit of society is the ___
options: State|School|Family|Community
rubric: The family is the fundamental unit of society from which all larger social groups develop.

subject: Social Studies
stem: An extended family consists of ___
options: Only parents and children|Parents children and other close relatives|Only the husband and wife|Neighbours and friends
answer: Parents children and other close relatives
rubric: An extended family includes grandparents, aunts, uncles, cousins and other relatives beyond the nuclear family.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a PRIMARY agent of socialisation?
options: School|Church|Peer group|Mass media
rubric: Primary agents of socialisation include the family and school — the first major institutions shaping behaviour.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The process by which individuals learn the norms and values of their society is called ___
options: Education|Socialisation|Colonisation|Industrialisation
rubric: Socialisation is the lifelong process through which people learn cultural norms and values.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A community can be defined as a group of people who ___
options: Look alike|Live in the same area and share common interests|Have the same religion only|Work in the same office
answer: Live in the same area and share common interests
rubric: A community is defined by shared location, interests and identity.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a function of the family?
options: Tax collection|Law enforcement|Socialisation of children|Making national laws
rubric: One of the primary functions of the family is to socialise children into the norms of society.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The nuclear family is made up of ___
options: Parents their children and grandparents|Only husband and wife with their children|Husband wife and all relatives|The entire village
answer: Only husband and wife with their children
rubric: The nuclear family consists of only parents and their unmarried children.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these represents a SECONDARY group in society?
options: Nuclear family|Extended family|A political party|A pair of siblings
rubric: Secondary groups (like parties, clubs) are larger and less personal than primary groups (family).

subject: Social Studies
stem: Rural-urban migration refers to ___
options: Movement of goods from farms to cities|The movement of people from rural to urban areas|City expansion|Industrial growth
answer: The movement of people from rural to urban areas
rubric: Rural-urban migration is the movement of people from villages/rural areas to towns/cities.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Urbanisation is best defined as ___
options: The process of building roads|The growth of cities and the movement of people to urban areas|The development of farmland|Building more schools
answer: The growth of cities and the movement of people to urban areas
rubric: Urbanisation describes the population shift from rural areas to urban centres.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is a challenge associated with rapid urbanisation in Nigeria?
options: Low birth rate|Overcrowding and slums|Excess food production|Too many schools
rubric: Rapid urbanisation leads to overcrowding, inadequate housing, slums and pressure on infrastructure.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The institution responsible for formal education in a community is ___
options: The family|The school|The marketplace|The farm
rubric: The school is the primary formal institution for education and intellectual development.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A monogamous family is one in which a man has ___
options: Many wives|Two wives|One wife|No wife
rubric: Monogamy is the practice of having only one spouse at a time.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a function of a community?
options: Printing money|Providing security and mutual support for its members|Electing the president|Making foreign policy
answer: Providing security and mutual support for its members
rubric: Communities provide shared support, security, social services and a sense of belonging.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The head of a traditional Nigerian family compound is usually called the ___
options: Governor|Mayor|Patriarch (oldest male)|Prime minister
rubric: In many Nigerian cultures the patriarch (eldest male) leads the family compound.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is a way of maintaining peace in a community?
options: Spreading rumours|Engaging in conflict|Dialogue and respect for others|Bullying neighbours
rubric: Peaceful coexistence in communities relies on dialogue, tolerance and mutual respect.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Social values are ___
options: Only found in books|Standards and principles that guide behaviour in society|Imposed by foreign governments|Rules made only by the police
answer: Standards and principles that guide behaviour in society
rubric: Social values (honesty, respect, hard work) guide acceptable conduct within a community.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is an effect of poverty on a family?
options: Better nutrition|Higher education|Inability to meet basic needs|Improved health
rubric: Poverty prevents families from meeting needs for food, shelter, healthcare and education.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The term 'polygamy' refers to ___
options: Having no spouse|Having only one spouse|Having more than one spouse|Marrying a foreigner
rubric: Polygamy is the practice of having more than one spouse — includes polygyny (multiple wives) and polyandry.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which type of family system is dominant in traditional Yoruba and Igbo societies?
options: Nuclear|Single-parent|Extended|Foster
rubric: Traditional Nigerian cultures (Yoruba, Igbo, Hausa) are predominantly organised around extended family systems.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Culture can be defined as ___
options: The government of a country|The way of life of a people|Only the music and dance of a group|The laws of a nation
answer: The way of life of a people
rubric: Culture encompasses the beliefs, customs, language, art, and practices of a group of people.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a MATERIAL aspect of culture?
options: Beliefs|Values|Clothing and tools|Language
rubric: Material culture refers to physical objects made by a society — tools, clothing, buildings.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A norm is best described as ___
options: A personal habit|An accepted rule or standard of behaviour in society|A government law|A religious belief only
answer: An accepted rule or standard of behaviour in society
rubric: Norms are shared expectations that guide behaviour within a group or society.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The spread of cultural traits from one society to another is called ___
options: Acculturation|Cultural diffusion|Socialisation|Assimilation
rubric: Cultural diffusion is the spread of cultural elements (ideas, styles, religion) from one group to another.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A taboo in a culture refers to ___
options: A traditional food|Something strictly forbidden by cultural norms|A type of music|A religious festival
answer: Something strictly forbidden by cultural norms
rubric: Taboos are acts or things that are forbidden based on cultural or religious beliefs.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The practice of female genital mutilation (FGM) is a harmful cultural practice because ___
options: It is expensive|It causes serious physical and psychological harm|It is foreign|It is not traditional
answer: It causes serious physical and psychological harm
rubric: FGM is a harmful cultural practice condemned internationally for the physical and psychological harm it causes.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a positive cultural value in Nigerian society?
options: Corruption|Laziness|Respect for elders|Discrimination
rubric: Respect for elders is a positive cultural value across Nigerian ethnic groups.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Multiculturalism means ___
options: Having only one culture|The coexistence of multiple cultures within a society|Rejecting other cultures|Following only Western culture
answer: The coexistence of multiple cultures within a society
rubric: Multiculturalism acknowledges and celebrates the presence of diverse cultures in one society.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Cultural heritage includes ___
options: Only modern inventions|The tangible and intangible legacies passed from earlier generations|Only foreign arts|Government records only
answer: The tangible and intangible legacies passed from earlier generations
rubric: Cultural heritage encompasses traditions, monuments, language, arts and practices passed down generations.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following BEST promotes national unity in Nigeria?
options: Tribalism|Nepotism|Respect for diverse cultures and religions|Promoting only one language
answer: Respect for diverse cultures and religions
rubric: Tolerance and respect for Nigeria's diversity fosters unity among its over 250 ethnic groups.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Social change refers to ___
options: Changes in only the government|Alterations in the structure and institutions of society over time|Changes in clothing only|Permanent unchanging traditions
answer: Alterations in the structure and institutions of society over time
rubric: Social change describes the transformation of culture, institutions and social structures over time.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is an example of non-material culture?
options: Buildings|Clothing|Language|Food
rubric: Non-material culture includes intangible elements such as language, beliefs, values and norms.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Ethnocentrism means judging other cultures ___
options: Fairly and openly|Using the standards of one's own culture|By their economic strength|Using international standards
answer: Using the standards of one's own culture
rubric: Ethnocentrism is the tendency to view other cultures from the perspective of one's own culture as superior.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Inter-ethnic marriage in Nigeria helps to ___
options: Increase tribalism|Promote national unity and integration|Weaken families|Cause more conflict
rubric: Inter-ethnic marriages create cross-cultural bonds that reduce ethnic tensions and build national unity.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which agency is responsible for promoting Nigeria's cultural heritage?
options: NAFDAC|EFCC|National Commission for Museums and Monuments|INEC
answer: National Commission for Museums and Monuments
rubric: The National Commission for Museums and Monuments (NCMM) preserves and promotes Nigeria's cultural heritage.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Patriotism means ___
options: Love and devotion to one's country|Disregard for one's nation|Preferring foreign countries|Criticising the government always
answer: Love and devotion to one's country
rubric: Patriotism is a strong feeling of love, loyalty and devotion to one's nation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is a harmful traditional practice?
options: Naming ceremonies|Dowry payment|Child marriage|Festival celebrations
rubric: Child marriage denies children their rights, education and health — it is a harmful traditional practice.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The process by which a person of one culture fully adopts the culture of another is called ___
options: Diffusion|Acculturation|Assimilation|Socialisation
rubric: Assimilation is when an individual fully adopts and is absorbed into another culture.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of cultural diversity in Nigeria?
options: All Nigerians speak one language|Nigeria has over 250 ethnic groups with different languages|Nigeria has one religion|All Nigerians wear the same dress
answer: Nigeria has over 250 ethnic groups with different languages
rubric: Nigeria is culturally diverse with over 250 ethnic groups, multiple languages and religions.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Community development is best achieved through ___
options: Individual selfishness|Corruption|Collective effort and cooperation of community members|Government alone
answer: Collective effort and cooperation of community members
rubric: Community development thrives when residents work together for shared goals.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria is currently operating under which type of government?
options: Monarchy|Military dictatorship|Federal democracy|Communism
rubric: Nigeria operates a federal democratic republic with elected representatives at all levels.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Nigerian constitution is the ___
options: President's personal rules|Supreme law of the land|State governor's orders|Decisions of the police
rubric: The constitution is the highest law; all other laws must be consistent with it.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria has ___ states and a Federal Capital Territory.
rubric: Nigeria has 36 states plus the FCT (Abuja), giving 37 administrative units in total.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The three arms of government in Nigeria are ___
options: Executive legislative and military|Executive legislative and judiciary|Police judiciary and executive|Military police and legislature
rubric: The three arms of government are the Executive, Legislative and Judiciary.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The arm of government responsible for making laws in Nigeria is the ___
options: Executive|Judiciary|Legislature (National Assembly)|Police
rubric: The Legislature (National Assembly) makes federal laws in Nigeria.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Nigerian National Assembly is made up of the ___
options: House of Representatives only|Senate only|Senate and House of Representatives|Senate and State Houses
rubric: Nigeria's bicameral legislature consists of the Senate (upper) and House of Representatives (lower).

subject: Social Studies
stem: The head of the executive arm of Nigeria's federal government is the ___
options: Senate President|Chief Justice|President|Governor
rubric: The President of Nigeria heads the Executive arm of the federal government.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The judiciary in Nigeria is responsible for ___
options: Making laws|Implementing government policies|Interpreting laws and settling disputes|Collecting taxes
rubric: The judiciary interprets laws and adjudicates disputes in courts of law.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Federalism in Nigeria means ___
options: One central government controls everything|Power is shared between the federal and state governments|States have no power|The military controls the states
answer: Power is shared between the federal and state governments
rubric: Federalism divides governmental power between central (federal) and regional (state) governments.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Local Government is the ___ tier of government in Nigeria.
options: First|Second|Third|Fourth
rubric: Nigeria's three tiers are: Federal (1st), State (2nd) and Local Government (3rd).

subject: Social Studies
stem: A democracy is a system of government in which ___
options: One person rules absolutely|Power belongs to the people|The military rules|Religious leaders govern
rubric: Democracy derives its authority from the people (Greek: demos = people, kratos = rule).

subject: Social Studies
stem: The current Nigerian constitution was enacted in ___
rubric: Nigeria's current democratic constitution was enacted in 1999 at the return to civilian rule.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which body is responsible for organising elections in Nigeria?
options: NAFDAC|INEC|EFCC|CBN
rubric: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) organises and conducts elections in Nigeria.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Separation of powers in government means ___
options: All power belongs to the President|Government functions are divided among different arms|Only the courts have power|States have all power
answer: Government functions are divided among different arms
rubric: Separation of powers divides government authority among the executive, legislative and judicial arms.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The rule of law means that ___
options: Only the powerful obey laws|The law applies equally to all persons and institutions|Soldiers make the laws|Only courts decide everything
answer: The law applies equally to all persons and institutions
rubric: The rule of law holds that no person is above the law — all are subject to it equally.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a fundamental right guaranteed under the Nigerian constitution?
options: Right to steal|Right to free expression|Right to hold office only|Right to ignore taxes
rubric: Freedom of expression is a fundamental right guaranteed under Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Senate in Nigeria has ___ members.
rubric: The Nigerian Senate consists of 3 senators from each of the 36 states plus 1 for Abuja = 109.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The head of government at the state level in Nigeria is the ___
options: President|Senator|Governor|Local Government Chairman
rubric: Each of Nigeria's 36 states is headed by an elected Governor.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which principle of government prevents any one arm from having too much power?
options: Rule of law|Federalism|Checks and balances|Sovereignty
rubric: Checks and balances ensure that each arm of government can limit and oversee the others.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The primary responsibility of a citizen to the state is to ___
options: Only vote in elections|Pay taxes obey laws and defend the nation|Only serve in the military|Only attend school
answer: Pay taxes obey laws and defend the nation
rubric: Citizens' core duties include obeying laws, paying taxes, and contributing to national defence.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Human rights are rights that ___
options: Must be earned|Apply only to adults|Are inherent to all human beings|Are given by government only
answer: Are inherent to all human beings
rubric: Human rights are universal — they belong to every person by virtue of being human.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Child rights in Nigeria are protected under the ___
options: EFCC Act|Child Rights Act 2003|Police Act|Electoral Act
rubric: The Child Rights Act 2003 domesticates the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in Nigeria.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a child's right?
options: The right to work in a factory|The right to education|The right to vote|The right to own property
rubric: The right to education is a fundamental right of every child under Nigerian and international law.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Child labour is condemned because it ___
options: Is expensive|Denies children their right to education and a safe childhood|Creates more jobs|Builds character
answer: Denies children their right to education and a safe childhood
rubric: Child labour robs children of education, health and freedom — violating their fundamental rights.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations in ___
rubric: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is NOT a fundamental right in Nigeria?
options: Right to life|Right to personal liberty|Right to own a car|Right to fair hearing
rubric: Owning a car is not a constitutional right. Rights to life, liberty and fair hearing are fundamental.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A good citizen must ___
options: Only enjoy rights without responsibilities|Fulfil their duties while enjoying their rights|Disobey all laws|Avoid paying taxes
answer: Fulfil their duties while enjoying their rights
rubric: Citizenship involves a balance — rights come with corresponding duties and responsibilities.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The right to vote in an election is called ___
options: Franchise|Mandate|Tenure|Immunity
rubric: Franchise is the right to vote in political elections — also called suffrage.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following best describes gender equality?
options: Girls should stay at home|Women should not vote|Men and women should have equal rights and opportunities|Only women should work
answer: Men and women should have equal rights and opportunities
rubric: Gender equality means equal rights, opportunities and treatment for all genders.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The freedom to practise any religion of one's choice is called ___
options: Freedom of assembly|Freedom of speech|Freedom of religion|Freedom of movement
rubric: Freedom of religion guarantees individuals the right to practise any faith without persecution.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Civic education is important because it ___
options: Teaches people to avoid voting|Makes people aware of their rights and responsibilities|Is only for politicians|Teaches mathematics
answer: Makes people aware of their rights and responsibilities
rubric: Civic education informs citizens about governance, rights and responsibilities.

subject: Social Studies
stem: In Nigeria a citizen is someone who ___
options: Was born abroad|Lives in another country|Is a national of Nigeria by birth or naturalisation|Is only from Lagos
answer: Is a national of Nigeria by birth or naturalisation
rubric: Citizenship is acquired by birth (jus soli/sanguinis) or through naturalisation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is an example of a civic responsibility?
options: Stealing from neighbours|Paying taxes and keeping the environment clean|Refusing to vote|Destroying public property
answer: Paying taxes and keeping the environment clean
rubric: Civic responsibilities include voting, paying taxes, obeying laws and community service.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The right of a person accused of a crime to be tried fairly is called ___
options: Right to immunity|Right to silence|Right to fair hearing|Right to bail
rubric: The right to fair hearing ensures every person gets a fair and impartial trial.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is an obligation of a citizen to the state?
options: Criticising the government|Paying taxes and obeying laws|Ignoring civic duties|Staying outside the country
rubric: Citizens must obey laws and pay taxes as obligations that sustain the functioning of the state.

subject: Social Studies
stem: What are the colours on the Nigerian national flag?
options: Red white and blue|Green and white|Green white and red|Blue and gold
rubric: The Nigerian flag consists of two green stripes (representing agriculture) and a white stripe (peace).

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Nigerian national anthem begins with ___
options: Nigeria we hail thee|Arise O compatriots|Nigeria my Nigeria|God bless Nigeria
rubric: Nigeria's national anthem (adopted 1978) begins 'Arise O compatriots, Nigeria's call obey.'

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Eagle on Nigeria's coat of arms represents ___
options: Military power|The strength of the nation|Rivers Niger and Benue|Agricultural wealth
rubric: The black Eagle on Nigeria's coat of arms symbolises strength and national pride.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The two rivers depicted on Nigeria's coat of arms are ___
options: Ogun and Sokoto|Niger and Benue|Gongola and Kaduna|Anambra and Ogun
rubric: The wavy white lines on Nigeria's coat of arms represent the confluence of Rivers Niger and Benue.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria's independence was declared on ___
options: 1st October 1960|1st January 1963|1st October 1963|15th January 1970
rubric: Nigeria gained independence from Britain on 1st October 1960.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The national pledge of Nigeria begins with ___
options: I pledge to Nigeria my country|I pledge allegiance to Nigeria|I pledge to the flag|I pledge my life
answer: I pledge to Nigeria my country
rubric: The National Pledge begins: 'I pledge to Nigeria my country, to be faithful, loyal and honest.'

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Federal Capital Territory of Nigeria is ___
options: Lagos|Enugu|Abuja|Kaduna
rubric: Abuja became Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory and seat of government in 1991.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) issues Nigeria's national currency which is the ___
options: Dollar|Euro|Naira|Pound
rubric: The Nigerian Naira (₦) is issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria's national motto is ___
options: Unity and Faith|Unity Faith Peace and Progress|Peace Progress and Prosperity|Faith Justice and Peace
rubric: Nigeria's national motto is 'Unity, Faith, Peace and Progress'.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Nigerian Coat of Arms includes which animal?
options: Lion|Eagle|Horse and Eagle|Buffalo
rubric: The Eagle (and two horses as supporters) appear on Nigeria's coat of arms.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria became a Federal Republic in ___
rubric: Nigeria became a Federal Republic on 1st October 1963 — three years after independence.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is Nigeria's national flower?
options: Rose|Tulip|Costus spectabilis (yellow trumpet flower)|Sunflower
rubric: Costus spectabilis (known as the yellow trumpet flower) is Nigeria's national flower.

subject: Social Studies
stem: How many geopolitical zones does Nigeria have?
rubric: Nigeria has 6 geopolitical zones: North-West, North-East, North-Central, South-West, South-East and South-South.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The colour green on the Nigerian flag symbolises ___
options: Water bodies|The sky|Agricultural wealth and forests|Military strength
rubric: Green on the Nigerian flag represents Nigeria's rich vegetation and agricultural wealth.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The first civilian president of Nigeria after independence was ___
options: Nnamdi Azikiwe|Abubakar Tafawa Balewa|Obafemi Awolowo|Aguiyi Ironsi
rubric: Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa was Nigeria's first Prime Minister (effective head of government) at independence.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The lowest level of government in Nigeria is the ___
options: Federal government|State government|Local government|Community government
rubric: Local Government Authorities (LGAs) are the third tier — the lowest level of government.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria has ___ Local Government Areas (LGAs).
rubric: Nigeria is divided into 774 LGAs — the smallest administrative units.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is a function of local government in Nigeria?
options: Collecting import duties|Making federal laws|Providing primary education and basic healthcare|Printing currency
answer: Providing primary education and basic healthcare
rubric: LGAs are responsible for primary education, healthcare, sanitation, market and roads in their areas.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The traditional ruler of a state or community is recognised as ___
options: A political officer|A ceremonial head and cultural authority|An elected official|A military officer
answer: A ceremonial head and cultural authority
rubric: Traditional rulers serve as ceremonial heads and custodians of culture — they hold no official executive power.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The chairperson of a Local Government Area in Nigeria is elected by ___
options: The state governor|The President|The local community through elections|The traditional ruler
rubric: LGA chairpersons are democratically elected by residents of the local government area.

subject: Social Studies
stem: State Houses of Assembly perform which function?
options: They declare war|They make laws for the state|They appoint judges|They print money
answer: They make laws for the state
rubric: State Houses of Assembly are the legislative bodies that make laws at the state level.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Joint Account Committee in a state handles ___
options: Foreign affairs|Distribution of revenue between the state and LGAs|Military recruitment|Election organising
answer: Distribution of revenue between the state and LGAs
rubric: The State-Local Government Joint Account manages the sharing of funds between state and LGAs.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Governor of a state in Nigeria serves a term of ___ years.
rubric: A state governor serves a four-year term renewable for one additional term.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Community service as a civic duty involves ___
options: Paid work only|Volunteer activities that benefit the community|Working for foreign companies|Government employment
answer: Volunteer activities that benefit the community
rubric: Community service is voluntary work done for the benefit of one's community.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Inter-governmental relations in Nigeria describe ___
options: Relations between Nigeria and other countries|Cooperation and interaction between federal state and local governments|Relations between tribes|Military cooperation
answer: Cooperation and interaction between federal state and local governments
rubric: Inter-governmental relations refers to the interactions among Nigeria's three tiers of government.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The main source of revenue for Nigerian state governments is ___
options: Local levies only|Federal allocations and internally generated revenue|Foreign aid only|Loans only
answer: Federal allocations and internally generated revenue
rubric: States rely on federal government allocations (FAAC) and their own internally generated revenue.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Good governance is characterised by ___
options: Corruption and secrecy|Transparency accountability and rule of law|Military control|Single-party rule
answer: Transparency accountability and rule of law
rubric: Good governance involves transparency, accountability, efficiency, justice and the rule of law.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of infrastructure that local governments provide?
options: Universities|Federal roads|Primary school buildings and rural roads|International airports
answer: Primary school buildings and rural roads
rubric: LGAs are responsible for maintaining primary schools, rural roads, markets and sanitation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Decentralisation of government means ___
options: Concentrating power in one centre|Distributing government powers and functions to lower levels|Removing government|Military takeover
answer: Distributing government powers and functions to lower levels
rubric: Decentralisation moves government authority from central to regional and local levels.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The concept of local government aims primarily to ___
options: Increase federal power|Bring government closer to the grassroots people|Reduce state power|Create more states
answer: Bring government closer to the grassroots people
rubric: Local government exists to deliver services at the community level and promote grassroots participation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The minimum voting age in Nigeria is ___
rubric: A Nigerian citizen must be at least 18 years old to register and vote in elections.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A ballot is used in elections to ___
options: Register voters|Record a person's vote|Choose party leaders|Announce election results
rubric: A ballot paper (or ballot box) is the instrument used to cast and record votes in an election.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Universal adult suffrage means ___
options: Only men can vote|Every adult citizen has the right to vote|Only educated people can vote|Only property owners can vote
answer: Every adult citizen has the right to vote
rubric: Universal adult suffrage gives every adult citizen the equal right to vote regardless of gender or class.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a requirement for contesting presidential elections in Nigeria?
options: Be 30 years of age|Be at least 40 years old|Have a secondary school certificate|Be married
rubric: The 1999 Constitution requires a presidential candidate to be at least 40 years old.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Free and fair elections are characterised by ___
options: Rigging and manipulation|Violence and intimidation|Equal opportunity for all candidates and transparent counting|Military supervision
answer: Equal opportunity for all candidates and transparent counting
rubric: Free and fair elections require all candidates to compete equally with transparent, credible processes.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Gerrymandering refers to ___
options: Registering voters|Manipulating electoral boundaries to favour a particular party|Counting votes honestly|Appointing election officials
answer: Manipulating electoral boundaries to favour a particular party
rubric: Gerrymandering is the manipulation of constituency boundaries for political advantage.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A political party is an organisation that ___
options: Only provides welfare|Seeks to win political power through elections|Manages businesses|Organises only cultural events
answer: Seeks to win political power through elections
rubric: Political parties are organised groups that contest elections to gain control of government.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Permanent Voter's Card (PVC) in Nigeria is issued by ___
options: The Nigerian Police|INEC|The State Government|The Presidency
rubric: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) issues PVCs to registered voters.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is electoral malpractice?
options: Voting once|Carrying your PVC|Voting multiple times (multiple voting)|Queuing at the polling station
rubric: Multiple voting (voting more than once) is a serious electoral offence.

subject: Social Studies
stem: In a democracy citizens participate in government primarily through ___
options: Protest and riots|Elections and civic engagement|Military service only|Paying higher taxes
rubric: Voting in elections and engaging in civic activities are the primary means of democratic participation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: An incumbent is ___
options: A new candidate|The current holder of a political office|The election official|A registered voter
answer: The current holder of a political office
rubric: An incumbent is the current holder of a political office seeking re-election.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A by-election is conducted when ___
options: A general election fails|A seat in government becomes vacant before the end of its term|A president is impeached|Annual elections are due
answer: A seat in government becomes vacant before the end of its term
rubric: By-elections fill vacancies that arise when a seat becomes empty between regular elections.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The principle of one man one vote means ___
options: Rich people vote more|Only men vote|Every registered voter has exactly one equal vote|Soldiers vote first
answer: Every registered voter has exactly one equal vote
rubric: Each voter regardless of status gets exactly one vote — ensuring political equality.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A manifesto is a document in which a political party ___
options: Lists its members|Outlines its policies and programmes for governance|Announces election dates|Counts votes
answer: Outlines its policies and programmes for governance
rubric: A party manifesto is a public declaration of its goals, plans and policies if elected.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Democracy is best described as government of the people by the people for ___
options: The military|The rich|The people|The politicians only
rubric: Abraham Lincoln defined democracy as 'government of the people, by the people, for the people'.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Population growth rate depends on ___
options: Birth rate and trade|Birth rate death rate and migration|Only birth rate|Only immigration
answer: Birth rate death rate and migration
rubric: A population's growth rate = (births + immigration) − (deaths + emigration).

subject: Social Studies
stem: Overpopulation occurs when the number of people ___
options: Exceeds available resources and infrastructure|Is less than expected|Equals the land area|Is reduced by emigration
rubric: Overpopulation is when population size exceeds the carrying capacity of available resources.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a consequence of deforestation?
options: Increased rainfall|Soil erosion and loss of biodiversity|Lower temperatures|More forest animals
answer: Soil erosion and loss of biodiversity
rubric: Cutting down forests causes erosion, reduces biodiversity, and contributes to climate change.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Environmental pollution can be reduced by ___
options: Burning all waste|Disposing waste properly and reducing emissions|Using more plastic|Deforestation
answer: Disposing waste properly and reducing emissions
rubric: Proper waste management and emission reduction are key to environmental protection.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A census is ___
options: A type of tax|An official count of the population|A national election|An economic survey only
answer: An official count of the population
rubric: A census is an official enumeration of an entire population, usually conducted periodically.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Family planning helps to control population by ___
options: Encouraging more births|Helping families choose the number and spacing of their children|Discouraging marriage|Increasing death rate
answer: Helping families choose the number and spacing of their children
rubric: Family planning gives individuals control over the timing and number of pregnancies.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Global warming is primarily caused by ___
options: Farming|Increased greenhouse gases from human activities|Natural rainfall|Sea waves
answer: Increased greenhouse gases from human activities
rubric: Human activities (burning fossil fuels, deforestation) release greenhouse gases that trap heat.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The three Rs of environmental management are ___
options: Read Recite Revise|Reduce Reuse Recycle|Rest Relax Recover|Run Race Ride
rubric: The 3Rs — Reduce, Reuse, Recycle — are principles for minimising waste and protecting the environment.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Biodiversity means ___
options: Only one species living in an area|The variety of plant and animal life in an ecosystem|High population density|Pollution of water bodies
answer: The variety of plant and animal life in an ecosystem
rubric: Biodiversity refers to the range of different species of plants and animals in a habitat.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Brain drain refers to ___
options: Memory loss|The emigration of skilled and educated people from a country|Foreign investment|Local migration
answer: The emigration of skilled and educated people from a country
rubric: Brain drain is the loss of a country's human capital when its educated citizens emigrate abroad.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The concept of sustainable development means ___
options: Using all resources now|Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs|Stopping all development|Only economic growth
answer: Meeting present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs
rubric: Sustainable development balances present development with the conservation of resources for future generations.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Desertification in northern Nigeria is mainly caused by ___
options: Too much rainfall|Overgrazing and deforestation|Industrial development|Sea level rise
rubric: Overgrazing and deforestation strip vegetation, allowing the desert to encroach on fertile land.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Push factors in migration are ___
options: Attractions that pull people to a new place|Conditions at home that drive people away|Only employment opportunities|Low birth rates
answer: Conditions at home that drive people away
rubric: Push factors (poverty, conflict, drought) drive people to leave their place of origin.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The agency responsible for environmental regulation in Nigeria is ___
options: NAFDAC|CBN|Federal Ministry of Environment / NESREA|INEC
rubric: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) enforces Nigeria's environmental laws.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Oil pollution in the Niger Delta is an example of ___
options: Agricultural development|Environmental degradation|Population growth|Urbanisation
rubric: Oil spills in the Niger Delta cause severe environmental degradation — harming soil water and biodiversity.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The key (legend) on a map ___
options: Shows the distance|Explains the symbols and signs used on the map|Indicates the direction|Gives the scale
answer: Explains the symbols and signs used on the map
rubric: The map legend/key explains what each symbol or colour on the map represents.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The scale of a map refers to ___
options: The colour of the map|The ratio between map distance and actual ground distance|The age of the map|The symbols used
answer: The ratio between map distance and actual ground distance
rubric: Map scale shows the relationship between distances on the map and real distances on the ground.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A relief map shows ___
options: Political boundaries|The physical features of the land including elevation|Only roads|Only rivers
answer: The physical features of the land including elevation
rubric: Relief maps show the physical landscape — hills, valleys, mountains and their heights.

subject: Social Studies
stem: North is indicated on a map by ___
options: The legend|The scale|The compass/north arrow|The title
rubric: A north arrow or compass rose on a map indicates the direction of north.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Lines of latitude on a map run ___
options: From north to south|From east to west (horizontally)|Diagonally|In a circle around the poles
rubric: Lines of latitude (parallels) run horizontally east-west around the globe.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The equator is located at ___
options: 0° longitude|90° north latitude|0° latitude|90° south latitude
rubric: The equator is at 0° latitude — dividing the Earth into northern and southern hemispheres.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A contour line on a topographic map connects points ___
options: Of the same temperature|Of equal elevation (height)|Of equal rainfall|On the same road
rubric: Contour lines join points of equal elevation above sea level on a topographic map.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Nigeria is located on the continent of ___
options: Asia|Europe|Africa|South America
rubric: Nigeria is located in West Africa on the African continent.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Greenwich Meridian (Prime Meridian) is located at ___
options: 0° latitude|180° longitude|0° longitude|90° latitude
rubric: The Prime Meridian (Greenwich Meridian) is at 0° longitude — the reference line for time zones.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which ocean lies to the south of Nigeria?
options: Indian Ocean|Arctic Ocean|Atlantic Ocean|Pacific Ocean
rubric: Nigeria's southern coast borders the Atlantic Ocean (Gulf of Guinea).

subject: Social Studies
stem: Economics is the study of ___
options: Only money|How societies allocate scarce resources to meet unlimited wants|Only trade|Only agriculture
answer: How societies allocate scarce resources to meet unlimited wants
rubric: Economics studies how people and societies make choices about resource allocation.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a basic economic problem?
options: Too much production|Scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants|Too many workers|Excess money
answer: Scarcity of resources relative to unlimited wants
rubric: Scarcity — limited resources vs. unlimited wants — is the fundamental economic problem.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The study of how individual households and firms make decisions is called ___
options: Macroeconomics|Microeconomics|Fiscal policy|Monetary policy
rubric: Microeconomics studies individual units (households, firms) and their market interactions.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Trade by barter is the exchange of ___
options: Goods for money|Goods for goods without money|Services for money|Labour for money
rubric: Barter is the direct exchange of goods and services without using money as a medium.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The value of the next best alternative given up when making a choice is called ___
options: Profit|Opportunity cost|Revenue|Price
rubric: Opportunity cost is the value of the best foregone alternative when a choice is made.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Inflation refers to a ___ rise in the general level of prices.
options: Sudden temporary|Sustained|Small seasonal|One-time
rubric: Inflation is a sustained and general increase in the price level of goods and services.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is a factor of production?
options: Television|Money in a bank|Land|Tax
rubric: The four factors of production are Land, Labour, Capital, and Entrepreneurship.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Supply and demand determine prices in a ___
options: Command economy|Market economy|Traditional economy|Mixed economy
rubric: In a market (free) economy prices are determined by the interaction of supply and demand.

subject: Social Studies
stem: An economy in which the government makes all production decisions is called ___
options: Market economy|Mixed economy|Command economy|Traditional economy
rubric: A command (planned) economy has central government controlling what is produced and how.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of a capital good?
options: A loaf of bread|A factory machine|A television set for home use|Clothing
rubric: Capital goods are used to produce other goods. A factory machine is a capital good.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Consumer goods are goods that ___
options: Are used to produce other goods|Satisfy human wants directly|Are owned by government|Are exported only
rubric: Consumer goods are final goods purchased for direct use by consumers.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Division of labour means ___
options: Workers work separately without cooperation|Breaking production into specialised tasks performed by different workers|Only management works|Labour laws
answer: Breaking production into specialised tasks performed by different workers
rubric: Division of labour increases efficiency by assigning workers to specialised tasks.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The main aim of a business enterprise is to ___
options: Reduce employment|Make a profit|Increase taxation|Distribute goods freely
rubric: The primary goal of a business is to generate profit — revenue exceeding costs.

subject: Social Studies
stem: When demand for a good is greater than its supply the price will ___
options: Fall|Stay the same|Rise|Disappear
rubric: When demand exceeds supply there is a shortage, which pushes prices upward.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A budget deficit occurs when ___
options: Revenue equals expenditure|Revenue exceeds expenditure|Expenditure exceeds revenue|No taxes are collected
rubric: A budget deficit means a government spends more than it earns in revenue.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Central Bank of Nigeria is responsible for ___
options: Collecting taxes|Making laws|Controlling money supply and monetary policy|Organising elections
answer: Controlling money supply and monetary policy
rubric: The CBN formulates and implements Nigeria's monetary policy, regulating money supply and banking.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Unemployment is a situation where ___
options: All people are working|Prices are very high|People who are willing and able to work cannot find jobs|Workers earn very high wages
answer: People who are willing and able to work cannot find jobs
rubric: Unemployment is when the labour force cannot find employment despite being able and willing to work.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Imports are goods and services that ___
options: A country produces for itself|A country sells to other countries|A country buys from other countries|Government gives for free
answer: A country buys from other countries
rubric: Imports are goods and services purchased from foreign countries.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures ___
options: Only agricultural output|The total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year|Government spending only|Import and export only
answer: The total value of goods and services produced in a country in a year
rubric: GDP is the monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country over a period.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Taxation is the main way that government ___
options: Borrows money|Generates revenue to fund public services|Prints money|Creates jobs
answer: Generates revenue to fund public services
rubric: Taxes are the primary source of government revenue used to fund roads, schools, healthcare etc.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following best describes peer group influence on adolescents?
options: It has no effect|It shapes behaviours attitudes and decisions|It only affects adults|It is always negative
answer: It shapes behaviours attitudes and decisions
rubric: Peer groups significantly influence teenagers' values, lifestyle choices and behaviour.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Conflict resolution in a community is best achieved through ___
options: Violence|Dialogue negotiation and compromise|Ignoring the problem|Taking revenge
rubric: Peaceful conflict resolution relies on dialogue, mediation and willingness to compromise.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these is a sign of a functional family?
options: Frequent fights|Neglect of children|Mutual respect care and communication|Parents always absent
rubric: A functional family is characterised by love, respect, open communication and shared responsibility.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Social stratification refers to ___
options: Equal treatment of all people|The ranking of people in a society by wealth status or power|The study of stars|A type of government
answer: The ranking of people in a society by wealth status or power
rubric: Social stratification is the hierarchical arrangement of people in society into different layers.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following best explains discrimination?
options: Treating everyone fairly|Unfair treatment of a person based on race gender religion or other characteristics|Promoting equality|Equal pay for equal work
answer: Unfair treatment of a person based on race gender religion or other characteristics
rubric: Discrimination is treating someone unfairly based on characteristics like race, gender or religion.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Integrity in governance means ___
options: Corruption and dishonesty|Honesty transparency and adherence to moral principles|Seeking personal gain|Promoting tribalism
answer: Honesty transparency and adherence to moral principles
rubric: Integrity means being honest, consistent and morally upright — a key civic virtue.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Religious tolerance means ___
options: Accepting only one religion|Respecting the right of others to hold different religious beliefs|Forcing others to change their religion|Banning religion
answer: Respecting the right of others to hold different religious beliefs
rubric: Religious tolerance promotes peaceful coexistence by respecting diversity of faith.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following promotes national unity in Nigeria?
options: Tribalism|Speaking only one's native language|Celebrating national festivals together|Encouraging ethnic rivalry
rubric: Shared national celebrations (Independence Day, Democracy Day) reinforce a common national identity.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Corruption undermines development because it ___
options: Creates employment|Builds infrastructure|Diverts public resources from essential services|Promotes transparency
answer: Diverts public resources from essential services
rubric: Corruption siphons public funds, reducing investment in education, healthcare and infrastructure.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of civic responsibility?
options: Tax evasion|Destroying public property|Reporting crimes to the police|Ignoring community problems
rubric: Reporting crimes is a civic responsibility — it supports law enforcement and community safety.

subject: Social Studies
stem: An impeachment is the process of ___
options: Electing a new president|Formally charging and removing a government official from office|Appointing judges|Declaring war
answer: Formally charging and removing a government official from office
rubric: Impeachment is the formal process by which a legislature charges an official with misconduct.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Attorney General of the Federation in Nigeria is the ___
options: Head of Police|Chief Law Officer of the Federation|President's spokesperson|Head of Army
answer: Chief Law Officer of the Federation
rubric: The AGF is the chief legal adviser to the federal government and head of the federal judiciary.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is NOT a tier of government in Nigeria?
options: Federal|State|Local Government|Community Government
rubric: Nigeria officially has three tiers: Federal, State and Local Government — community government is not a tier.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The concept of sovereignty means ___
options: Dependence on other nations|A nation's supreme authority over its territory|Military rule|Paying foreign debts
answer: A nation's supreme authority over its territory
rubric: Sovereignty is a nation's supreme independent authority over its own affairs.

subject: Social Studies
stem: An oligarchy is a system of government where power is held by ___
options: The majority|A small privileged group|Religious leaders only|The military only
rubric: Oligarchy is rule by a small, elite group — often based on wealth or family.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The right to life means that ___
options: A person may be killed at will|No one should be arbitrarily deprived of their life|Only criminals lose this right|Government can take any life
answer: No one should be arbitrarily deprived of their life
rubric: The right to life is a fundamental right — no person should be unlawfully killed.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A person accused of a crime is presumed ___
options: Guilty until proven innocent|Innocent until proven guilty|Already convicted|A danger to society
rubric: The presumption of innocence is a cornerstone of justice — guilt must be proven in court.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The right to freedom of movement means ___
options: Citizens can travel anywhere in the world freely|Citizens can move freely within Nigeria and exit or enter the country|Only politicians can travel|Foreign travel is prohibited
answer: Citizens can move freely within Nigeria and exit or enter the country
rubric: Freedom of movement guarantees Nigerians the right to move within and in and out of the country.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a duty of a student citizen?
options: Avoiding school|Respecting school rules and contributing to a safe learning environment|Bullying classmates|Damaging school property
answer: Respecting school rules and contributing to a safe learning environment
rubric: Student citizens have the duty to obey school rules, respect others and care for school property.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) in Nigeria help to ___
options: Make laws|Elect officials|Provide social services and advocate for citizens' rights|Print currency
answer: Provide social services and advocate for citizens' rights
rubric: NGOs fill gaps in public service delivery and advocate for vulnerable groups' rights.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following is a feature of a constitutional democracy?
options: Unlimited power of the president|Protection of citizens' rights under a constitution|No elections|Military appointments
answer: Protection of citizens' rights under a constitution
rubric: Constitutional democracy limits government power and guarantees rights through a written constitution.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Civic education encourages citizens to ___
options: Avoid elections|Participate actively in democratic processes|Ignore government activities|Support only one party
rubric: Civic education empowers citizens to vote, engage with government and hold leaders accountable.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of these best describes a referendum?
options: A type of court case|A direct vote by all eligible voters on a specific issue|A party election|A military decision
answer: A direct vote by all eligible voters on a specific issue
rubric: A referendum is a direct democratic vote in which citizens decide on a specific question.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The term 'electorate' refers to ___
options: Only the candidates in an election|All people eligible to vote in an election|Election officials only|The election commission
answer: All people eligible to vote in an election
rubric: The electorate is the body of all persons entitled to vote in an election.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which of the following discourages voter participation in elections?
options: Easy registration|Accessible polling units|Voter intimidation and violence|Civic education
rubric: Intimidation, threats and violence at polling stations suppress voter turnout.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The greenhouse effect causes ___
options: Cooling of the earth|Global warming through trapped heat|More rainfall|Stronger winds
rubric: Greenhouse gases trap heat in the atmosphere causing global warming.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Water pollution is mainly caused by ___
options: Planting trees|Releasing untreated sewage and chemicals into water bodies|Recycling|Clean farming practices
answer: Releasing untreated sewage and chemicals into water bodies
rubric: Industrial waste, sewage and agricultural chemicals are major sources of water pollution.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Afforestation means ___
options: Cutting down all trees|Burning forests|Planting trees in areas where there were none or few|Only cultivating farmland
answer: Planting trees in areas where there were none or few
rubric: Afforestation is the establishment of a forest by planting trees — it restores vegetation cover.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The major cause of rural-urban migration in Nigeria is ___
options: Better weather in cities|The search for better employment and economic opportunities|Rural areas having too much land|Government orders
answer: The search for better employment and economic opportunities
rubric: People move to cities primarily seeking jobs, higher incomes and better services.

subject: Social Studies
stem: An ecosystem is ___
options: Only the plants in an area|A community of living organisms interacting with their physical environment|Only the animals in an area|Only the soil
answer: A community of living organisms interacting with their physical environment
rubric: An ecosystem comprises all living organisms and their interactions with the non-living environment.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Lines of longitude on a map run ___
options: Horizontally east to west|From north to south (vertically)|Diagonally|In circles around the equator
rubric: Lines of longitude (meridians) run from the North Pole to the South Pole — vertically.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The Tropic of Cancer is located at ___
options: 0° latitude|23.5° North latitude|23.5° South latitude|66.5° North latitude
rubric: The Tropic of Cancer is at approximately 23.5° North — the northernmost point the sun is directly overhead.

subject: Social Studies
stem: A political map primarily shows ___
options: Physical features like mountains|National and state boundaries and capitals|Rainfall patterns|Population density
answer: National and state boundaries and capitals
rubric: Political maps show human-made boundaries — countries, states, capitals and cities.

subject: Social Studies
stem: Which direction is directly opposite to North?
options: East|West|South|Northeast
rubric: On a compass, South is directly opposite (180°) from North.

subject: Social Studies
stem: The distance between the equator and the poles in degrees of latitude is ___
rubric: From the equator (0°) to either pole (90°N or 90°S) is exactly 90 degrees of latitude.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Business is best defined as ___
options: Any leisure activity|An organised effort to produce goods and services for profit|Working for the government|Saving money in a bank
answer: An organised effort to produce goods and services for profit
rubric: Business involves the production, buying and selling of goods/services with the aim of making profit.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a PRIMARY industry?
options: Banking|Farming and mining|Manufacturing|Retailing
rubric: Primary industries extract raw materials from nature — farming, fishing, mining and forestry.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A secondary industry is one that ___
options: Extracts raw materials|Converts raw materials into finished goods|Provides services|Distributes goods
answer: Converts raw materials into finished goods
rubric: Secondary (manufacturing) industries process raw materials into finished products.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The tertiary sector of the economy provides ___
options: Raw materials|Manufactured goods|Services|Agricultural produce
rubric: The tertiary sector provides services — banking, transport, education, healthcare, retail.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a feature of a sole proprietorship?
options: Shared ownership|Owned and managed by one person|Limited liability|Issued shares
answer: Owned and managed by one person
rubric: A sole proprietorship is a business owned and managed by a single individual.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A partnership business is owned by ___
options: One person|The government|Two to twenty persons|An unlimited number of shareholders
rubric: A partnership has between 2 and 20 partners (in most jurisdictions) who share ownership.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The main advantage of a sole proprietorship is ___
options: Limited liability|Easy access to large capital|Quick decision-making and full control|Shared risk
rubric: The sole trader makes all decisions quickly without consulting others.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of a sole proprietorship?
options: Easy to set up|Full control by owner|Unlimited personal liability|Cheap to run
rubric: The sole trader bears personal (unlimited) liability — personal assets can settle business debts.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A cooperative society is formed to ___
options: Maximise individual profit|Provide mutual benefit and support to its members|Avoid paying taxes|Compete against all other businesses
answer: Provide mutual benefit and support to its members
rubric: Cooperatives are formed for the mutual economic benefit of their members.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A public limited company (PLC) can raise capital by ___
options: Borrowing only from family|Selling shares to the public on a stock exchange|Using only the owner's money|Receiving government grants only
answer: Selling shares to the public on a stock exchange
rubric: PLCs can sell shares (equities) to the general public through a stock exchange.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Entrepreneurship involves ___
options: Following orders only|Taking the risk of starting and running a business|Working for others|Avoiding all risk
answer: Taking the risk of starting and running a business
rubric: Entrepreneurs organise resources, take risks and innovate to create and run businesses.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an incentive for starting a business?
options: Guaranteed employment|Profit motive and independence|Free government salary|No risk of failure
rubric: Entrepreneurs are motivated by the desire to earn profit and be their own boss.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Limited liability means that ___
options: Shareholders are personally liable for all debts|Shareholders' liability is limited to the amount they invested|The company cannot borrow money|Owners share unlimited risk
answer: Shareholders' liability is limited to the amount they invested
rubric: Limited liability protects shareholders — they can only lose what they invested in the company.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The capital of a business refers to ___
options: Only buildings and machines|Money and other resources invested in the business|Only the profits earned|The number of workers
answer: Money and other resources invested in the business
rubric: Capital is the financial and physical resources used to start and run a business.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Government enterprises are businesses owned and run by ___
options: Private individuals|Foreign companies|The government|Cooperatives only
rubric: Government enterprises (parastatals) are owned and operated by the state.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a business document used to order goods?
options: Invoice|Receipt|Purchase order|Statement of account
rubric: A purchase order is a document sent to a supplier requesting specific goods at an agreed price.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Profit is calculated as ___
options: Revenue + Cost|Revenue − Cost|Cost − Revenue|Revenue × Cost
rubric: Profit = Total Revenue − Total Cost.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following best describes the concept of demand?
options: The amount a producer is willing to supply|The desire to buy backed by ability to pay|Only government purchases|Wants without money
answer: The desire to buy backed by ability to pay
rubric: Effective demand = want + ability (purchasing power) to buy.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The process of buying goods in large quantities and selling them in smaller quantities is called ___
options: Manufacturing|Wholesaling|Retailing|Exporting
rubric: Wholesalers buy in bulk from producers and sell in smaller lots to retailers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An invoice is a document that ___
options: Orders goods|Shows the amount owed for goods or services supplied|Confirms payment received|Records staff attendance
answer: Shows the amount owed for goods or services supplied
rubric: An invoice is a bill sent by a seller to a buyer detailing goods supplied and amount payable.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Commerce involves ___
options: Only farming activities|The exchange and distribution of goods and services|Only manufacturing|Only mining
answer: The exchange and distribution of goods and services
rubric: Commerce is the branch of business concerned with the exchange, distribution and trade in goods and services.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a barrier to trade?
options: Low taxation|High tariffs and import restrictions|Good transport network|Stable currency
