rubric: Tariffs, quotas and import duties are barriers that restrict international trade.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Exports refer to goods and services ___
options: Imported from other countries|Sold to other countries|Produced only for local use|Given to other countries free
rubric: Exports are goods and services produced domestically and sold to foreign buyers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A retailer sells goods ___
options: In bulk to other traders|Directly to the final consumer|Only to the government|Only to manufacturers
rubric: Retailers are the final link in the distribution chain — they sell to end consumers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an aid to trade?
options: Production|Farming|Banking and insurance|Manufacturing
rubric: Aids to trade (banking, transport, insurance, warehousing, advertising) facilitate commerce.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Insurance in business protects against ___
options: Making profit|Financial loss from unexpected events|Paying wages|Increasing sales
rubric: Insurance transfers the risk of financial loss from fire, theft or accidents to an insurer.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A bill of exchange is a ___
options: Government bond|Written order to pay a specified sum at a future date|Product receipt|Stock certificate
answer: Written order to pay a specified sum at a future date
rubric: A bill of exchange is a negotiable instrument — a written order directing payment at a future date.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is a function of a warehouse?
options: Manufacturing goods|Storing goods until they are needed|Selling to consumers|Advertising products
answer: Storing goods until they are needed
rubric: Warehouses store goods between production and sale — smoothing supply chains.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Advertising aims to ___
options: Increase production costs|Inform and persuade customers to buy a product|Reduce supply|Pay workers
answer: Inform and persuade customers to buy a product
rubric: Advertising communicates product information and persuades consumers to purchase.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The channel of distribution for most consumer goods is ___
options: Producer → Consumer|Producer → Retailer → Consumer|Producer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer|Retailer → Producer → Consumer
rubric: Most consumer goods pass through: Manufacturer → Wholesaler → Retailer → Consumer.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Credit sales allow customers to ___
options: Pay before receiving goods|Receive goods now and pay later|Return goods freely|Get goods for free
answer: Receive goods now and pay later
rubric: Credit sales allow buyers to take goods now and pay at a future agreed date.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A discount is a ___
options: Penalty for late payment|Reduction in the price of goods|Tax on goods|Additional charge
answer: Reduction in the price of goods
rubric: A discount is a deduction from the listed price offered to encourage payment or bulk buying.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Home trade refers to ___
options: Trade between Nigeria and other countries|Trade within Nigeria|Only agricultural trade|Only market trading
rubric: Home trade (domestic trade) is the buying and selling of goods within a country.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of e-commerce?
options: Buying goods in a market|Selling products through a website or app|Trade by barter|Hawking on streets
answer: Selling products through a website or app
rubric: E-commerce involves buying and selling goods and services over the internet.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A cash-and-carry supermarket requires customers to ___
options: Order goods in advance|Pay cash and take goods away immediately|Return goods next day|Buy on credit only
answer: Pay cash and take goods away immediately
rubric: Cash-and-carry stores require payment at point of purchase and customers collect immediately.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The Stock Exchange is a market where ___
options: Agricultural products are sold|Company shares and securities are bought and sold|Only government bonds are traded|Only foreign currencies are exchanged
answer: Company shares and securities are bought and sold
rubric: A stock exchange is a regulated market for trading company shares, bonds and securities.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A receipt is a document that confirms ___
options: An order has been placed|Payment has been received|Goods have been dispatched|Credit has been given
rubric: A receipt is issued to acknowledge that payment has been made.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Trade by barter was replaced by the use of money because barter ___
options: Was too expensive|Requires a double coincidence of wants|Made trading easier|Created too much profit
answer: Requires a double coincidence of wants
rubric: Barter is inefficient because both parties must simultaneously want what the other offers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A pro-forma invoice is sent to a buyer ___
options: After payment|After delivery|Before the goods are dispatched to indicate the price|As a final receipt
answer: Before the goods are dispatched to indicate the price
rubric: A pro-forma invoice is a preliminary bill sent before goods are supplied, showing the expected price.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following best describes a market?
options: Only a physical place|Any arrangement where buyers and sellers interact to trade|Only a building|A government office
answer: Any arrangement where buyers and sellers interact to trade
rubric: A market is any mechanism (physical or virtual) through which buyers and sellers exchange goods.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The primary function of a bank is to ___
options: Make laws|Accept deposits and give loans|Sell goods|Manufacture products
rubric: Banks accept deposits from savers and provide loans to borrowers — their core function.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A savings account is best suited for ___
options: Frequent daily transactions|Saving money and earning interest|Paying salaries|Buying shares
rubric: Savings accounts are designed for storing money and earning interest over time.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A cheque is a written order directing a bank to ___
options: Deposit money|Issue a loan|Pay a specified sum to the named person|Block an account
answer: Pay a specified sum to the named person
rubric: A cheque is a written instruction to a bank to pay a specified amount to the payee.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A current account in a bank is mainly used for ___
options: Long-term savings|Frequent deposits and withdrawals for business transactions|Investing in shares|Receiving government benefits
answer: Frequent deposits and withdrawals for business transactions
rubric: Current accounts support regular business transactions — frequent deposits and withdrawals.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Interest on a loan is the ___
options: Principal amount borrowed|Cost of borrowing money|Collateral provided|Bank's profit only
rubric: Interest is the charge paid for using borrowed money — a percentage of the principal.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Collateral in banking is ___
options: The interest rate charged|An asset pledged as security for a loan|The bank's profit|Monthly account charges
answer: An asset pledged as security for a loan
rubric: Collateral is property or assets offered by a borrower to secure a loan.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The Central Bank of Nigeria is responsible for ___
options: Retail banking services|Controlling money supply and regulating commercial banks|Selling goods|Making federal laws
answer: Controlling money supply and regulating commercial banks
rubric: The CBN is Nigeria's apex bank — it implements monetary policy and supervises all banks.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Microfinance banks in Nigeria primarily serve ___
options: Large corporations|Rich individuals|Small businesses and low-income earners|Foreign investors
rubric: Microfinance banks provide small loans and financial services to micro-enterprises and low-income people.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A bank statement shows ___
options: What a customer wants to buy|A record of all transactions in a bank account over a period|Future plans of the bank|A customer's investment portfolio
answer: A record of all transactions in a bank account over a period
rubric: A bank statement is a document showing all debits, credits and balances on an account.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Insurance premium is ___
options: The amount claimed after a loss|The regular payment made to maintain an insurance policy|The profit of the insurance company|The type of risk covered
answer: The regular payment made to maintain an insurance policy
rubric: The premium is the amount paid periodically to keep an insurance policy active.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is a function of money?
options: Producing goods|Medium of exchange store of value and unit of account|Creating employment|Generating profit
answer: Medium of exchange store of value and unit of account
rubric: Money serves as a medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account and standard of deferred payment.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Mobile banking allows customers to ___
options: Visit the bank daily|Access banking services through a mobile phone|Print their own currency|Lend money to others
answer: Access banking services through a mobile phone
rubric: Mobile banking provides financial services (transfers, payments) via smartphones.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A debit card allows the user to ___
options: Borrow money from the bank|Spend only the money available in their bank account|Earn interest|Print money
answer: Spend only the money available in their bank account
rubric: A debit card draws directly from the cardholder's existing bank account balance.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Fixed deposit accounts are characterised by ___
options: Frequent withdrawals|Money deposited for a fixed period at a higher interest rate|Low interest rates|No minimum deposit
answer: Money deposited for a fixed period at a higher interest rate
rubric: Fixed (term) deposits lock money for a set period in exchange for higher interest.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An overdraft is when a bank allows a customer to ___
options: Deposit extra money|Withdraw more money than is in their account|Freeze the account|Earn bonus interest
answer: Withdraw more money than is in their account
rubric: An overdraft is a credit facility allowing withdrawal beyond the current account balance.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The insurance principle of indemnity means ___
options: You can profit from a claim|The insured is restored to the same financial position as before the loss|Insurance is free|Only property is insured
answer: The insured is restored to the same financial position as before the loss
rubric: Indemnity ensures the insured is compensated to their pre-loss financial position — not for profit.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a negotiable instrument?
options: It cannot be transferred|It can be transferred from one person to another|It has no monetary value|Only banks can use it
answer: It can be transferred from one person to another
rubric: Negotiable instruments (cheques, bills of exchange) can be transferred by endorsement.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The ATM (Automated Teller Machine) allows customers to ___
options: Get loans instantly|Withdraw cash and check balances without a teller|Buy shares|Pay taxes only
answer: Withdraw cash and check balances without a teller
rubric: ATMs allow cardholders to withdraw cash, check balances and perform basic transactions 24/7.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Capital market in Nigeria refers to the market for ___
options: Agricultural goods|Long-term financial instruments like shares and bonds|Short-term cash loans|Commodities
answer: Long-term financial instruments like shares and bonds
rubric: The capital market deals in long-term securities — equity (shares) and debt (bonds).

subject: Business Studies
stem: The Nigerian Stock Exchange (NGX) is located in ___
options: Abuja|Port Harcourt|Lagos|Kano
rubric: The Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX), formerly NSE, is headquartered in Lagos.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Book-keeping is the process of ___
options: Making business decisions|Systematically recording business financial transactions|Manufacturing products|Paying taxes
rubric: Book-keeping involves the accurate recording of all financial transactions of a business.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A ledger is a book that contains ___
options: Daily records of all transactions|Summarised accounts classified by type|Only sales records|Only purchase records
rubric: The ledger organises transactions into accounts (assets, liabilities, income, expenses).

subject: Business Studies
stem: In accounting assets are items that ___
options: A business owes to others|A business owns and that have value|Are always cash|Only include land
answer: A business owns and that have value
rubric: Assets are resources owned or controlled by a business that have economic value.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Liabilities in a balance sheet represent ___
options: What the business owns|What the business owes to others|The owner's equity|Cash in hand
answer: What the business owes to others
rubric: Liabilities are the financial obligations (debts) owed by the business to external parties.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The accounting equation is ___
options: Assets = Liabilities + Capital|Assets = Capital − Liabilities|Capital = Assets + Liabilities|Liabilities = Assets + Capital
rubric: The fundamental accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity (Capital).

subject: Business Studies
stem: A debit entry in a ledger account ___
options: Always decreases the account|Increases assets and expenses; decreases liabilities and capital|Always increases the account|Means money received
answer: Increases assets and expenses; decreases liabilities and capital
rubric: Debit (DR): increases assets and expenses; decreases liabilities, capital and income.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The cash book records ___
options: Only sales|All cash and bank receipts and payments|Only purchases|Only wages
answer: All cash and bank receipts and payments
rubric: The cash book is a primary book of account that records all cash and bank transactions.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Gross profit is calculated as ___
options: Sales − Total expenses|Sales − Cost of goods sold|Cost of goods sold + Expenses|Net profit + Expenses
rubric: Gross Profit = Net Sales − Cost of Goods Sold (before deducting operating expenses).

subject: Business Studies
stem: A trial balance is prepared to ___
options: Record daily sales|Check that total debits equal total credits in the ledger|Calculate profit|List all assets
answer: Check that total debits equal total credits in the ledger
rubric: A trial balance verifies the arithmetic accuracy of the double-entry bookkeeping system.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Net profit is ___
options: Revenue − Cost of goods sold|Gross profit − Operating expenses|Revenue alone|Total expenses alone
rubric: Net Profit = Gross Profit − All Operating Expenses.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A petty cash book is used to record ___
options: Large purchases|Small day-to-day cash expenses|Bank transactions only|Salary payments
rubric: The petty cash book records minor, routine cash payments (postage, cleaning, refreshments).

subject: Business Studies
stem: Depreciation is ___
options: The increase in value of an asset over time|The decrease in value of an asset over time due to wear and tear|A bank charge|A type of tax
answer: The decrease in value of an asset over time due to wear and tear
rubric: Depreciation allocates the cost of a fixed asset over its useful life as its value declines.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A balance sheet shows ___
options: Only profits and losses|The financial position of a business at a specific date|Only cash transactions|Future financial plans
answer: The financial position of a business at a specific date
rubric: The balance sheet (statement of financial position) shows assets, liabilities and equity at a point in time.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Source documents in book-keeping include ___
options: Ledgers and trial balances|Invoices receipts and purchase orders|Balance sheets only|Tax returns only
rubric: Source documents (invoices, receipts, orders) provide original evidence for accounting entries.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The double-entry principle in accounting means ___
options: All transactions are recorded twice in the same account|Every transaction affects two accounts — a debit in one and a credit in another|Only income is recorded|Only expenses are recorded
answer: Every transaction affects two accounts — a debit in one and a credit in another
rubric: Double-entry bookkeeping records every transaction as both a debit and a credit in different accounts.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Working capital is calculated as ___
options: Fixed assets − Current liabilities|Current assets − Current liabilities|Capital + Liabilities|Revenue − Expenses
rubric: Working capital = Current Assets − Current Liabilities; it measures short-term liquidity.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a current asset?
options: Buildings|Machinery|Trade debtors (money owed by customers)|Long-term investments
rubric: Current assets include cash, debtors and stock — items expected to convert to cash within a year.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Purchases in a trading account refers to ___
options: All goods bought|Goods bought specifically for resale|Only fixed assets bought|Services purchased
rubric: In a trading account 'Purchases' means goods bought with the intention of reselling them.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The profit and loss account shows ___
options: Only the sales figures|Net profit or loss after all income and expenses are considered|Only the expenses|The balance sheet total
answer: Net profit or loss after all income and expenses are considered
rubric: The profit and loss account summarises revenues and expenses to show net profit or loss.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An audit is ___
options: The preparation of accounts|An independent examination of financial records to verify their accuracy|A bank deposit|A type of tax
answer: An independent examination of financial records to verify their accuracy
rubric: An audit is an official inspection of accounts by an independent auditor for accuracy and compliance.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The main function of an office is to ___
options: Manufacture goods|Receive store process and communicate information|Sell products to consumers|Transport goods
answer: Receive store process and communicate information
rubric: An office processes information — receiving, storing, retrieving and communicating it.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Filing in an office means ___
options: Throwing away documents|Systematically arranging and storing documents for easy retrieval|Printing documents|Sending documents by post
answer: Systematically arranging and storing documents for easy retrieval
rubric: Filing is the systematic organisation and storage of documents so they can be found quickly.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a function of a secretary?
options: Making company policy|Managing accounts|Handling correspondence scheduling and organising the office|Manufacturing products
answer: Handling correspondence scheduling and organising the office
rubric: A secretary manages correspondence, schedules, meetings and supports office administration.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A memorandum (memo) is used for ___
options: External business communication|Internal communication within an organisation|Advertising products|Legal contracts
rubric: Memos are used for internal communication between staff members within the same organisation.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The correct salutation when writing a formal business letter to someone whose name you do not know is ___
options: Dear Friend|Dear Sir/Madam|To Whom It Concerns|Hello
rubric: When the recipient is unknown the standard formal salutation is 'Dear Sir/Madam'.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An agenda in a business meeting is ___
options: The minutes of a past meeting|A list of items to be discussed at a meeting|A type of report|A formal letter
answer: A list of items to be discussed at a meeting
rubric: The agenda outlines the topics scheduled for discussion at a meeting.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Minutes of a meeting record ___
options: Future plans only|A summary of proceedings decisions and actions taken at a meeting|Only attendees|Only the chairperson's speech
answer: A summary of proceedings decisions and actions taken at a meeting
rubric: Minutes are the official written record of a meeting's proceedings and decisions.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is a quality of a good business letter?
options: Ambiguous language|Clear concise and courteous language|Very long paragraphs|Informal slang
rubric: Good business letters are clear, concise, correct, complete, courteous and considerate.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A curriculum vitae (CV) is a document used to ___
options: Apply for a bank loan|Present a person's qualifications and experience when applying for a job|Record sales figures|File a tax return
answer: Present a person's qualifications and experience when applying for a job
rubric: A CV summarises a person's education, skills and work experience for job applications.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Office equipment that is used to make copies of documents is a ___
options: Scanner|Fax machine|Photocopier|Shredder
rubric: A photocopier (copier) reproduces paper documents in the same format.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Confidentiality in an office means ___
options: Sharing all documents with everyone|Keeping sensitive business information private|Loudly discussing business matters|Posting information on notice boards
rubric: Office confidentiality means protecting sensitive data from unauthorised access or disclosure.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A circular letter is sent to ___
options: One specific person|A large group of people at the same time|The government only|A bank
answer: A large group of people at the same time
rubric: A circular is a letter distributed to many recipients simultaneously, often conveying the same message.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Word processing software is used mainly for ___
options: Accounting calculations|Creating editing and formatting written documents|Video editing|Internet browsing
answer: Creating editing and formatting written documents
rubric: Word processors (like MS Word) create, edit and format text documents.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An organisation chart shows ___
options: Financial accounts|The hierarchy and structure of an organisation|Office equipment|A map of the office
answer: The hierarchy and structure of an organisation
rubric: An org chart illustrates the reporting relationships and structure within an organisation.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Reprographics refers to ___
options: Accounting procedures|The processes of reproducing and duplicating documents|Sending emails|Filing records
answer: The processes of reproducing and duplicating documents
rubric: Reprographics covers copying, printing and duplicating documents in an office context.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is a method of internal communication in an organisation?
options: Customer advertisement|Memo notice board and staff meeting|Newspaper|Radio
answer: Memo notice board and staff meeting
rubric: Internal communication uses memos, meetings, notice boards, intranets and emails.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The purpose of a quotation in business is to ___
options: Confirm goods have been received|State the price and terms at which goods can be supplied|Record payment|List all employees
answer: State the price and terms at which goods can be supplied
rubric: A quotation is a formal statement of the price and conditions for supplying goods or services.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Good time management in an office means ___
options: Spending time chatting|Prioritising tasks to maximise productivity|Arriving late daily|Avoiding urgent work
rubric: Effective time management involves planning and prioritising tasks to work efficiently.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is an example of an external business communication?
options: Staff memo|Internal newsletter|Letter to a customer or supplier|Team meeting
answer: Letter to a customer or supplier
rubric: External communication goes outside the organisation — letters, emails and calls to customers/suppliers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A ledger account that shows how much customers owe a business is the ___
options: Purchases ledger|Sales ledger (debtors ledger)|Nominal ledger|Wages ledger
rubric: The sales/debtors ledger records amounts owed to the business by its credit customers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A business plan is ___
options: A daily work schedule|A written document outlining a business idea goals and strategies|Only a financial forecast|A government requirement only
answer: A written document outlining a business idea goals and strategies
rubric: A business plan details the business concept, market, finances and operational strategies.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Consumer education teaches people to ___
options: Spend money carelessly|Make informed choices when buying goods and services|Avoid all spending|Buy only luxury goods
answer: Make informed choices when buying goods and services
rubric: Consumer education empowers buyers with knowledge to make wise purchasing decisions.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a right of a consumer?
options: The right to be deceived|The right to safety and accurate product information|The right to buy unlimited goods|The right to avoid paying
answer: The right to safety and accurate product information
rubric: Consumer rights include safety, information, choice and redress when goods are defective.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An entrepreneur differs from an employee mainly because the entrepreneur ___
options: Earns a salary|Takes risks and creates business opportunities|Only follows instructions|Works fewer hours
answer: Takes risks and creates business opportunities
rubric: Entrepreneurs innovate, take financial risks and create enterprises; employees work for wages.

subject: Business Studies
stem: NAFDAC in Nigeria is responsible for ___
options: Collecting taxes|Organising elections|Regulating food drugs and consumer products for safety|Banking regulation
answer: Regulating food drugs and consumer products for safety
rubric: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) ensures product safety.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A brand is ___
options: A type of account|A name symbol or design that identifies a product|A government agency|A type of tax
answer: A name symbol or design that identifies a product
rubric: A brand is a distinguishing identity (name, logo, design) that sets a product or company apart.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Market research is carried out to ___
options: Reduce sales|Understand customer needs and market conditions|Increase production costs|Dismiss employees
answer: Understand customer needs and market conditions
rubric: Market research gathers information about consumers and competitors to inform business decisions.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Start-up capital for a small business can come from ___
options: Only banks|Personal savings family loans and grants|Only foreign investors|Only government only
answer: Personal savings family loans and grants
rubric: Small businesses typically start with the owner's savings, family support, grants or microfinance.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is a characteristic of a successful entrepreneur?
options: Laziness|Fear of taking risks|Creativity and resilience|Dependence on government
rubric: Successful entrepreneurs are creative, risk-tolerant, resilient and self-motivated.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The break-even point is when ___
options: Revenue exceeds costs greatly|Revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss|Costs exceed revenue|Sales are at their highest
answer: Revenue equals total costs — neither profit nor loss
rubric: Break-even is where total revenue equals total costs — the point of zero profit/loss.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Consumers should check the ___ label before buying packaged food.
options: Colour|NAFDAC registration and expiry date|Weight only|Brand name only
rubric: Consumers should verify NAFDAC approval and expiry dates to ensure product safety.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of a cottage industry?
options: An oil refinery|A steel factory|A woman making baskets at home|A large automobile plant
answer: A woman making baskets at home
rubric: Cottage industries are small-scale home-based production activities.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The management function that sets goals and outlines how to achieve them is ___
options: Controlling|Organising|Leading|Planning
rubric: Planning is the management function of setting objectives and determining courses of action.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is an economic problem that small businesses face in Nigeria?
options: Too many customers|Access to finance and high interest rates|Excess raw materials|Low inflation
answer: Access to finance and high interest rates
rubric: Nigerian SMEs are constrained by limited credit access and high borrowing costs.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Consumer protection law exists to ___
options: Help sellers only|Protect buyers from unfair trade practices and unsafe products|Increase profits|Reduce competition
answer: Protect buyers from unfair trade practices and unsafe products
rubric: Consumer protection legislation safeguards buyers from exploitation, fraud and harmful goods.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) means businesses ___
options: Maximise profit at all costs|Have obligations to society beyond just making profit|Ignore environmental issues|Pay no taxes
answer: Have obligations to society beyond just making profit
rubric: CSR is the idea that businesses should contribute positively to society and the environment.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Franchising is when ___
options: A government seizes a business|A business owner sells the right to use their brand and system to another party|A partnership dissolves|Shares are sold publicly
answer: A business owner sells the right to use their brand and system to another party
rubric: A franchise grants a franchisee the right to operate using the franchisor's brand and model.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The Standard Organisation of Nigeria (SON) is responsible for ___
options: Tax collection|Setting and enforcing standards for products made in or imported into Nigeria|Organising elections|Managing the stock exchange
answer: Setting and enforcing standards for products made in or imported into Nigeria
rubric: SON ensures Nigerian products and imports meet quality and safety standards.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Gross domestic product (GDP) is used to measure ___
options: A company's profit|The total output of a national economy|Only government spending|Only exports
answer: The total output of a national economy
rubric: GDP measures the total monetary value of all goods and services produced within a country.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of a public sector enterprise in Nigeria?
options: Dangote Group|NNPCL (Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited)|GTBank|Zenith Bank
rubric: NNPCL is a government-owned (public sector) enterprise in Nigeria's oil industry.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Transportation is important to business because it ___
options: Increases office costs|Moves goods and people from one place to another|Replaces advertising|Reduces production
answer: Moves goods and people from one place to another
rubric: Transportation enables the physical movement of raw materials and finished goods across distances.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which mode of transport is most suitable for carrying heavy bulky goods over long distances within Nigeria?
options: Air transport|Pipeline|Road transport|Rail transport
rubric: Rail transport is cost-effective for heavy, bulky cargo over long distances.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Air transport is most suitable for ___
options: Heavy bulky goods|Perishable high-value goods over long distances|Local goods delivery|Oil pipelines
answer: Perishable high-value goods over long distances
rubric: Air freight moves high-value or perishable goods quickly over long distances despite higher cost.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A bill of lading is a document used in ___
options: Road transport only|Air transport|Sea (shipping) transport|Rail transport
rubric: A bill of lading is a shipping document acknowledging receipt of cargo for sea transport.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Pipeline transport is mainly used for moving ___
options: Passengers|Oil gas and water|Manufactured goods|Farm produce
rubric: Pipelines efficiently transport liquid and gaseous products like crude oil and natural gas.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The Internet has revolutionised business communication by ___
options: Making communication slower|Enabling instant global exchange of information|Replacing all face-to-face meetings|Eliminating written documents
answer: Enabling instant global exchange of information
rubric: The internet allows instant, low-cost communication (email, video calls) across the globe.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A waybill is a document used to ___
options: Record bank transactions|Accompany goods in transit and describe their contents|File income tax|Register a business
answer: Accompany goods in transit and describe their contents
rubric: A waybill is a transport document listing the details of goods being shipped.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of road transport in Nigeria?
options: Flexibility|Door-to-door delivery|Traffic congestion and poor road conditions|Low cost for short distances
answer: Traffic congestion and poor road conditions
rubric: Road transport is hampered by poor infrastructure and heavy traffic — particularly in cities.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Communication in business is the process of ___
options: Making goods|Sending and receiving information between parties|Transporting goods|Storing goods
answer: Sending and receiving information between parties
rubric: Business communication is the transmission of information between individuals or organisations.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a form of non-verbal communication?
options: A telephone call|A letter|Body language and gestures|A text message
rubric: Non-verbal communication includes facial expressions, gestures, eye contact and body language.

subject: Business Studies
stem: NIPOST is the government agency in Nigeria responsible for ___
options: Water transport|Postal and courier services|Air transport|Pipeline transport
rubric: NIPOST (Nigeria Postal Service) provides mail and parcel delivery services across Nigeria.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The advantage of water transport over road is ___
options: Faster speed|Ability to carry very heavy cargo at low cost|Door-to-door delivery|Flexibility of routes
answer: Ability to carry very heavy cargo at low cost
rubric: Water transport is ideal for bulk, heavy goods — it is slower but cheaper per tonne.

subject: Business Studies
stem: E-mail is preferred in business because it is ___
options: Expensive and slow|Fast cheap and leaves a written record|Only for large companies|Not secure
answer: Fast cheap and leaves a written record
rubric: Email is cost-effective, near-instant and creates a documented trail of communication.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of vertical communication in a business?
options: Two colleagues chatting|A manager giving instructions to a subordinate|Two departments emailing each other|A customer complaint
answer: A manager giving instructions to a subordinate
rubric: Vertical communication flows up or down the organisational hierarchy — e.g. manager to staff.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Courier services differ from regular post in that they ___
options: Are slower|Offer tracked faster and often door-to-door delivery|Are cheaper|Only handle letters
answer: Offer tracked faster and often door-to-door delivery
rubric: Courier companies provide express, tracked parcel delivery — faster than standard postal service.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A freight forwarder is a company that ___
options: Manufactures goods|Arranges and manages the shipment of goods on behalf of clients|Insures cargo only|Produces transport vehicles
answer: Arranges and manages the shipment of goods on behalf of clients
rubric: Freight forwarders coordinate logistics and documentation for moving goods between countries.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The cost of transporting goods from a factory to a retailer is called ___
options: Handling charge|Freight or carriage charge|Warehouse rent|Commission
rubric: Freight is the charge paid for transporting goods from one place to another.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Radio and television are examples of ___ communication.
options: Personal|Interpersonal|Mass|One-way only
rubric: Radio and TV broadcast to large audiences simultaneously — mass communication media.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of intra-city transport in Nigeria?
options: Lagos to Abuja flight|Kano to Port Harcourt train|Danfo bus service within Lagos|Lagos to London cruise
rubric: Danfo (yellow minibuses) provide intra-city (within Lagos) public transport.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Port Harcourt is important to Nigerian trade mainly because ___
options: It has a major international airport|It is the federal capital|It has a major seaport handling oil exports and imports|It has the largest market
answer: It has a major seaport handling oil exports and imports
rubric: Port Harcourt's seaport handles significant crude oil exports and general cargo imports.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Insurance works on the principle of ___
options: Every person saving alone|Pooling contributions from many people to compensate the few who suffer losses|Guaranteeing profit|Eliminating all risk
answer: Pooling contributions from many people to compensate the few who suffer losses
rubric: Insurance spreads risk — many policyholders pay premiums to a pool that compensates those who suffer loss.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The person or company that takes out an insurance policy is called the ___
options: Insurer|Broker|Insured (policyholder)|Assessor
rubric: The insured (policyholder) is the person or entity protected under an insurance contract.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Life assurance differs from general insurance in that ___
options: It covers property|It pays out on death or at the end of a fixed period|It covers motor vehicles only|It is not offered in Nigeria
answer: It pays out on death or at the end of a fixed period
rubric: Life assurance (not 'insurance') is a long-term policy paying on death or maturity — a certainty, not just a risk.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The principle of insurable interest means ___
options: Anyone can insure anything|You can only insure something in which you have a financial stake|Insurance is free|You must own the insurer
answer: You can only insure something in which you have a financial stake
rubric: Insurable interest requires the policyholder to benefit from the insured item's preservation.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Motor vehicle third-party insurance covers ___
options: Damage to the policyholder's own vehicle|Theft of the car|Injury or damage caused to other people or their property|Fire to the car
answer: Injury or damage caused to other people or their property
rubric: Third-party insurance is the minimum legal requirement — it only covers liability to others.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The principle of subrogation means that after paying a claim the insurer ___
options: Cancels the policy|Takes over the policyholder's rights to claim from a third party|Gives a refund|Reduces the premium
answer: Takes over the policyholder's rights to claim from a third party
rubric: Subrogation allows the insurer to recover its payout by suing the third party responsible.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A no-claims bonus in motor insurance is given to drivers who ___
options: Have had the most accidents|Have not made any claims during the policy period|Pay the highest premiums|Insure the most expensive cars
answer: Have not made any claims during the policy period
rubric: A no-claims discount rewards policyholders who have not claimed — reducing their next premium.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Fire insurance compensates a business for losses due to ___
options: Flood damage|Theft|Fire outbreaks that damage property|Market price drops
rubric: Fire insurance covers financial loss from fire damage to buildings, stock and equipment.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An insurance broker is ___
options: An employee of an insurance company|An independent agent who arranges insurance on behalf of clients|A claims assessor|A government regulator
answer: An independent agent who arranges insurance on behalf of clients
rubric: Brokers are intermediaries who match clients with suitable insurance products from different insurers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The NAICOM in Nigeria regulates ___
options: Banks|Insurance companies|The stock exchange|Government spending
rubric: NAICOM (National Insurance Commission) supervises and regulates Nigeria's insurance industry.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Marine insurance covers ___
options: Air cargo only|Ships cargo and freight against sea-voyage risks|Inland road transport|Agricultural produce
answer: Ships cargo and freight against sea-voyage risks
rubric: Marine insurance protects ships, cargo and freight against losses at sea.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An excess (deductible) in insurance means ___
options: The full amount the insurer pays|The amount the policyholder must pay first before the insurer pays the rest|A bonus for no claims|The total premium
answer: The amount the policyholder must pay first before the insurer pays the rest
rubric: An excess is the first portion of any claim that the insured must bear themselves.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Assurance is different from insurance because assurance ___
options: Covers uncertain events|Covers events that will certainly happen (like death)|Does not pay benefits|Is only for property
answer: Covers events that will certainly happen (like death)
rubric: Assurance covers events that will definitely occur (death); insurance covers uncertain risks.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Health insurance helps individuals by ___
options: Making them immune to disease|Covering medical costs when they fall ill|Giving them free medicine|Preventing accidents
answer: Covering medical costs when they fall ill
rubric: Health insurance pays for medical expenses — consultations, hospitalisation and treatment.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Comprehensive car insurance covers ___
options: Third-party liability only|Third-party liability fire theft AND damage to the policyholder's own car|Only theft|Only engine damage
answer: Third-party liability fire theft AND damage to the policyholder's own car
rubric: Comprehensive cover is the most complete — it covers own damage plus all third-party risks.

subject: Business Studies
stem: An insurance policy document is ___
options: A banking document|The formal contract between the insurer and the insured|A receipt for goods|A customs form
answer: The formal contract between the insurer and the insured
rubric: The policy document is the legal contract specifying the terms, conditions and coverage of insurance.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Crop insurance helps farmers by ___
options: Increasing crop prices|Providing compensation for crop losses due to drought flood or pests|Giving free seeds|Reducing farm labour
answer: Providing compensation for crop losses due to drought flood or pests
rubric: Crop insurance protects farmers against income loss from weather events or pests.

subject: Business Studies
stem: When an insurance company shares a large risk with other insurers it is called ___
options: Subrogation|Reinsurance|Underwriting|Premium discount
rubric: Reinsurance allows insurers to transfer portions of large risks to other insurance companies.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Contributory negligence in insurance means ___
options: The insurer is negligent|Both the insured and another party share responsibility for a loss|Only the third party is at fault|The insurer refuses to pay
answer: Both the insured and another party share responsibility for a loss
rubric: When the insured partly contributed to the loss, contributory negligence may reduce the claim payout.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The purpose of a proposal form in insurance is to ___
options: Record the premium paid|Provide the insurer with information needed to assess and price the risk|Show proof of ownership|Confirm a claim
answer: Provide the insurer with information needed to assess and price the risk
rubric: A proposal form collects details about the risk so the insurer can decide whether and at what premium to insure.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A cooperative society is an autonomous association of persons united voluntarily to meet their ___
options: Competitive needs|Common economic social and cultural needs through a jointly owned enterprise|Political ambitions|Government requirements
answer: Common economic social and cultural needs through a jointly owned enterprise
rubric: Cooperatives are member-owned organisations formed for mutual economic and social benefit.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is a type of cooperative society in Nigeria?
options: Public limited company|Consumer cooperative|Government parastatal|Sole proprietorship
rubric: Consumer cooperatives buy goods in bulk and sell to members at lower prices.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) identifies ___ cooperative principles.
options: Three|Five|Seven|Ten
rubric: The ICA's 1995 Statement of Cooperative Identity defines seven principles for cooperatives.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A thrift and credit cooperative helps members by ___
options: Manufacturing goods|Collecting savings and providing loans at low interest to members|Selling groceries|Organising elections
answer: Collecting savings and providing loans at low interest to members
rubric: Thrift and credit cooperatives pool members' savings and lend at favourable rates.

subject: Business Studies
stem: In a cooperative the surplus (profit) is distributed to members based on ___
options: The amount they invested only|Their level of patronage (transactions with the cooperative)|Age of membership|Educational qualification
answer: Their level of patronage (transactions with the cooperative)
rubric: In cooperatives, surplus (dividend) is distributed proportionally to members' use of the cooperative.

subject: Business Studies
stem: One benefit of belonging to a cooperative is ___
options: Higher individual risk|Access to credit and bulk-purchase discounts|Reduced ability to save|No profit sharing
answer: Access to credit and bulk-purchase discounts
rubric: Cooperatives give members access to affordable credit and the benefits of bulk buying.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A producer cooperative helps farmers by ___
options: Competing against them|Collectively processing and marketing their produce for better prices|Employing them only|Reducing their land
answer: Collectively processing and marketing their produce for better prices
rubric: Producer cooperatives aggregate members' output and negotiate better prices with buyers.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The governing body of a cooperative society is the ___
options: Managing Director|Board of Directors appointed by government|Committee of Management elected by members|Bank Manager
answer: Committee of Management elected by members
rubric: Cooperative members elect a committee of management to run the society on their behalf.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Workers in a factory form a cooperative to ___
options: Compete with management|Provide welfare services social activities and financial support for members|Avoid paying taxes|Reduce output
answer: Provide welfare services social activities and financial support for members
rubric: Workers' cooperatives provide mutual support — savings, loans, welfare and social activities.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A housing cooperative helps members by ___
options: Renting expensive apartments|Collectively building or purchasing affordable homes for members|Managing a hotel|Selling land at high prices
answer: Collectively building or purchasing affordable homes for members
rubric: Housing cooperatives pool resources to provide affordable housing for their members.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The law governing cooperative societies in Nigeria includes ___
options: Companies and Allied Matters Act|Cooperative Societies Law of each state|Banking Act|Insurance Act
answer: Cooperative Societies Law of each state
rubric: Cooperatives in Nigeria are primarily regulated by individual state cooperative society laws.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A marketing cooperative assists farmers mainly by ___
options: Growing their crops|Providing seeds only|Pooling their produce for collective sale at better prices|Building irrigation only
answer: Pooling their produce for collective sale at better prices
rubric: Marketing cooperatives aggregate members' produce to negotiate stronger market prices.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The registration of a cooperative society in Nigeria is done by the ___
options: National Revenue Service|State Ministry of Agriculture or Cooperative Affairs|Central Bank|Corporate Affairs Commission
answer: State Ministry of Agriculture or Cooperative Affairs
rubric: Cooperatives are registered with the relevant state ministry — usually cooperative or agricultural affairs.

subject: Business Studies
stem: One-member-one-vote in a cooperative means ___
options: Only large investors vote|Every member has equal voting rights regardless of the amount invested|The chairman has extra votes|Only founders vote
answer: Every member has equal voting rights regardless of the amount invested
rubric: Democratic control is a core cooperative principle — each member has one vote, not proportional to shares.

subject: Business Studies
stem: School cooperative societies teach students to ___
options: Spend money wastefully|Save regularly and learn financial discipline|Avoid teamwork|Take loans only
answer: Save regularly and learn financial discipline
rubric: School cooperatives instil habits of saving, borrowing responsibly and cooperative management.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A share in a cooperative is different from a company share because ___
options: It is worth more|It does not carry voting rights in cooperatives|It entitles the member to one vote regardless of shares held|It can be sold on the stock exchange
answer: It entitles the member to one vote regardless of shares held
rubric: Unlike company shareholders, cooperative members each have one vote irrespective of their shareholding.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The Rochdale Pioneers of England are famous for ___
options: Inventing banking|Establishing the first successful modern cooperative in 1844|Starting the industrial revolution|Building the first railway
answer: Establishing the first successful modern cooperative in 1844
rubric: The Rochdale Society of Equitable Pioneers (1844) is considered the model for the modern cooperative movement.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The annual general meeting (AGM) of a cooperative is held to ___
options: Plan marketing campaigns|Review the year's activities elect officers and approve accounts|Train new employees|Sign contracts with banks
answer: Review the year's activities elect officers and approve accounts
rubric: The AGM is the cooperative's principal democratic meeting — for accountability, elections and planning.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A cooperative society differs from a public limited company in that a cooperative ___
options: Seeks maximum profit for investors|Gives greater voting rights to larger investors|Exists primarily for the benefit of its members not investors|Sells shares to the general public freely
answer: Exists primarily for the benefit of its members not investors
rubric: Cooperatives prioritise member benefit over profit maximisation — their core distinction from corporations.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A multipurpose cooperative society offers ___
options: Only credit services|Only grocery retail|A wide range of services such as savings credit farming and marketing to members|Only housing services
answer: A wide range of services such as savings credit farming and marketing to members
rubric: Multipurpose cooperatives combine several functions — finance, marketing, inputs — for member benefit.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Marketing is the process of ___
options: Only selling goods|Identifying customer needs and satisfying them profitably|Only advertising products|Only producing goods
answer: Identifying customer needs and satisfying them profitably
rubric: Marketing encompasses research, product development, pricing, promotion and distribution.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The four Ps of marketing are ___
options: People Place Profit Plan|Product Price Place Promotion|Purchase Price Profit Position|Production Planning Pricing Publicity
rubric: The marketing mix (4Ps): Product, Price, Place and Promotion.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Advertising differs from personal selling because advertising ___
options: Is more expensive per contact|Reaches a large audience at once through mass media|Involves face-to-face interaction|Is more persuasive
answer: Reaches a large audience at once through mass media
rubric: Advertising uses mass media (TV, radio, print) to reach many people simultaneously.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an above-the-line advertising medium?
options: Free samples|Sales representatives|Television commercials|Point-of-sale displays
rubric: Above-the-line advertising uses mass media (TV, radio, newspaper) — paid, broad-reach media.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A sales promotion activity is ___
options: A TV advertisement|Buy-one-get-one-free offers and loyalty discounts|Publishing a company report|Registering a company
rubric: Sales promotion (below-the-line) uses short-term incentives to stimulate immediate purchase.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Public relations (PR) in business aims to ___
options: Sell products directly|Build and maintain a positive image of the company with the public|Manage accounts|Manufacture goods
answer: Build and maintain a positive image of the company with the public
rubric: PR creates and maintains a favourable public perception of a company or brand.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A market survey helps a business to ___
options: Reduce production|Understand what customers want and current market conditions|Hire more workers|Avoid taxes
answer: Understand what customers want and current market conditions
rubric: Market surveys gather consumer opinions to guide product development and marketing decisions.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A product's brand name is important because it ___
options: Increases production cost|Helps consumers identify and differentiate it from competitors|Has no legal protection|Reduces demand
answer: Helps consumers identify and differentiate it from competitors
rubric: A brand name identifies a product and builds customer loyalty and recognition.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The pricing strategy where a product is launched at a low price to gain market share quickly is called ___
options: Price skimming|Penetration pricing|Cost-plus pricing|Psychological pricing
rubric: Penetration pricing sets a low initial price to attract many customers and build market share rapidly.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of the following is an example of after-sales service?
options: Advertising the product|Offering warranty repairs and customer support after purchase|Setting the price|Transporting goods to the shop
answer: Offering warranty repairs and customer support after purchase
rubric: After-sales service includes warranties, repairs, helplines and follow-up — it builds customer loyalty.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Social media marketing uses platforms like ___
options: Newspapers and billboards|Instagram Facebook and Twitter/X to promote products|Radio and TV only|Postal mail only
answer: Instagram Facebook and Twitter/X to promote products
rubric: Social media marketing leverages platforms like Instagram, Facebook and X (Twitter) for brand promotion.

subject: Business Studies
stem: A product life cycle has the stages ___
options: Planning growth decline end|Introduction growth maturity and decline|Start success and failure|Only growth and decline
rubric: The product life cycle has four stages: Introduction, Growth, Maturity and Decline.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Customer satisfaction in business leads to ___
options: Higher costs|Repeat purchases and positive word-of-mouth|Reduced sales|Lower quality
rubric: Satisfied customers return and recommend the business to others — driving sustained growth.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which of these is an outdoor advertising medium?
options: Social media post|Newspaper ad|Billboard on a highway|Radio jingle
rubric: Billboards are out-of-home (OOH) advertising — visible to road users and pedestrians.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Point-of-sale materials such as shelf-talkers and display stands are examples of ___
options: Above-the-line advertising|Below-the-line promotion in retail stores|Mass media advertising|Public relations
rubric: Point-of-sale (POS) materials are below-the-line — placed in retail stores to influence purchase decisions.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The AIDA model in advertising stands for ___
options: Awareness Interest Desire Action|Advertising Investment Distribution Analysis|Ability Income Demand Awareness|Attention Interest Decision Analysis
rubric: AIDA describes the stages a consumer passes through: Awareness → Interest → Desire → Action.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Niche marketing means targeting ___
options: Every possible customer|A very specific narrow segment of the market|Only wealthy customers|Only government customers
answer: A very specific narrow segment of the market
rubric: Niche marketing focuses on a small, specific, well-defined segment with particular needs.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Which body in Nigeria regulates advertising content?
options: NCC|NAFDAC|Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON)|SON
rubric: ARCON (formerly APCON) is the statutory body that regulates advertising practice in Nigeria.

subject: Business Studies
stem: Market segmentation involves ___
options: Selling to everyone the same way|Dividing the market into distinct groups with similar needs|Reducing the product range|Cutting prices for all customers
answer: Dividing the market into distinct groups with similar needs
rubric: Market segmentation divides the total market into sub-groups (segments) with similar characteristics.

subject: Business Studies
stem: The main purpose of packaging is to ___
options: Make the product heavier|Protect the product attract buyers and provide product information|Increase production cost|Replace advertising
answer: Protect the product attract buyers and provide product information
rubric: Good packaging protects the product, differentiates it on shelves and communicates product details.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Yoruba kingdom that was the largest and most powerful in the 18th century was ___
options: Benin|Oyo|Ife|Ijebu
rubric: The Old Oyo Empire was the dominant Yoruba political and military power in the 18th century.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Benin Kingdom is famous for its ___
options: Cotton textiles|Elaborate bronze and ivory artworks|Gold trade|Iron smelting only
rubric: The Benin Kingdom produced world-famous bronze plaques and ivory carvings from at least the 13th century.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Kanem-Bornu Empire was located in the ___
options: South-west of Nigeria|North-east of Nigeria around Lake Chad|South-east of Nigeria|Middle Belt only
answer: North-east of Nigeria around Lake Chad
rubric: Kanem-Bornu was centred around Lake Chad — spanning modern north-east Nigeria, Niger and Chad.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Ile-Ife is regarded as the cradle of ___
options: Hausa civilisation|Yoruba civilisation|Igbo civilisation|Fulani civilisation
rubric: Ile-Ife (Ife) is the spiritual and historical origin of Yoruba culture and the seat of their creation myth.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Sokoto Caliphate was founded in 1804 by ___
options: Muhammadu Buhari|Usman Dan Fodio|Alafin of Oyo|Jaja of Opobo
rubric: Usman Dan Fodio led the Fulani Jihad that established the Sokoto Caliphate in 1804.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Nri Kingdom is associated with the origins of ___
options: Yoruba people|Igbo cultural institutions and sacred authority|Hausa states|Efik traders
answer: Igbo cultural institutions and sacred authority
rubric: The Nri Kingdom in present-day Anambra State is regarded as a foundation of Igbo civilisation.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Oba is the title of the traditional ruler among the ___
options: Hausa|Yoruba and Edo people|Igbo|Tiv
rubric: 'Oba' is the royal title used by traditional rulers in Yoruba and Benin (Edo) kingdoms.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Hausa city-states (Hausa Bakwai) included ___
options: Kano Katsina and Zaria|Lagos Ibadan and Abeokuta|Enugu Onitsha and Aba|Calabar Uyo and Benin City
rubric: The seven 'true' Hausa states (Hausa Bakwai) included Kano, Katsina, Zaria, Gobir, Biram, Daura and Rano.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The ancient trans-Saharan trade route linked ___
options: West Africa to East Africa|West African kingdoms to North Africa and the Middle East|Nigeria only to Ghana|South America to West Africa
answer: West African kingdoms to North Africa and the Middle East
rubric: Trans-Saharan trade routes connected sub-Saharan West Africa to Mediterranean North Africa and beyond.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Jukun, Kwararafa and Nupe were ___
options: Yoruba sub-groups|Middle Belt kingdoms and peoples|Lagos districts|Colonial provinces
rubric: These were influential states/peoples in the Middle Belt region of central Nigeria.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Efik and Ibibio peoples are mainly found in present-day ___
options: Oyo State|Borno State|Cross River and Akwa Ibom States|Kano State
answer: Cross River and Akwa Ibom States
rubric: The Efik (Calabar) and Ibibio are indigenous peoples of Cross River and Akwa Ibom States.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The first Ooni of Ife according to Yoruba tradition is ___
options: Sango|Oduduwa|Obatala|Shango
rubric: Oduduwa is regarded in Yoruba tradition as the progenitor of the Yoruba people and first Ooni of Ife.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Ogiso dynasty preceded which Nigerian kingdom?
options: Oyo|The Benin Kingdom|The Sokoto Caliphate|The Nri Kingdom
rubric: The Ogiso ('rulers of the sky') were the pre-Oba dynasty that ruled Benin before the current Oba dynasty.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The main commodity that made the Kano emirate wealthy was ___
options: Oil|Long-distance trade in leather goods textiles and kola|Fish|Timber
answer: Long-distance trade in leather goods textiles and kola
rubric: Kano was a great commercial city exporting leather goods, cloth and kola nuts across the Sahara.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Arochukwu oracle (Chukwu oracle) was significant because it ___
options: Controlled Benin|Exercised spiritual and political authority over many Igbo communities|Ruled the Hausa states|Managed the slave trade alone
answer: Exercised spiritual and political authority over many Igbo communities
rubric: The Long Juju of Arochukwu (Ibini Ukpabi) was a powerful oracle used to settle disputes and controlled trade routes.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The concept of Igbo 'stateless society' refers to the fact that ___
options: The Igbo had no culture|Most Igbo communities were governed by councils of elders and age grades rather than monarchs|The Igbo had no territory|The Igbo were not organised
answer: Most Igbo communities were governed by councils of elders and age grades rather than monarchs
rubric: Most Igbo groups were decentralised — governed by age grades, titled men and village assemblies, not kings.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Yoruba god of thunder and lightning is ___
options: Ogun|Sango|Oya|Obatala
rubric: Sango is the Yoruba deity of thunder and lightning — he was a historical Alaafin of Oyo deified after death.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Jihad of Usman Dan Fodio aimed to ___
options: Fight British colonisation|Purify Islam and establish Sharia governance in the Hausa states|Conquer the Yoruba|Trade with Europeans
answer: Purify Islam and establish Sharia governance in the Hausa states
rubric: Dan Fodio's Jihad (1804–1808) overthrew corrupt Hausa rulers and established Islamic governance.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Which of the following empires controlled the Nupe people before the Jihad?
options: Kanem-Bornu|The Oyo Empire at its height|Benin Kingdom|The British
answer: The Oyo Empire at its height
rubric: At its zenith the Oyo Empire exacted tribute from the Nupe and other neighbouring groups.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Trade in which commodity first drew European traders to the Niger Delta region?
options: Gold|Palm oil|Pepper and cloth|Ivory
rubric: After the slave trade, European merchants shifted to palm oil — the main commodity from the Niger Delta.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The term 'Emirate' in the Sokoto Caliphate referred to ___
options: A province governed by an Emir under the Caliph|A type of market|A trade route|A Yoruba clan
answer: A province governed by an Emir under the Caliph
rubric: The Caliphate was divided into Emirates — territories governed by Emirs answerable to the Sultan of Sokoto.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Oyo Ile (Old Oyo) declined mainly because of ___
options: British invasion|Fulani Jihad pressure and internal power struggles|Igbo migration|Natural disaster
answer: Fulani Jihad pressure and internal power struggles
rubric: The Oyo Empire collapsed in the early 19th century due to Fulani raids and internal political crises.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Bronze casting in the Benin Kingdom was the work of ___
options: Farmers|A hereditary guild of palace craftsmen|European missionaries|Arab traders
answer: A hereditary guild of palace craftsmen
rubric: Bronze casting was controlled by the Igun Eronmwon guild — hereditary craftsmen who worked exclusively for the Oba.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The main political unit among the Tiv people was the ___
options: Kingdom with a king|The tar (clan/lineage group) with elders|A caliphate|A city-state
rubric: Tiv society was organised around lineage groups (tar) governed by councils of elders — acephalous.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The first known dynasty of Borno was the ___
options: Kanem|Sefuwa (Sayfawa)|Fulani|Hausa
rubric: The Sayfawa dynasty ruled Kanem-Bornu for about a thousand years — one of the world's longest-running dynasties.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Kola nuts were important in pre-colonial Nigerian trade because they ___
options: Were used as currency|Were highly valued for cultural religious and stimulant uses and widely traded|Had medical properties only|Were exported to Europe mainly
answer: Were highly valued for cultural religious and stimulant uses and widely traded
rubric: Kola nuts were used in ceremonies, offered as gifts and traded across West Africa — a major pre-colonial commodity.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Agemo cult and Oro society are associated with ___
options: Igbo people|The Ijebu Yoruba|Hausa people|Efik people
rubric: Agemo and Oro are important religious societies among the Ijebu Yoruba of Ogun State.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Which river was historically central to trade and communication in southern Nigeria?
options: River Niger and River Benue|River Nile|River Congo|River Zambezi
rubric: The Niger and Benue rivers were major arteries of trade, communication and transport in pre-colonial Nigeria.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Alafin was the supreme ruler of ___
options: Benin Kingdom|The Oyo Empire|Kanem-Bornu|The Sokoto Caliphate
rubric: The Alafin of Oyo was the paramount ruler of the Oyo Empire.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Obi is the traditional ruler of ___
options: The Hausa|The Igbo of Delta State and Onitsha|The Fulani|The Kanuri
answer: The Igbo of Delta State and Onitsha
rubric: The Obi is the title of traditional rulers among the Western Igbo and the Obi of Onitsha.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Atlantic slave trade transported enslaved Africans mainly to ___
options: Europe and Asia|The Americas (Caribbean and North and South America)|Australia|The Middle East
answer: The Americas (Caribbean and North and South America)
rubric: The transatlantic slave trade (15th–19th centuries) took millions of Africans to the New World.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Which European country first arrived on the West African coast for trade in the 15th century?
options: Britain|France|Portugal|Spain
rubric: Portuguese explorers arrived on the West African coast in the mid-15th century — the first Europeans to trade.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The abolition of the British slave trade was achieved in ___
rubric: The British Slave Trade Act 1807 abolished the slave trade (not slavery) in the British Empire.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The 'legitimate trade' that replaced the slave trade in Nigeria involved mainly ___
options: Gold and diamonds|Palm oil palm kernels and groundnuts|Ivory only|Rubber only
answer: Palm oil palm kernels and groundnuts
rubric: After abolition, 'legitimate' commerce shifted to agricultural products — palm oil, palm kernels and groundnuts.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Berlin Conference of 1884–1885 resulted in ___
options: African independence|The partition of Africa among European powers|The end of colonialism|A peace treaty
answer: The partition of Africa among European powers
rubric: The Berlin Conference formalised European colonisation by dividing Africa into spheres of influence.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Royal Niger Company was a British company that ___
options: Traded in salt only|Held a charter to govern trade and territory in the Niger Delta and northern Nigeria|Helped Nigerians gain independence|Manufactured goods in Nigeria
answer: Held a charter to govern trade and territory in the Niger Delta and northern Nigeria
rubric: The Royal Niger Company (formerly United African Company) governed trade and territory under British charter 1886–1900.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Frederick Lugard introduced the policy of ___ in northern Nigeria.
options: Direct rule|Indirect rule through existing emirs and chiefs|Complete military rule|Federal rule
answer: Indirect rule through existing emirs and chiefs
rubric: Lord Lugard implemented Indirect Rule — governing through existing traditional rulers — in northern Nigeria.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The amalgamation of the Northern and Southern Protectorates of Nigeria occurred in ___
rubric: Lord Lugard amalgamated the Northern and Southern Protectorates to form the Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria on 1 January 1914.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Which Nigerian city served as the colonial capital before Abuja?
options: Kano|Enugu|Lagos|Ibadan
rubric: Lagos was Nigeria's capital from colonial times until 1991 when Abuja became the new federal capital.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Christian missionaries in Nigeria contributed to ___
options: The slave trade|Spreading education establishing schools and translating the Bible into local languages|Opposing all Nigerian culture|Opposing independence
answer: Spreading education establishing schools and translating the Bible into local languages

rubric: Soyinka's works examine the tension between Yoruba tradition and the disruption of colonialism.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Chinua Achebe's novel 'Things Fall Apart' depicts ___
options: Colonial administration|The impact of colonialism on traditional Igbo society through the character Okonkwo|Nigerian independence|A love story
answer: The impact of colonialism on traditional Igbo society through the character Okonkwo
rubric: Achebe's landmark novel (1958) portrays the disintegration of Igbo society under colonial pressure.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Major Chukwuma Nzeogwu is associated with ___
options: The 1979 election|The first military coup of January 1966|The Biafran declaration|The 1983 coup
answer: The first military coup of January 1966
rubric: Nzeogwu was the lead planner and face of the January 15, 1966 coup.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Sani Abacha ruled Nigeria from ___
rubric: Sani Abacha came to power in November 1993 and ruled until his death in June 1998.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Gani Fawehinmi was a prominent Nigerian ___
options: Businessman|Pro-democracy lawyer and human rights activist|Military officer|Journalist only
answer: Pro-democracy lawyer and human rights activist
rubric: Chief Gani Fawehinmi was a senior advocate and fierce defender of human rights and democracy.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Ogoni struggle led by Ken Saro-Wiwa was a campaign against ___
options: Military rule only|Environmental degradation and oil pollution in Ogoniland by Shell|Taxation|Lagos expansion
answer: Environmental degradation and oil pollution in Ogoniland by Shell
rubric: Ken Saro-Wiwa led MOSOP's non-violent campaign against Shell's environmental damage in Ogoniland.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Umaru Yar'Adua was notable for ___
options: Being Nigeria's longest-serving president|Enacting the 7-Point Agenda and the Niger Delta Amnesty Programme|Starting the civil war|Leading the 1983 coup
answer: Enacting the 7-Point Agenda and the Niger Delta Amnesty Programme
rubric: Yar'Adua's key legacies were his 7-Point Agenda development plan and the 2009 Niger Delta amnesty.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Goodluck Jonathan became president in 2010 because ___
options: He won an election|He led a coup|He succeeded Yar'Adua who died in office|He was appointed by the military
answer: He succeeded Yar'Adua who died in office
rubric: Goodluck Jonathan became Acting then full President after Umaru Yar'Adua's death in May 2010.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Peace Accord signed before the 2015 election was significant because it ___
options: Was ignored by all parties|Committed candidates to accept results peacefully — enabling the first opposition victory in Nigerian history|Ended the Boko Haram insurgency|Changed the constitution
answer: Committed candidates to accept results peacefully — enabling the first opposition victory in Nigerian history
rubric: The Abuja Peace Accord helped ensure a peaceful transfer of power after Buhari defeated Jonathan in 2015.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Aliko Dangote is significant in Nigerian economic history as ___
options: A military general|Nigeria's richest person and founder of one of Africa's largest industrial conglomerates|The Central Bank Governor|An elected senator
answer: Nigeria's richest person and founder of one of Africa's largest industrial conglomerates
rubric: Dangote Group (cement, sugar, flour, refinery) makes Aliko Dangote Africa's wealthiest person.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Philip Emeagwali is a Nigerian-American known for ___
options: Founding Nollywood|His work in supercomputing — developing early high-speed computing methods|Being a nationalist politician|Winning the Nobel Prize
answer: His work in supercomputing — developing early high-speed computing methods
rubric: Philip Emeagwali's work on the Connection Machine earned him the 1989 Gordon Bell Prize.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Niger Delta avengers and MEND are militant groups associated with ___
options: Northern Nigeria|The Delta region protesting marginalisation and oil pollution|The Yoruba south-west|Biafra agitation
answer: The Delta region protesting marginalisation and oil pollution
rubric: MEND (Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta) and similar groups agitate for resource control.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Biafran War ended on ___
options: 30 May 1967|12 January 1970|1 October 1963|15 January 1966
rubric: Biafra surrendered on 12 January 1970 — ending the civil war after about 30 months.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Muhammadu Buhari first became head of state through ___
options: A democratic election in 1983|A military coup in December 1983|Appointment by ECOWAS|Being vice-president
rubric: Buhari came to power via a coup on 31 December 1983 overthrowing Shehu Shagari.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Bola Tinubu became Nigeria's president in ___
rubric: Bola Ahmed Tinubu was inaugurated as Nigeria's 16th president on 29 May 2023.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The EndSARS protest of October 2020 was a demonstration against ___
options: High electricity tariffs|Police brutality — specifically demanding the disbandment of the SARS unit|Government corruption|Fuel scarcity
answer: Police brutality — specifically demanding the disbandment of the SARS unit
rubric: #EndSARS was a mass protest against SARS (Special Anti-Robbery Squad) police brutality in Nigeria.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The phrase 'Africa's giant' is used to describe Nigeria because ___
options: It has the largest land area in Africa|It has Africa's largest population and economy|It won the most World Cups|It is militarily strongest
answer: It has Africa's largest population and economy
rubric: Nigeria is called 'The Giant of Africa' for its population (~220m), economy and cultural influence.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala is significant as ___
options: Nigeria's first female president|The first African and first woman to serve as Director-General of the WTO|The first female senator|A military officer
answer: The first African and first woman to serve as Director-General of the WTO
rubric: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala became DG of the World Trade Organization in March 2021.

subject: Nigerian History
