stem: Nigeria's oil industry began when oil was first commercially discovered at ___
options: Warri|Aba|Oloibiri in Bayelsa State|Port Harcourt
rubric: Nigeria's first commercial oil find was at Oloibiri (then Rivers Province) in 1956 by Shell-BP.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The oil boom of the 1970s led to ___
options: Improved agriculture|Massive government revenue but neglect of agriculture and manufacturing|Reduced corruption|Cheaper imports
answer: Massive government revenue but neglect of agriculture and manufacturing
rubric: The oil boom funded infrastructure but caused 'Dutch Disease' — collapse of agriculture and other exports.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Nigeria joined OPEC in ___
rubric: Nigeria joined OPEC (Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries) on 1 July 1971.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The groundnut pyramids of Kano were a symbol of ___
options: Oil wealth|Nigeria's agricultural export prosperity before the oil era|Foreign aid|Charity
answer: Nigeria's agricultural export prosperity before the oil era
rubric: Groundnut pyramids — huge stacks of bagged groundnuts — symbolised Kano's pre-oil agricultural wealth.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Universal Basic Education (UBE) scheme was designed to ___
options: Reduce university enrolment|Ensure free compulsory education for all children from primary through JSS 3|Train only teachers|Fund private schools
answer: Ensure free compulsory education for all children from primary through JSS 3
rubric: UBE (launched 1999) provides 9 years of free and compulsory basic education in Nigeria.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Nigeria's Vision 20:2020 was a development plan aimed at ___
options: Military supremacy|Making Nigeria one of the world's 20 largest economies by the year 2020|Electoral reform|Oil production targets
answer: Making Nigeria one of the world's 20 largest economies by the year 2020
rubric: Vision 20:2020 (launched 2009) targeted placing Nigeria among the top-20 global economies.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 reformed the oil sector by ___
options: Nationalising all oil companies|Restructuring governance commercialising NNPC and creating a host community fund|Banning foreign oil firms|Reducing oil production
answer: Restructuring governance commercialising NNPC and creating a host community fund
rubric: The PIA 2021 overhauled Nigeria's petroleum law — transforming NNPC into NNPCL and benefiting host communities.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Agricultural Development Projects (ADPs) were set up in Nigeria to ___
options: Process oil|Modernise smallholder farming through extension services inputs and infrastructure|Build schools only|Manage water supply
answer: Modernise smallholder farming through extension services inputs and infrastructure
rubric: ADPs (established in the 1970s–80s) provided technical support, inputs and credit to smallholder farmers.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The removal of fuel subsidy in 2023 led to ___
options: Cheaper petrol|Immediate sharp increase in petrol prices and inflation|More oil production|Stronger naira
answer: Immediate sharp increase in petrol prices and inflation
rubric: When Tinubu removed fuel subsidy in May 2023 petrol prices rose sharply, driving inflation.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Operation Feed the Nation (OFN) was launched in 1976 to ___
options: Export food|Encourage Nigerians to grow their own food and reduce dependence on imports|Import more food|Privatise agriculture
answer: Encourage Nigerians to grow their own food and reduce dependence on imports
rubric: OFN (Obasanjo military government) aimed to boost domestic food production and reduce food imports.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Anchor Borrowers Programme was designed to ___
options: Support urban construction|Provide smallholder farmers with inputs and a guaranteed market through CBN financing|Fund oil exploration|Pay civil servants
answer: Provide smallholder farmers with inputs and a guaranteed market through CBN financing
rubric: The Anchor Borrowers Programme (CBN) links smallholder farmers to agro-processors via subsidised inputs.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Nigeria's largest single source of export revenue is ___
options: Cocoa|Groundnuts|Crude oil|Gold
rubric: Crude oil accounts for over 80% of Nigeria's export earnings and about 50% of government revenue.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The National Economic Recovery and Growth Plan (ERGP) was Nigeria's economic blueprint under ___
options: Jonathan|Obasanjo|Buhari (2016–2020)|Tinubu
rubric: The ERGP was Nigeria's medium-term plan (2017–2020) under the Buhari administration.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The naira was devalued significantly in 2023 because ___
options: Oil production increased|The CBN unified exchange rate windows — removing the artificial official rate|Trade increased|Gold was discovered
answer: The CBN unified exchange rate windows — removing the artificial official rate
rubric: In June 2023 the CBN unified FX windows, effectively devaluing the naira to reflect market rates.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Lagos is Nigeria's economic capital because it ___
options: Is the federal capital|Hosts the government|Accounts for about 25–30% of Nigeria's GDP and most financial activity|Has the most oil
answer: Accounts for about 25–30% of Nigeria's GDP and most financial activity
rubric: Lagos dominates Nigeria's economy — it hosts the financial sector, ports and most large corporations.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline (TSGP) project was designed to ___
options: Supply oil to Europe|Transport Nigerian natural gas to Algeria and on to Europe|Supply water across the Sahara|Move groundnuts northward
answer: Transport Nigerian natural gas to Algeria and on to Europe
rubric: The TSGP (Nigeria–Niger–Algeria) pipeline was planned to export Nigerian gas to Europe.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Nigeria's economic policy of import substitution industrialisation (ISI) aimed to ___
options: Import more manufactured goods|Produce locally goods that were previously imported to save foreign exchange|Export raw materials only|Reduce farming
answer: Produce locally goods that were previously imported to save foreign exchange
rubric: ISI encouraged domestic manufacturing to reduce import dependence and build industrial capacity.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Ajaokuta Steel Complex was built in Kogi State to ___
options: Produce crude oil|Develop Nigeria's iron and steel industry for industrialisation|Manufacture cars|Process cocoa
answer: Develop Nigeria's iron and steel industry for industrialisation
rubric: Ajaokuta Steel Company (started 1979) was meant to anchor Nigeria's heavy industrialisation.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The NCC (Nigerian Communications Commission) regulates ___
options: Banking|Telecommunications and internet services in Nigeria|Broadcasting only|Road transport
answer: Telecommunications and internet services in Nigeria
rubric: The NCC licenses and regulates Nigeria's telecoms sector — including mobile networks and ISPs.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: MTN Nigeria is historically significant as ___
options: Nigeria's oldest bank|One of the first and largest mobile network operators that transformed telecommunications in Nigeria|A government oil company|A food company
answer: One of the first and largest mobile network operators that transformed telecommunications in Nigeria
rubric: MTN launched in Nigeria in 2001 and helped drive the mobile telephony revolution — Nigeria now has 200m+ subscriptions.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Ife-Modakeke conflict is historically rooted in ___
options: Colonial land policy|A longstanding dispute between two Osun State communities over land and identity|Military affairs|Oil resources
answer: A longstanding dispute between two Osun State communities over land and identity
rubric: The Ife-Modakeke conflict is a historic communal dispute in Osun State between Ife and Modakeke communities.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Deji is the title of the traditional ruler of ___
options: Ile-Ife|Akure|Oyo|Ondo
rubric: The Deji of Akure is the paramount traditional ruler of Akure in Ondo State.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Awka blacksmiths were famous pre-colonially for ___
options: Weaving cloth|Producing high-quality iron tools and travelling widely as itinerant smiths|Fishing|Salt production
answer: Producing high-quality iron tools and travelling widely as itinerant smiths
rubric: Awka blacksmiths of Anambra State were renowned craftsmen who traded their skills across Igboland.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The word 'Nigeria' was coined by ___
options: Frederick Lugard|Queen Victoria|Flora Shaw (later Flora Lugard)|King Edward VII
rubric: Flora Shaw, a journalist and later wife of Lugard, coined 'Nigeria' in a 1897 Times article.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Direct rule as a colonial policy meant ___
options: Governing through existing chiefs|European officials governing Africans directly replacing traditional rulers|Partnership with local rulers|Self-governance
answer: European officials governing Africans directly replacing traditional rulers
rubric: Direct rule replaced indigenous governance with European administrators — contrasting with Lugard's indirect rule.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Abandoned Property controversy after the Civil War affected mainly ___
options: Hausa traders|Igbo who had fled properties in Rivers and Cross River States during the war|Yoruba professionals|Foreign investors
answer: Igbo who had fled properties in Rivers and Cross River States during the war
rubric: Post-war, Igbo found properties they had abandoned in the east and midwest declared 'abandoned property'.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) in Nigeria is responsible for ___
options: Printing currency|Promoting and protecting human rights and investigating violations|Conducting elections|Managing prisons
answer: Promoting and protecting human rights and investigating violations
rubric: The NHRC monitors, protects and promotes human rights across Nigeria.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Nigeria's COAS stands for ___
options: Chief of Army Science|Chief of Army Staff|Commander of Armed Services|Chief Adviser on Security
rubric: COAS is the professional head of the Nigerian Army — the Chief of Army Staff.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Ojude-Oba Festival is celebrated in ___
options: Kano by the Hausa|Ijebu-Ode by the Ijebu Yoruba|Calabar by the Efik|Enugu by the Igbo
rubric: The Ojude-Oba ('King's Frontyard') is an Ijebu Yoruba festival held three days after Eid al-Adha.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Ogoni People's Declaration of 1990 called for ___
options: More oil drilling|Political autonomy and environmental justice for the Ogoni in the Niger Delta|Military rule|Separation from Nigeria
answer: Political autonomy and environmental justice for the Ogoni in the Niger Delta
rubric: MOSOP's 1990 Ogoni Bill of Rights demanded autonomy, fair share of oil revenue and environmental repair.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is used to measure ___
options: GDP growth|The average price change of a basket of goods and services — i.e. inflation|Stock market performance|Trade balance
answer: The average price change of a basket of goods and services — i.e. inflation
rubric: CPI measures inflation by tracking price changes of a representative basket of consumer goods.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Nigeria's external debt is managed by ___
options: CBN alone|The Debt Management Office (DMO)|NNPCL|EFCC
rubric: The DMO coordinates and manages Nigeria's domestic and external public debt.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Olusegun Obasanjo served as Nigeria's leader ___
options: Once as a civilian|Once as military head of state (1976–1979) and once as elected president (1999–2007)|Three times|Only as a civilian
answer: Once as military head of state (1976–1979) and once as elected president (1999–2007)
rubric: Obasanjo led Nigeria twice — as military head of state and later as elected president.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: Dora Akunyili served as Director-General of NAFDAC and became known for ___
options: Her banking career|Her aggressive campaign against fake and substandard drugs in Nigeria|Military service|Oil production|
answer: Her aggressive campaign against fake and substandard drugs in Nigeria
rubric: Prof. Dora Akunyili transformed NAFDAC — her crusade against counterfeit drugs saved countless lives.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The masquerade tradition in Igbo culture is tied to ___
options: Tourism only|The ancestors (mmuo) — masquerades represent the spirits of the dead|Colonial influence|Christian worship
answer: The ancestors (mmuo) — masquerades represent the spirits of the dead
rubric: In Igbo belief, masquerades (mmuo) are manifestations of ancestral spirits returning to the living world.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The phrase 'divide and rule' describes a colonial strategy of ___
options: Sharing colonial wealth|Creating divisions among colonised peoples to prevent unified resistance|Sharing governing power|Dividing land equally
answer: Creating divisions among colonised peoples to prevent unified resistance
rubric: Britain exploited ethnic, religious and political differences to prevent a unified resistance to colonial rule.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The 1978 Land Use Act in Nigeria ___
options: Privatised all land|Vested all land in Nigeria in the state governments held in trust for citizens|Abolished traditional land ownership|Gave land to foreign investors
answer: Vested all land in Nigeria in the state governments held in trust for citizens
rubric: The Land Use Act 1978 nationalised all land — vesting it in state governors as trustees for the people.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Supreme Court of Nigeria is ___
options: A legislative body|The highest court of the land with final jurisdiction on constitutional matters|The Central Bank's oversight body|A police body
answer: The highest court of the land with final jurisdiction on constitutional matters
rubric: The Supreme Court is Nigeria's apex court — its rulings on constitutional and civil matters are final.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Dangote Refinery in Lagos is significant because it ___
options: Refines gold|Is one of the world's largest single-train oil refineries aiming to end petrol imports|Is government-owned|Processes food crops
answer: Is one of the world's largest single-train oil refineries aiming to end petrol imports
rubric: The Dangote Refinery (650,000 bpd capacity) aims to refine Nigeria's crude oil locally.

subject: Nigerian History
stem: The Atilogwu dance is a traditional acrobatic dance of the ___
options: Yoruba|Hausa|Igbo|Efik
rubric: Atilogwu is a vibrant, acrobatic Igbo youth dance from Igboland — known for its athleticism.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Puberty is the period when ___
options: A child starts school|The body develops adult sexual characteristics|Bones stop growing|A person learns to walk
answer: The body develops adult sexual characteristics
rubric: Puberty is the stage of physical development where the body matures sexually.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The skeletal system provides the body with ___
options: Blood supply|Support shape and protection for internal organs|Digestion|Hormone production
answer: Support shape and protection for internal organs
rubric: The skeleton supports the body, gives it shape and protects vital organs like the brain and heart.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The muscular system enables the body to ___
options: Digest food|Pump blood|Move and produce body heat|Filter blood
rubric: Muscles contract to produce movement and generate heat — maintaining body temperature.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which organ pumps blood through the body?
options: Liver|Lungs|Brain|Heart
rubric: The heart is a muscular pump that circulates blood through the cardiovascular system.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The lungs are responsible for ___
options: Filtering blood|Absorbing nutrients|Exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide (respiration)|Producing hormones
rubric: The lungs are the site of gaseous exchange — oxygen enters the blood and CO₂ is expelled.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cartilage in the body is ___
options: Harder than bone|A flexible connective tissue found at joints and in the ears and nose|The same as muscle|Made of fat
answer: A flexible connective tissue found at joints and in the ears and nose
rubric: Cartilage is a firm but flexible connective tissue that cushions joints and shapes ears and nose.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: During adolescence boys experience all of the following EXCEPT ___
options: Growth of facial hair|Deepening of voice|Widening of hips|Increased height
rubric: Widening of the hips is a female puberty change — not typical in boys.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The endocrine system controls body functions through ___
options: Nerve impulses|Hormones released into the bloodstream|Muscles|The skeleton
rubric: The endocrine system regulates growth, metabolism and reproduction via hormones.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which nutrient is the main building material for muscles and tissues?
options: Carbohydrates|Fats|Protein|Vitamins
rubric: Proteins are the building blocks of body tissues — essential for growth and repair.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The average normal body temperature of a healthy adult is ___
rubric: Normal human body temperature is approximately 37°C (98.6°F).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The nervous system is responsible for ___
options: Digesting food|Controlling and coordinating all body activities|Producing blood cells|Fighting infections
answer: Controlling and coordinating all body activities
rubric: The nervous system receives stimuli and coordinates the body's responses.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Joints where the bones can move freely are called ___
options: Fixed joints|Slightly movable joints|Freely movable (synovial) joints|Cartilaginous joints
rubric: Synovial joints (e.g. knee, hip, shoulder) allow a wide range of movement.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The spine (vertebral column) consists of ___
options: 12 bones|24 bones|33 vertebrae|40 bones
rubric: The adult vertebral column typically has 33 vertebrae (or 26 considering fused sections).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Red blood cells are produced in the ___
options: Liver|Kidneys|Bone marrow|Spleen
rubric: Red blood cells (erythrocytes) are produced in the red bone marrow.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The function of white blood cells is to ___
options: Carry oxygen|Clot blood|Fight infections and pathogens|Transport nutrients
rubric: White blood cells (leucocytes) are the immune system's soldiers — they destroy pathogens.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of these is a long bone in the human body?
options: Skull|Rib|Femur (thigh bone)|Sternum
rubric: The femur is the body's longest bone — a classic long bone.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The digestive system breaks food into ___
options: Only water|Nutrients small enough to be absorbed into the bloodstream|Waste only|Energy directly
answer: Nutrients small enough to be absorbed into the bloodstream
rubric: Digestion converts food into absorbable nutrients — glucose, amino acids, fatty acids.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Menarche refers to ___
options: The growth of underarm hair|A boy's voice breaking|A girl's first menstrual period|The end of puberty
rubric: Menarche is the first occurrence of menstruation — a key milestone in female puberty.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The skin's main functions include ___
options: Blood production|Protection sensation temperature regulation and vitamin D synthesis|Digestion|Reproduction
answer: Protection sensation temperature regulation and vitamin D synthesis
rubric: The skin protects against infection, senses the environment, regulates temperature and synthesises vitamin D.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of these is NOT a function of the liver?
options: Detoxifying harmful substances|Producing bile|Pumping blood|Storing glycogen
rubric: The liver detoxifies, produces bile and stores glycogen — pumping blood is the heart's role.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The kidneys maintain body health by ___
options: Producing insulin|Filtering waste products from blood and regulating fluid balance|Making red blood cells only|Digesting food
answer: Filtering waste products from blood and regulating fluid balance
rubric: The kidneys filter blood, excrete waste as urine and balance fluid and electrolyte levels.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Growth in children is mainly controlled by ___
options: Blood pressure|The growth hormone produced by the pituitary gland|Diet alone|Sleep only
answer: The growth hormone produced by the pituitary gland
rubric: Growth hormone (GH) from the anterior pituitary gland stimulates growth and cell reproduction.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Posture refers to ___
options: A person's height|The way a person holds and positions their body|Speed of movement|Body weight
answer: The way a person holds and positions their body
rubric: Good posture means the body is correctly aligned — reducing strain on muscles and joints.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The correct classification of joints by movement includes ___
options: Flexible immovable and fixed|Fixed slightly movable and freely movable|Hard soft and middle|Open closed and half-open
answer: Fixed slightly movable and freely movable
rubric: Joints are classified as: fixed (sutures of skull), slightly movable (vertebrae) and freely movable (synovial).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Semen in males is produced by the ___
options: Bladder|Testes|Kidney|Prostate only
rubric: Sperm (semen) is produced in the testes — the male reproductive organs.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Personal hygiene involves ___
options: Cleaning the environment only|Caring for the cleanliness of your own body — washing bathing and dental care|Eating balanced meals|Exercising daily
answer: Caring for the cleanliness of your own body — washing bathing and dental care
rubric: Personal hygiene practices (bathing, handwashing, dental care) prevent infection and disease.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The correct way to brush teeth is ___
options: Back and forth vigorously|With circular and up-down strokes for two minutes twice a day|Only when eating sweets|Once a week
answer: With circular and up-down strokes for two minutes twice a day
rubric: Proper brushing technique uses gentle circular/up-down strokes for 2 minutes, twice daily.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Washing hands with soap is important mainly because it ___
options: Makes hands smell nice|Removes dirt jewellery and germs preventing the spread of disease|Softens the skin|Whitens the hands
answer: Removes dirt jewellery and germs preventing the spread of disease
rubric: Handwashing with soap is one of the most effective ways to prevent diarrhoea, respiratory and other infections.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Dehydration occurs when ___
options: The body has too much water|The body loses more fluid than it takes in|A person eats too much|A person exercises too little
answer: The body loses more fluid than it takes in
rubric: Dehydration happens when fluid loss exceeds intake — causing dizziness, dark urine and weakness.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Safe water for drinking should be ___
options: Any water from a river|Treated or boiled — free of harmful bacteria and chemicals|Coloured water|Salty water
answer: Treated or boiled — free of harmful bacteria and chemicals
rubric: Drinking water must be treated (or boiled) to be free of pathogens and harmful chemicals.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Immunisation protects against diseases by ___
options: Treating disease after infection|Stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies before infection|Providing nutrients|Eliminating all germs
answer: Stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies before infection
rubric: Vaccines expose the immune system to antigens, building immunity without causing the disease.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Oral rehydration therapy (ORS) is used to treat ___
options: Malaria|Dehydration caused by diarrhoea and vomiting|Broken bones|High blood pressure
answer: Dehydration caused by diarrhoea and vomiting
rubric: ORS replaces fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhoea — a life-saving treatment.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Body odour is mainly caused by ___
options: Eating too much protein|Bacteria breaking down sweat on the skin|Too much exercise|Wearing perfume
answer: Bacteria breaking down sweat on the skin
rubric: Body odour results from bacteria metabolising sweat — regular washing controls it.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Acne (pimples) in adolescents is caused mainly by ___
options: Poor diet only|Overactive sebaceous (oil) glands blocking and infecting pores|Sunburn|Lack of sleep
answer: Overactive sebaceous (oil) glands blocking and infecting pores
rubric: Adolescent hormones stimulate excess sebum production — causing blocked pores and pimples.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Fluoride in toothpaste helps to ___
options: Whiten teeth instantly|Strengthen tooth enamel and prevent cavities|Remove all bacteria|Replace brushing
answer: Strengthen tooth enamel and prevent cavities
rubric: Fluoride remineralises enamel and inhibits the bacteria that cause dental caries.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The recommended daily water intake for an average adult is about ___
options: 1 litre|2–3 litres (8–10 glasses)|5 litres|Half a litre
rubric: Adults generally need 2–3 litres of fluid per day — more in hot conditions or during exercise.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Malaria is transmitted through ___
options: Contaminated water|The bite of a female Anopheles mosquito|Touching an infected person|Eating infected food
answer: The bite of a female Anopheles mosquito
rubric: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted by the bite of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sleeping under an insecticide-treated mosquito net helps to ___
options: Improve sleep quality only|Reduce malaria by preventing mosquito bites|Cure malaria|Repel all insects
answer: Reduce malaria by preventing mosquito bites
rubric: ITNs create a physical and chemical barrier against mosquito bites — significantly reducing malaria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cholera is spread mainly through ___
options: Airborne droplets|Insect bites|Contaminated food and water|Sexual contact
rubric: Cholera is a waterborne disease caused by Vibrio cholerae — spread via contaminated water and food.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Regular medical check-ups are important because they ___
options: Are compulsory by law|Help detect diseases early when they are easier to treat|Are only for sick people|Replace healthy eating
answer: Help detect diseases early when they are easier to treat
rubric: Routine health screenings catch conditions early — improving treatment outcomes.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) can be prevented by ___
options: Taking vitamins only|Abstinence and consistent use of condoms|Drinking more water|Taking antibiotics daily
answer: Abstinence and consistent use of condoms
rubric: Abstinence is 100% effective; condoms significantly reduce STI transmission.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: HIV is mainly transmitted through ___
options: Sharing food|Insect bites|Unprotected sexual contact and sharing needles|Shaking hands
answer: Unprotected sexual contact and sharing needles
rubric: HIV is spread by contact with infected blood, semen or breast milk — primarily through sex or needles.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) for HIV ___
options: Cures HIV completely|Suppresses the virus allowing people to live longer healthier lives|Is the same as a vaccine|Is harmful
answer: Suppresses the virus allowing people to live longer healthier lives
rubric: ART controls HIV viral load to undetectable levels — people on ART live near-normal lifespans.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Open defecation is dangerous because it ___
options: Is unhygienic only|Contaminates water sources and food with pathogens causing diseases like cholera and typhoid|Uses too much land|Causes air pollution mainly
answer: Contaminates water sources and food with pathogens causing diseases like cholera and typhoid
rubric: Faecal contamination of water spreads diarrhoeal diseases — open defecation is a major public health hazard.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Typhoid fever is caused by ___
options: A virus|Bacterium Salmonella typhi from contaminated food and water|A parasite in blood|A fungal infection
answer: Bacterium Salmonella typhi from contaminated food and water
rubric: Typhoid is a bacterial disease caused by Salmonella typhi — spread through contaminated food and water.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of the following is a sign of good mental health?
options: Constant anxiety|Ability to manage stress make decisions and relate well to others|Avoiding all social contact|Refusing to eat
answer: Ability to manage stress make decisions and relate well to others
rubric: Good mental health includes emotional stability, effective coping and healthy social relationships.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Adequate sleep is important for health because it ___
options: Increases body fat|Allows the body to repair and restore energy and supports brain function|Reduces physical activity|Causes laziness
answer: Allows the body to repair and restore energy and supports brain function
rubric: Sleep is when the body repairs tissues, consolidates memory and resets the immune system.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sunscreen protects the skin by ___
options: Moisturising only|Blocking harmful UV radiation from the sun|Making skin lighter|Removing sweat
answer: Blocking harmful UV radiation from the sun
rubric: Sunscreen absorbs or reflects ultraviolet radiation — reducing sunburn and skin cancer risk.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Anaemia results from ___
options: Too much iron|A deficiency of haemoglobin or red blood cells reducing oxygen transport|High blood pressure|Excess calcium
answer: A deficiency of haemoglobin or red blood cells reducing oxygen transport
rubric: Anaemia (often iron or folate deficiency) reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of the following is a communicable (infectious) disease?
options: Diabetes|High blood pressure|Tuberculosis (TB)|Cancer
rubric: Tuberculosis is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spreads from person to person — a communicable disease.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Carbohydrates provide the body mainly with ___
options: Building materials|Energy|Immunity|Vitamin A
rubric: Carbohydrates (starch and sugars) are the body's primary and most readily available energy source.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Vitamins are nutrients needed by the body in ___
options: Very large quantities|Moderate quantities|Small quantities but are essential for normal functioning|No specific quantity
answer: Small quantities but are essential for normal functioning
rubric: Vitamins are micronutrients required in small amounts to support vital biochemical processes.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A deficiency of vitamin C causes ___
options: Rickets|Night blindness|Scurvy|Anaemia
rubric: Scurvy — characterised by bleeding gums and weakness — results from vitamin C deficiency.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Rickets in children is caused by lack of ___
options: Vitamin C|Vitamin B12|Vitamin D and calcium|Iron
rubric: Rickets causes soft, weak bones — due to vitamin D and/or calcium deficiency in growing children.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Iron is an important mineral because it is needed to ___
options: Strengthen bones|Form haemoglobin in red blood cells|Build muscles|Produce hormones
answer: Form haemoglobin in red blood cells
rubric: Iron is essential for haemoglobin synthesis — deficiency causes iron-deficiency anaemia.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Kwashiorkor is a disease of ___
options: Excess fat intake|Severe protein deficiency in young children|Vitamin A deficiency|Excess sugar intake
answer: Severe protein deficiency in young children
rubric: Kwashiorkor typically affects children after weaning — caused by inadequate protein intake.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Marasmus differs from kwashiorkor in that marasmus is caused by ___
options: Too much protein|Only protein deficiency|Severe deficiency of BOTH calories and protein|Only calorie excess
answer: Severe deficiency of BOTH calories and protein
rubric: Marasmus is severe wasting caused by overall energy and protein starvation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which food group provides the most energy per gram?
options: Carbohydrates|Proteins|Fats and oils|Vitamins
rubric: Fats provide 9 kcal/g — more than double the energy of carbohydrates or proteins (4 kcal/g each).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of ___
options: Vitamin D|Vitamin K|Vitamin A|Vitamin B1
rubric: Vitamin A (retinol) is essential for night vision — deficiency causes night blindness.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A balanced diet should contain ___
options: Only carbohydrates and proteins|Foods from all nutrient groups in the right proportions|Only vitamins and minerals|As much fat as possible
answer: Foods from all nutrient groups in the right proportions
rubric: A balanced diet includes carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water in correct amounts.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Dietary fibre is important because it ___
options: Builds muscles|Has high caloric value|Aids digestion and prevents constipation|Replaces water
rubric: Dietary fibre (roughage) promotes bowel regularity and supports gut health.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of the following is the best source of protein for a Nigerian diet?
options: Rice|Beans and legumes|Yam|Palm oil
rubric: Beans, soybeans and other legumes are excellent and affordable plant sources of protein.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Calcium is most needed by the body for ___
options: Blood production|Energy|Strong bones and teeth|Fighting infections
rubric: Calcium is essential for building and maintaining strong bones and teeth.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Obesity is linked to eating too much ___
options: Fresh vegetables|Water|High-calorie processed and fatty foods combined with low physical activity|Protein only
answer: High-calorie processed and fatty foods combined with low physical activity
rubric: Excess calorie intake and insufficient exercise lead to obesity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of the following is a function of water in the body?
options: Building muscles|Regulating temperature transporting nutrients and removing waste|Providing energy|Strengthening bones
answer: Regulating temperature transporting nutrients and removing waste
rubric: Water regulates body temperature, transports substances and flushes waste through urine and sweat.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Iodine deficiency causes ___
options: Anaemia|Scurvy|Goitre (swelling of the thyroid gland)|Rickets
rubric: Iodine is needed for thyroid hormones — deficiency causes the thyroid to enlarge (goitre).

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which nutrient group should form the largest part of a balanced diet?
options: Fats|Proteins|Carbohydrates|Vitamins and minerals
rubric: Carbohydrates should form the largest energy proportion of a balanced diet — about 50–60%.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Junk food is characterised by ___
options: High nutritional value|Being rich in vitamins|High calories low nutrients and excessive sugar salt or fat|Being good for athletes
answer: High calories low nutrients and excessive sugar salt or fat
rubric: Junk food (fast food, snacks) provides empty calories — high energy but low nutritional value.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Food fortification means ___
options: Cooking food longer|Adding extra nutrients (e.g. vitamins and minerals) to food to improve its nutritional value|Making food spicier|Preserving food for longer
answer: Adding extra nutrients (e.g. vitamins and minerals) to food to improve its nutritional value
rubric: Food fortification adds micronutrients to commonly consumed foods — e.g. vitamin A to cooking oil.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for infants up to ___
options: 1 month|3 months|6 months|1 year
rubric: WHO recommends exclusive breastfeeding (no other food or drink) for the first 6 months of life.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In football (soccer) a match consists of ___
options: Two halves of 40 minutes each|Two halves of 45 minutes each|Four quarters of 20 minutes|Three periods of 30 minutes
rubric: A standard football match has two 45-minute halves — 90 minutes of regulation play.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In basketball how many players from each team are on the court at one time?
rubric: Basketball is played with 5 players per team on the court — 10 players total.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In volleyball a team scores a point when ___
options: It serves|The ball touches the ground on the opponent's side or the opponent faults|A player jumps|The referee calls time
answer: The ball touches the ground on the opponent's side or the opponent faults
rubric: Rally-point scoring: a team scores when the ball lands in the opponent's court or the opponent commits an error.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A 'birdie' in table tennis or badminton refers to ___
options: A very fast serve|A shuttlecock in badminton|A missed shot|A foul serve
rubric: The shuttlecock (birdie) is the conical projectile used in badminton.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In a standard football team the goalkeeper's main role is to ___
options: Score goals|Prevent the opposing team from scoring by guarding the goal|Referee the game|Pass the ball from midfield
answer: Prevent the opposing team from scoring by guarding the goal
rubric: The goalkeeper (goalie) is the last line of defence — the only player permitted to use their hands.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A 'penalty kick' in football is awarded when ___
options: A player scores a goal|A foul is committed inside the penalty area of the defending team|A corner kick is given|A goal kick is awarded
answer: A foul is committed inside the penalty area of the defending team
rubric: A penalty kick is awarded for a direct-free-kick offence inside the defending team's penalty area.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In athletics the ___ event combines running jumping and throwing skills.
options: 100m sprint|Heptathlon/decathlon|Long jump|Javelin
rubric: The heptathlon (women) and decathlon (men) combine 7 and 10 events respectively — all disciplines.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The baton change in relay races must occur within ___
options: The starting blocks|The exchange zone (a 20m section of the track)|Any part of the track|The finish line
answer: The exchange zone (a 20m section of the track)
rubric: In relay races, baton exchanges must be completed within the designated 20m takeover zone.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In high jump the athlete must clear the bar ___
options: By any means|By jumping from both feet|Without knocking it off — using any technique (now Fosbury Flop)|Using only the feet
answer: Without knocking it off — using any technique (now Fosbury Flop)
rubric: Clearing the bar cleanly is the rule — the Fosbury Flop (back-first) is the dominant modern technique.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: How many sets does a standard men's tennis Grand Slam match usually require to win?
options: 2 of 3|3 of 5|2 of 4|1 of 3
rubric: Men's Grand Slam matches are best of 5 sets — a player must win 3 sets to win the match.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In netball the goal shooter can shoot from ___
options: Anywhere on the court|Only the centre circle|Inside the shooting circle (goal circle)|Behind the centre line
rubric: Only the GS (Goal Shooter) and GA (Goal Attack) can shoot — and only from within the shooting circle.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The standard height of a basketball hoop above the floor is ___
rubric: The standard basketball rim height is 10 feet (3.048m) above the court.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: An offside in football occurs when ___
options: A player is behind the ball|A player is nearer to the opponent's goal line than the ball and the last outfield defender at the moment the ball is played|A player handles the ball|A goalkeeper picks up the ball
answer: A player is nearer to the opponent's goal line than the ball and the last outfield defender at the moment the ball is played
rubric: Offside: an attacker is in an offside position when closer to the goal than the last defender at the moment the ball is played.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In boxing a 'knockout' (KO) means ___
options: A foul by the fighter|The opponent is knocked to the floor and cannot get up within 10 counts|A draw|A disqualification
answer: The opponent is knocked to the floor and cannot get up within 10 counts
rubric: A KO occurs when a boxer is floored and cannot rise before the referee counts to 10.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The long jump take-off must be made from ___
options: Anywhere in the runway|The edge of the take-off board without overstepping|A running start of exactly 10m|Both feet simultaneously
answer: The edge of the take-off board without overstepping
rubric: The long jump requires a one-foot take-off from behind the take-off board — stepping over is a foul.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A 'red card' in football means ___
options: A warning only|The player is sent off and cannot return|A penalty kick|A corner kick
answer: The player is sent off and cannot return
rubric: A red card results in immediate expulsion from the game — the player cannot be replaced.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The swimming stroke that uses both arms simultaneously in an overhead motion is the ___
options: Backstroke|Breaststroke|Butterfly stroke|Freestyle
rubric: The butterfly stroke uses both arms simultaneously in an overhead arc — the most demanding stroke.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The dimensions of a standard football pitch are approximately ___
rubric: FIFA rules allow pitch length 90–120m and width 45–90m — typically about 105 × 68m.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In cricket the batting team aims to score ___
options: Goals|Runs by hitting the ball and running between the wickets|Tries|Points by throwing
answer: Runs by hitting the ball and running between the wickets
rubric: Cricket teams score runs — batters hit the ball and run between the wickets.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A 'fault' in tennis means ___
options: Winning a point|Failing to serve the ball correctly into the service box|A lost set|The net is hit
answer: Failing to serve the ball correctly into the service box
rubric: A fault in tennis is when the serve fails to land in the correct service box.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In athletics the shot put requires the athlete to ___
options: Throw a javelin|Propel a heavy metal ball (shot) as far as possible from a circular throwing area|Run 100m|Perform a high jump
answer: Propel a heavy metal ball (shot) as far as possible from a circular throwing area
rubric: Shot put involves pushing/putting a heavy metal ball from the shoulder within a 2.135m circle.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The duty of a referee in sports is to ___
options: Play alongside athletes|Enforce the rules of the game ensure fair play and settle disputes|Coach the team|Keep score only
answer: Enforce the rules of the game ensure fair play and settle disputes
rubric: The referee is the on-field official responsible for enforcing rules and managing fair play.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In swimming the freestyle event allows any stroke but swimmers usually choose the ___ as it is fastest.
options: Breaststroke|Butterfly|Front crawl|Backstroke
rubric: The front crawl (crawl) is the fastest swimming stroke — almost universally used in freestyle events.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The IAAF (now World Athletics) governs ___
options: Football worldwide|International athletics (track and field and road running)|Olympic boxing|Swimming
answer: International athletics (track and field and road running)
rubric: World Athletics (formerly IAAF) is the international federation governing track and field and road running.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In a 4 × 100m relay how many runners are in each team?
rubric: The 4 × 100m relay has 4 runners who each run 100m — passing a baton to the next runner.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Physical fitness is defined as ___
options: Being a professional athlete|The ability to carry out daily tasks with vigour without undue fatigue|Only having big muscles|Being very thin
answer: The ability to carry out daily tasks with vigour without undue fatigue
rubric: Physical fitness is the capacity to perform daily activities efficiently with energy to spare.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cardiovascular endurance refers to ___
options: Strength of the arms|The ability of the heart and lungs to sustain prolonged physical activity|Speed of running|Flexibility of joints
answer: The ability of the heart and lungs to sustain prolonged physical activity
rubric: Cardiovascular endurance (aerobic capacity) is the heart–lung system's ability to sustain exercise.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Flexibility is best developed through ___
options: Weightlifting|Sprinting|Regular stretching exercises|Swimming only
rubric: Flexibility exercises (stretches, yoga) increase the range of motion at joints.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Muscular strength refers to ___
options: The ability to run fast|The maximum force a muscle or muscle group can exert in a single effort|Muscle endurance|Flexibility
answer: The maximum force a muscle or muscle group can exert in a single effort
rubric: Muscular strength is the peak force a muscle can generate in one maximal contraction.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Warming up before exercise helps to ___
options: Make exercise shorter|Prepare the muscles and joints for activity and reduce injury risk|Make athletes faster|Replace training
answer: Prepare the muscles and joints for activity and reduce injury risk
rubric: Warm-up increases body temperature and blood flow — reducing the risk of muscle tears and sprains.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cool-down after exercise is important because it ___
options: Is only for professional athletes|Gradually lowers heart rate and prevents blood pooling in the muscles|Makes muscles weaker|Wastes time
answer: Gradually lowers heart rate and prevents blood pooling in the muscles
rubric: Cool-down brings the body safely back to resting state — reducing post-exercise dizziness and soreness.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Aerobic exercise is characterised by ___
options: Short intense bursts without oxygen|Sustained moderate activity that uses oxygen — like jogging and swimming|Lifting maximum weights|Holding the breath
answer: Sustained moderate activity that uses oxygen — like jogging and swimming
rubric: Aerobic exercise uses oxygen to generate energy — it improves cardiovascular endurance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Body composition refers to ___
options: Height and weight only|The ratio of fat to lean (muscle bone and organ) mass in the body|Only muscle mass|Bone density only
answer: The ratio of fat to lean (muscle bone and organ) mass in the body
rubric: Body composition measures fat vs lean tissue — an indicator of health beyond just body weight.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Agility in physical fitness is ___
options: The ability to lift heavy weights|The ability to change body position quickly and accurately|Running very fast in a straight line|Standing on one leg
answer: The ability to change body position quickly and accurately
rubric: Agility is the capacity for rapid, accurate movement changes — important in many sports.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Reaction time in sports refers to ___
options: The time to complete a full race|The time between a stimulus and the body's movement response|The time to recover after injury|Flexibility speed
answer: The time between a stimulus and the body's movement response
rubric: Reaction time is how quickly an athlete responds to a signal — e.g. a sprinter reacting to the starter's gun.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Regular physical activity reduces the risk of all of the following EXCEPT ___
options: Heart disease|Type 2 diabetes|Obesity|Flu caused by a virus
rubric: Exercise reduces risk of lifestyle diseases (heart disease, diabetes, obesity) but cannot prevent viral infections like flu.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Muscle cramps during exercise are often caused by ___
options: Too much water|Dehydration and mineral (electrolyte) imbalance|Too much rest|Lack of sleep
rubric: Dehydration and loss of electrolytes (sodium, potassium) during exercise cause painful muscle cramps.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The recommended minimum physical activity for adolescents per day is ___
options: 10 minutes of light walking|60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity|2 hours of any activity|30 minutes of sitting exercise
answer: 60 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity
rubric: WHO recommends adolescents accumulate at least 60 minutes of moderate-to-vigorous activity daily.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Overtraining syndrome occurs when ___
options: An athlete rests too much|An athlete trains too intensely without adequate recovery causing fatigue and injury|An athlete eats too much|An athlete stops sport
answer: An athlete trains too intensely without adequate recovery causing fatigue and injury
rubric: Overtraining leads to performance decline, chronic fatigue and increased injury risk.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The FITT principle in exercise planning stands for ___
options: Fast Intense Timed Training|Frequency Intensity Time and Type of exercise|Fun Interesting Tiring and Tough|Fast Intense Tactical Training
answer: Frequency Intensity Time and Type of exercise
rubric: FITT guides exercise programming: how often, how hard, how long and what kind of exercise.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Isometric exercises involve ___
options: Running or jumping|Muscle contractions where the muscle length does not change (pushing against a fixed object)|Stretching alone|Lifting weights only
answer: Muscle contractions where the muscle length does not change (pushing against a fixed object)
rubric: Isometric exercise generates force without movement — e.g. pressing against a wall.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of these activities is classified as anaerobic exercise?
options: Jogging 5km|Long-distance swimming|A 100m sprint|Slow cycling for 30 minutes
rubric: Anaerobic exercise is short, very high-intensity work — like sprinting — where oxygen supply is insufficient.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Good balance and coordination in sports is attributed to ___
options: Large muscles only|The cerebellum of the brain and practised motor skills|High calorie intake|Strong bones
answer: The cerebellum of the brain and practised motor skills
rubric: The cerebellum coordinates balance and fine motor control — practice reinforces these neural pathways.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sports massage helps athletes by ___
options: Replacing warm-up|Reducing muscle tension improving circulation and speeding recovery|Building muscles|Improving flexibility permanently
answer: Reducing muscle tension improving circulation and speeding recovery
rubric: Sports massage loosens muscle knots, improves blood flow and accelerates post-exercise recovery.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: An athlete's resting heart rate tends to be ___ that of a non-athlete of the same age.
options: Higher than|The same as|Lower than|Double
rubric: Trained athletes have stronger, more efficient hearts — their resting heart rate is typically lower.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The primary purpose of first aid is to ___
options: Replace professional medical treatment|Preserve life prevent deterioration and promote recovery until medical help arrives|Only bandage wounds|Diagnose illness
answer: Preserve life prevent deterioration and promote recovery until medical help arrives
rubric: First aid is immediate care to stabilise a victim before professional medical treatment.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The RICE treatment for sports injuries stands for ___
options: Rest Ice Compression Elevation|Run Immediately Continue Exercise|Reduce Injury Continue Exercise|Rest Inject Cool Elevate
rubric: RICE is the standard first-aid protocol for soft tissue injuries — reducing pain and swelling.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation) chest compressions should be ___
options: Slow and gentle|Hard rapid compressions — about 100–120 per minute at 5–6cm depth|Done only on children|Done once then stopped
answer: Hard rapid compressions — about 100–120 per minute at 5–6cm depth
rubric: Effective CPR compressions are hard and fast — pushing down 5–6cm at 100–120 per minute.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A sprain is an injury to ___
options: A bone|A muscle|A ligament (tissue connecting bones)|An artery
rubric: A sprain stretches or tears a ligament — the tissue connecting bones at a joint.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A strain (muscle pull) differs from a sprain because it involves ___
options: Ligament damage|Bone fracture|Stretching or tearing of a muscle or tendon|Joint dislocation
answer: Stretching or tearing of a muscle or tendon
rubric: A strain is an overstretched or torn muscle or tendon — tendons connect muscle to bone.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The recovery position is used for ___
options: Performing CPR|Placing an unconscious breathing person on their side to keep the airway clear|Treating fractures|Cooling a burn
answer: Placing an unconscious breathing person on their side to keep the airway clear
rubric: The recovery position (lateral position) prevents an unconscious casualty from choking on vomit.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: When treating a minor burn the first step is to ___
options: Apply butter or oil|Cover with a blanket|Cool under running cold water for 10–20 minutes|Pop any blisters
answer: Cool under running cold water for 10–20 minutes
rubric: Cooling a burn under running water for 10–20 minutes reduces heat damage and pain.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Heimlich manoeuvre is used to help a person who is ___
options: Drowning|Unconscious|Choking on an airway obstruction|Having a heart attack
rubric: The Heimlich manoeuvre uses abdominal thrusts to expel a foreign object blocking the airway.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: When controlling severe bleeding the recommended first action is to ___
options: Remove the object if embedded|Apply firm direct pressure to the wound|Apply a tourniquet immediately|Elevate the limb first without pressure
answer: Apply firm direct pressure to the wound
rubric: Direct pressure on the wound is the first and most effective step to control haemorrhage.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Protective equipment in contact sports is important to ___
options: Improve performance only|Reduce the risk of injury during play|Make athletes look professional|Satisfy sponsors
answer: Reduce the risk of injury during play
rubric: Helmets, pads, mouthguards and other protective gear minimise sports injury risk.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A sports first aid kit should contain ___
options: Food and drinks|Bandages antiseptic wipes ice packs scissors and latex gloves|Only painkillers|Only a thermometer
answer: Bandages antiseptic wipes ice packs scissors and latex gloves
rubric: A sports first aid kit includes wound care, bandages, cold packs and protective supplies.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: In the event of a suspected spinal injury the victim should ___
options: Be moved immediately|Be lifted by one person|Not be moved unless trained help is available and the scene is dangerous|Be given water immediately
answer: Not be moved unless trained help is available and the scene is dangerous
rubric: Moving a spinal injury patient incorrectly can cause paralysis — keep still until trained help arrives.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Asthma during physical activity is managed by ___
options: Ignoring symptoms|Ensuring the athlete has their reliever inhaler available and resting when symptoms appear|Forcing activity to continue|Drinking cold water
answer: Ensuring the athlete has their reliever inhaler available and resting when symptoms appear
rubric: Exercise-induced asthma requires reliever medication and rest — medical advice governs long-term management.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Dehydration during sports can be prevented by ___
options: Avoiding water|Drinking water before during and after activity|Eating only solid food|Wearing heavy clothing
answer: Drinking water before during and after activity
rubric: Regular fluid intake before, during and after exercise prevents dehydration and maintains performance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A concussion is a brain injury caused by ___
options: Eating too much|A blow to the head causing the brain to shake inside the skull|Lack of sleep|High blood pressure
answer: A blow to the head causing the brain to shake inside the skull
rubric: Concussion results from a head impact that shakes the brain — causing confusion, headache and nausea.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Road safety rules for cyclists include ___
options: Riding on the pavement|Cycling against traffic|Wearing a helmet using lights and cycling with traffic|Not stopping at red lights
answer: Wearing a helmet using lights and cycling with traffic
rubric: Cyclists should wear helmets, use lights at night and follow the same traffic direction as vehicles.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The emergency number for ambulance services in Nigeria is ___
rubric: 112 is Nigeria's national emergency number — for ambulance, fire and police services.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: An epileptic seizure should be managed by ___
options: Holding the person down firmly|Putting something in the person's mouth|Protecting the person from injury and placing them in the recovery position after the seizure|Giving water during the seizure
answer: Protecting the person from injury and placing them in the recovery position after the seizure
rubric: During a seizure: clear space around them; after it stops, place in the recovery position and seek medical help.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Heat stroke during outdoor sports requires ___
options: Keeping the person in the sun|Immediate cooling of the body and urgent medical attention|Feeding the person|Wrapping in warm clothing
answer: Immediate cooling of the body and urgent medical attention
rubric: Heat stroke is life-threatening — move to shade, cool the body with water and seek emergency help immediately.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of the following is an example of passive safety in sports?
options: Wearing shin guards|Following rules|Using protective padding on goalposts|Warming up
rubric: Passive safety measures protect players without active participation — padded posts, soft flooring.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Drug abuse in sports (doping) refers to ___
options: Taking prescribed medication|Using banned performance-enhancing substances to gain an unfair advantage|Drinking water during competition|Wearing performance clothing
answer: Using banned performance-enhancing substances to gain an unfair advantage
rubric: Doping is using prohibited substances or methods to enhance athletic performance — it is banned by WADA.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Anabolic steroids are abused in sport to ___
options: Improve reaction time|Increase muscle mass and strength|Improve cardiovascular fitness|Reduce body fat only
rubric: Anabolic steroids mimic testosterone — illegally used to build muscle and strength.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency) is responsible for ___
options: Coaching athletes|Organising the Olympics|Setting the list of banned substances and promoting dope-free sport|Awarding medals
answer: Setting the list of banned substances and promoting dope-free sport
rubric: WADA maintains the Prohibited List and coordinates anti-doping efforts globally.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Alcohol consumption affects sports performance by ___
options: Improving reaction time|Reducing coordination balance and judgement|Making athletes stronger|Improving endurance
rubric: Alcohol impairs the central nervous system — slowing reaction time and reducing coordination.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Cigarette smoking harms athletes because it ___
options: Builds muscles|Reduces lung capacity and cardiovascular fitness — carbon monoxide replaces oxygen in blood|Has no effect on performance|Improves breathing
answer: Reduces lung capacity and cardiovascular fitness — carbon monoxide replaces oxygen in blood
rubric: Smoking reduces oxygen delivery to muscles — severely affecting endurance and overall fitness.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Marijuana use is prohibited in sport because it ___
options: Is legal everywhere|Alters perception and can pose a safety risk in certain sports|Improves strength|Has no performance effect
answer: Alters perception and can pose a safety risk in certain sports
rubric: Cannabis alters coordination, reaction time and judgement — banned in competition by WADA.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Peer pressure in drug use means ___
options: Personal choice to use drugs|Being influenced by friends or a group to try drugs|A doctor's prescription|Parental advice
answer: Being influenced by friends or a group to try drugs
rubric: Peer pressure is social pressure from friends or peers encouraging someone to use drugs.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The safest response to peer pressure to take drugs is to ___
options: Always comply|Ignore the danger|Confidently refuse and walk away|Try once to see the effect
rubric: A firm 'no' and walking away from the situation is the most effective response to drug peer pressure.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Heroin and cocaine are examples of ___
options: Legal performance enhancers|Hard (narcotic) drugs that are highly addictive and dangerous|Vitamin supplements|Natural herbs
answer: Hard (narcotic) drugs that are highly addictive and dangerous
rubric: Heroin (opioid) and cocaine (stimulant) are hard drugs — highly addictive and illegal.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Drug tolerance means ___
options: Disliking a drug|Needing increasingly larger doses to achieve the same effect|Immunity to a drug|A doctor's approval
answer: Needing increasingly larger doses to achieve the same effect
rubric: Tolerance is when the body adapts to a drug — requiring more to get the same effect.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Withdrawal symptoms occur when ___
options: A person takes too much of a drug|A physically dependent person stops using a drug abruptly|Someone tries a new sport|A person refuses medication
answer: A physically dependent person stops using a drug abruptly
rubric: Withdrawal is the physical and psychological reaction when an addicted person stops or reduces drug use.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The NDLEA in Nigeria is responsible for ___
options: Education funding|Investigating and prosecuting drug trafficking and abuse|Organising elections|Banking regulation
answer: Investigating and prosecuting drug trafficking and abuse
rubric: The NDLEA (National Drug Law Enforcement Agency) combats drug trafficking and addiction in Nigeria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Inhalant abuse (sniffing glue or fuel) can cause ___
options: Better concentration|Immediate death sudden sniffing death syndrome and brain damage|Improved sports performance|Weight loss only
answer: Immediate death sudden sniffing death syndrome and brain damage
rubric: Inhalant abuse causes serious risks — sudden cardiac death, brain damage and organ failure.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of these is a short-term effect of alcohol?
options: Long-term liver damage|Impaired judgement slurred speech and loss of coordination|Lung cancer|Heart disease
answer: Impaired judgement slurred speech and loss of coordination
rubric: Short-term alcohol effects include reduced inhibition, impaired coordination and slurred speech.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Caffeine in small quantities is found in ___
options: Only medications|Coffee tea energy drinks and some soft drinks|Vegetables|Plain water
answer: Coffee tea energy drinks and some soft drinks
rubric: Caffeine is a mild stimulant present in coffee, tea, cocoa and many energy/carbonated drinks.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Prescription drug abuse refers to ___
options: Taking medicine as a doctor prescribes|Using prescription-only drugs without a prescription or in higher doses than prescribed|Refusing medicine|Getting a second opinion
answer: Using prescription-only drugs without a prescription or in higher doses than prescribed
rubric: Prescription drug abuse includes using controlled medicines recreationally or in excess of prescribed doses.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Long-term alcohol abuse can damage the ___
options: Kidneys only|Lungs|Liver causing cirrhosis|Bones only
rubric: Chronic alcohol abuse leads to liver cirrhosis — irreversible scarring of the liver.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A blood doping test in sport checks for ___
options: Alcohol|EPO (erythropoietin) and other substances that artificially boost red blood cell count|Vitamins|Dehydration
answer: EPO (erythropoietin) and other substances that artificially boost red blood cell count
rubric: Blood doping tests detect EPO, blood transfusions and other methods of illegally boosting oxygen delivery.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Rehabilitation from drug addiction involves ___
options: Immediate cold-turkey only|Counselling medical detoxification support groups and lifestyle change|Using other addictive drugs|Isolation from all people
answer: Counselling medical detoxification support groups and lifestyle change
rubric: Effective addiction treatment combines medical detox, psychological support and social reintegration.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Why is drug abuse particularly harmful to young athletes?
options: It makes them faster initially|Drugs during adolescence can permanently disrupt growth hormones brain development and health|It costs too much|Coaches dislike it
answer: Drugs during adolescence can permanently disrupt growth hormones brain development and health
rubric: Drug abuse during adolescence can permanently damage the developing brain and hormonal system.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Environmental health focuses on ___
options: Indoor fitness only|How the physical and social environment affects people's health|Business activities|Government policies only
answer: How the physical and social environment affects people's health
rubric: Environmental health examines the relationship between environmental conditions and human health.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Air pollution can cause ___
options: Improved lung function|Respiratory diseases such as asthma and bronchitis|Strong bones|Better cardiovascular fitness
answer: Respiratory diseases such as asthma and bronchitis
rubric: Air pollutants damage the respiratory system — worsening asthma, bronchitis and lung function.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Noise pollution in sports facilities can be reduced by ___
options: Increasing stadium size|Using sound-absorbing materials and crowd management|Banning all crowds|Playing without music
answer: Using sound-absorbing materials and crowd management
rubric: Acoustic design and crowd management reduce harmful noise levels in sports venues.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Proper waste disposal prevents disease by ___
options: Making the environment look clean only|Eliminating breeding sites for disease-carrying insects and preventing water/food contamination|Improving the weather|Reducing noise
answer: Eliminating breeding sites for disease-carrying insects and preventing water/food contamination
rubric: Proper waste management removes mosquito and fly breeding grounds and prevents waterborne disease.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Recycling materials such as paper and plastic helps by ___
options: Increasing waste|Conserving natural resources and reducing pollution from manufacturing|Raising product costs|Polluting water
answer: Conserving natural resources and reducing pollution from manufacturing
rubric: Recycling reduces raw material extraction, energy use and pollution from new production.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A healthy school environment should have ___
options: Overcrowded classrooms with no ventilation|Clean water proper sanitation adequate lighting and safe play areas|No gardens|Poor waste disposal
answer: Clean water proper sanitation adequate lighting and safe play areas
rubric: A healthy school environment provides safe, clean conditions conducive to learning and wellbeing.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Lead poisoning from old paint or petrol affects mainly ___
options: The stomach|The liver only|The brain and nervous system — especially in children|The lungs only
answer: The brain and nervous system — especially in children
rubric: Lead is a neurotoxin — children are particularly vulnerable to brain damage from lead exposure.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Potable water is ___
options: Water used for irrigation|Water safe for human consumption (drinking and cooking)|Dirty river water|Salty sea water
answer: Water safe for human consumption (drinking and cooking)
rubric: Potable water meets safety standards for drinking — free from harmful pathogens and chemicals.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The correct disposal of syringes and medical waste is important to prevent ___
options: Noise|Needle-stick injuries and spread of blood-borne infections like HIV and hepatitis|Littering only|Food poisoning
answer: Needle-stick injuries and spread of blood-borne infections like HIV and hepatitis
rubric: Medical sharp waste disposal in puncture-proof containers prevents accidental infections.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of the following is a vector of malaria?
options: Housefly|Cockroach|Female Anopheles mosquito|Rat
rubric: The female Anopheles mosquito is the vector that transmits malaria parasites to humans.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Burning of household waste contributes to ___
options: Clean air|Water purification|Air pollution through releasing toxic smoke and particulates|Soil fertility
answer: Air pollution through releasing toxic smoke and particulates
rubric: Open burning of waste releases harmful gases (dioxins, carbon monoxide) and particulates.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Overcrowding in urban areas leads to ___
options: Better health outcomes|Easier disease transmission and poor sanitation|Cleaner environments|More physical space
answer: Easier disease transmission and poor sanitation
rubric: Overcrowding facilitates the spread of communicable diseases and strains sanitation infrastructure.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The concept of 'One Health' recognises that ___
options: Only human health matters|Animal environment and human health are interconnected|Animals have no impact on humans|Only plants affect health
answer: Animal environment and human health are interconnected
rubric: One Health is an approach recognising that human, animal and environmental health are interdependent.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Flooding in Nigerian cities is worsened by ___
options: Too much sun|Blocking drainage channels with solid waste and building on floodplains|Too many trees|Cold weather
answer: Blocking drainage channels with solid waste and building on floodplains
rubric: Solid waste blocking drains and development on floodplains amplify urban flooding in Nigerian cities.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Safe food handling includes all of the following EXCEPT ___
options: Washing hands before cooking|Cooking meat to the correct internal temperature|Storing raw meat above cooked food in the fridge|Keeping food covered
answer: Storing raw meat above cooked food in the fridge
rubric: Raw meat should always be stored BELOW cooked food to prevent drip contamination.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Chlorination of water is a method of ___
options: Filtering sediment|Softening hard water|Killing pathogens to make water safe for drinking|Adding minerals
answer: Killing pathogens to make water safe for drinking
rubric: Chlorine disinfects water by killing bacteria, viruses and protozoa.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The WHO defines health as ___
options: Absence of disease|A state of complete physical mental and social wellbeing — not merely the absence of disease|Being able to work|Having no infection
answer: A state of complete physical mental and social wellbeing — not merely the absence of disease
rubric: WHO's 1946 definition: health is complete physical, mental and social wellbeing — beyond absence of disease.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Indoor air pollution in Nigerian homes is mainly caused by ___
options: Air conditioning|Using well-ventilated gas stoves|Cooking with biomass fuels (firewood charcoal) in poorly ventilated spaces|Electric lighting
answer: Cooking with biomass fuels (firewood charcoal) in poorly ventilated spaces
rubric: Biomass cooking fires produce smoke and particulates — a major source of indoor air pollution in Nigeria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to health include ___
options: Only SDG 1|SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing) and SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation)|Only education goals|Only economic goals
answer: SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing) and SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation)
rubric: SDG 3 targets good health for all; SDG 6 targets universal access to safe water and sanitation.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Ozone layer depletion increases exposure to ___
options: Visible light|Infrared radiation|Ultraviolet (UV) radiation|Sound waves
rubric: The ozone layer blocks harmful UV radiation — its depletion increases skin cancer and eye damage risk.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Abstinence as a method of preventing STIs and pregnancy means ___
options: Using contraceptives|Completely refraining from sexual activity|Delaying marriage|Using only natural methods
rubric: Abstinence — not engaging in sex — is 100% effective at preventing STIs and pregnancy.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The menstrual cycle in females typically lasts about ___
options: 7 days|14 days|28 days|60 days
rubric: The average menstrual cycle is approximately 28 days — though normal ranges from 21–35 days.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Fertilisation in human reproduction occurs when ___
options: A sperm meets an egg in the fallopian tube|A baby is born|The egg reaches the uterus|Ovulation happens
answer: A sperm meets an egg in the fallopian tube
rubric: Fertilisation (conception) occurs when a sperm cell fuses with an ovum in the fallopian tube.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Teen pregnancy is associated with all of the following EXCEPT ___
options: School dropout|Health risks for the mother|Improved academic performance|Economic hardship
rubric: Teen pregnancy typically leads to school dropout, not improved academic performance.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Sexual harassment is ___
options: A form of compliment|Any unwanted sexual attention conduct or advances|Normal social interaction|Only physical contact
answer: Any unwanted sexual attention conduct or advances
rubric: Sexual harassment includes unwanted sexual comments, gestures, touching or advances — it is unacceptable.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A victim of sexual abuse should ___
options: Keep it secret|Blame themselves|Report the abuse to a trusted adult or authority|Pretend it did not happen
answer: Report the abuse to a trusted adult or authority
rubric: Victims should report abuse to a trusted adult, teacher or authority — they are not at fault.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Gender refers to ___
options: Only biological sex|The social and cultural roles and expectations associated with being male or female|Physical strength|Age group
answer: The social and cultural roles and expectations associated with being male or female
rubric: Gender is socially constructed — the roles, behaviours and attributes a society considers appropriate for men/women.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Contraception is used to ___
options: Cure STIs|Prevent unwanted pregnancy|Increase fertility|Treat hormonal disorders
rubric: Contraception (birth control) prevents pregnancy through various methods — condoms also prevent STIs.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A healthy relationship is characterised by ___
options: Control and jealousy|Mutual respect trust communication and equality|One partner making all decisions|Fear and pressure
answer: Mutual respect trust communication and equality
rubric: Healthy relationships are built on respect, trust, open communication and mutual support.
