subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Puberty changes in girls include all of the following EXCEPT ___
options: Development of breasts|Widening of hips|Growth of facial hair|Onset of menstruation
rubric: Facial hair growth is a male puberty change — not a typical female characteristic.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Child marriage is harmful because it ___
options: Promotes independence|Deprives children of education health and childhood — and increases maternal mortality|Supports tradition|Has no health effects
answer: Deprives children of education health and childhood — and increases maternal mortality
rubric: Child marriage harms girls physically and psychologically — it is associated with high maternal and infant mortality.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Ovulation occurs when ___
options: A baby is born|Fertilisation happens|A mature egg is released from the ovary|Menstruation begins
answer: A mature egg is released from the ovary
rubric: Ovulation is the release of a mature egg from the ovarian follicle — mid-cycle, around day 14.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The age of consent in most Nigerian contexts under the Child Rights Act is ___
rubric: The Child Rights Act sets the age of consent and legal adulthood at 18 in Nigeria.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Self-esteem refers to ___
options: How fast a person runs|The value and respect a person has for themselves|A person's weight|Academic performance only
answer: The value and respect a person has for themselves
rubric: Self-esteem is an individual's overall subjective sense of personal worth and value.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Gender-based violence (GBV) includes ___
options: Academic competitions|Physical emotional and sexual violence directed at someone because of their gender|Sports rivalry|Government policy
answer: Physical emotional and sexual violence directed at someone because of their gender
rubric: GBV is violence targeting people because of their gender — predominantly affecting women and girls.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: A condom is effective at preventing ___
options: All diseases|Both pregnancy and STIs including HIV when used consistently and correctly|Only pregnancy|Only HIV
answer: Both pregnancy and STIs including HIV when used consistently and correctly
rubric: When used correctly and consistently, condoms significantly reduce the risk of both pregnancy and STIs.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Responsible parenthood means ___
options: Having as many children as possible|Providing adequate care love education and support for one's children|Only the mother cares for children|Sending children away to relatives
answer: Providing adequate care love education and support for one's children
rubric: Responsible parents meet children's physical, emotional, educational and spiritual needs.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Coercion in a relationship means ___
options: Mutual agreement|Forcing or pressuring someone to do something against their will|Honest communication|Respectful disagreement
answer: Forcing or pressuring someone to do something against their will
rubric: Coercion is using threats, manipulation or force to make someone do what they otherwise wouldn't.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Body autonomy means ___
options: Others can touch your body without permission|You have the right to decide what happens to your own body|Physical strength|Good posture
answer: You have the right to decide what happens to your own body
rubric: Body autonomy is every person's right to make decisions about their own body — including who touches it.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Nocturnal emission (wet dream) in adolescent boys is ___
options: A sign of illness|An abnormal development|A normal part of puberty as the reproductive system matures|Caused by diet
answer: A normal part of puberty as the reproductive system matures
rubric: Nocturnal emissions are a normal physiological occurrence during male puberty — not a sign of disorder.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The best way to handle unwanted romantic advances from a fellow student is to ___
options: Ignore it forever|Respond aggressively|Clearly and calmly decline and report to a teacher or counsellor if it persists|Avoid school
answer: Clearly and calmly decline and report to a teacher or counsellor if it persists
rubric: Assertively declining and, if necessary, reporting to a trusted adult is the appropriate response.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Emotional abuse in a relationship includes ___
options: Physical hitting|Constant criticism humiliation and isolation that damages self-esteem|Shared decision-making|Financial support
answer: Constant criticism humiliation and isolation that damages self-esteem
rubric: Emotional abuse uses words and behaviour to control, belittle and isolate — causing lasting psychological harm.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Which of these organisations supports victims of domestic violence in Nigeria?
options: NAFDAC|INEC|WARDC and FIDA (women and legal rights organisations)|NDLEA only
answer: WARDC and FIDA (women and legal rights organisations)
rubric: Women's rights organisations like WARDC and FIDA provide legal aid and support to GBV victims.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: The recommended age for a first cervical cancer (Pap smear) screening is ___
options: 10|15|21 (or within 3 years of becoming sexually active)|35
answer: 21 (or within 3 years of becoming sexually active)
rubric: Health guidelines recommend first cervical cancer screening at 21 or within 3 years of sexual activity.

subject: Physical & Health Education
stem: Good communication with parents about puberty changes helps adolescents to ___
options: Avoid growing up|Understand changes seek support and make healthy decisions|Hide personal development|Stay uninformed
answer: Understand changes seek support and make healthy decisions
rubric: Open parent–child communication about puberty supports healthy development and decision-making.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A computer is best defined as ___
options: A television set|An electronic device that accepts processes stores and outputs data|A printing machine|A telephone
answer: An electronic device that accepts processes stores and outputs data
rubric: A computer is an electronic device that processes data according to instructions and produces output.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The four basic operations of a computer system are ___
options: Type save print delete|Input Process Store Output|On Off Restart Sleep|Read Write Execute Close
rubric: The information processing cycle: Input → Process → Store → Output.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The first generation of computers used ___
options: Transistors|Integrated circuits|Vacuum tubes|Microprocessors
rubric: First-generation computers (1940s–1950s) used vacuum tubes — they were large, slow and generated great heat.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A laptop computer differs from a desktop mainly because it ___
options: Has a slower processor|Is portable and runs on battery power|Cannot connect to the internet|Has no keyboard
answer: Is portable and runs on battery power
rubric: Laptops are portable, battery-powered computers — designed for mobile use.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: ICT stands for ___
options: International Computer Technology|Information and Communication Technology|Integrated Circuit Transistor|Internet Computer Terminal
rubric: ICT = Information and Communication Technology — encompassing computers, networks and digital communication.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The Central Processing Unit (CPU) is called the brain of the computer because it ___
options: Stores all data permanently|Controls and executes all operations and instructions|Connects to the internet|Displays images
answer: Controls and executes all operations and instructions
rubric: The CPU fetches, decodes and executes instructions — it is the core processing unit of a computer.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Data is best described as ___
options: Processed information|Raw unorganised facts and figures that have not yet been processed|A computer program|The internet
answer: Raw unorganised facts and figures that have not yet been processed
rubric: Data is raw input — numbers, text, images. Information is data that has been processed into meaning.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Information is data that has been ___
options: Deleted|Processed and given meaning|Printed|Typed
rubric: Information = processed data with context and meaning — useful for decision-making.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A tablet computer is an example of a ___
options: Supercomputer|Mainframe|Mobile handheld computing device|Server
rubric: Tablets (e.g. iPad, Android tablets) are portable handheld computers with touchscreens.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is NOT a use of computers in schools?
options: Record keeping|Online learning|Storing student data|Growing crops
rubric: Computers are used in schools for records, e-learning and data — not for agriculture.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The binary number system used by computers has a base of ___
rubric: Computers use binary (base-2) — only digits 0 and 1 — because electronic circuits have two states: on/off.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A bit is ___
options: 8 bytes|The smallest unit of digital data (a 0 or 1)|A type of computer virus|A type of printer
answer: The smallest unit of digital data (a 0 or 1)
rubric: A bit (binary digit) is the most basic unit of data — a single 0 or 1.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: One byte equals ___
options: 4 bits|16 bits|2 bits|8 bits
rubric: 1 byte = 8 bits — the standard unit for representing a single character in computers.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: 1 Gigabyte (GB) is approximately equal to ___
options: 1,000 bytes|1,000 kilobytes|1,000 megabytes (1,024 MB precisely)|1,000 terabytes
rubric: 1 GB = 1,024 MB (binary) or approximately 1,000 MB — used for storage and memory sizes.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is an advantage of using computers?
options: They never break down|They process large amounts of data quickly and accurately|They think for themselves|They replace all human work
answer: They process large amounts of data quickly and accurately
rubric: Computers excel at fast, accurate, repetitive processing of large data volumes.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A supercomputer is used for ___
options: Word processing only|Complex scientific and mathematical calculations requiring extreme speed|Basic internet browsing|Simple games
answer: Complex scientific and mathematical calculations requiring extreme speed
rubric: Supercomputers (e.g. weather forecasting, nuclear simulation) perform trillions of calculations per second.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The generation of computers that use microprocessors is the ___
options: First|Second|Third|Fourth
rubric: Fourth-generation computers (1971–present) use microprocessors — entire CPUs on a single chip.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following correctly lists computer sizes from smallest to largest?
options: Desktop Laptop Server Supercomputer|Smartphone Tablet Laptop Desktop Supercomputer|Supercomputer Desktop Laptop Tablet|Server Desktop Laptop Smartphone
rubric: From smallest to largest: Smartphone → Tablet → Laptop → Desktop → Server → Supercomputer.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Computers are used in hospitals mainly for ___
options: Cooking food|Managing patient records running diagnostic equipment and research|Physical exercise|Transporting patients
answer: Managing patient records running diagnostic equipment and research
rubric: Hospitals use computers for electronic health records, diagnostics, imaging and medical research.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A computer network is ___
options: A single computer with many programs|Two or more computers connected to share resources and communicate|A type of software|A printer
answer: Two or more computers connected to share resources and communicate
rubric: A network connects computers to share data, devices and internet access.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The term 'booting' a computer means ___
options: Kicking the computer|Starting the computer and loading the operating system|Shutting it down|Installing software
answer: Starting the computer and loading the operating system
rubric: Booting is the startup process where the BIOS/UEFI loads the OS into RAM.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Computer hardware refers to ___
options: Programs and applications|The physical components of a computer that can be touched|Only the monitor|Data stored on disk
answer: The physical components of a computer that can be touched
rubric: Hardware includes all physical parts: CPU, RAM, keyboard, mouse, monitor, storage.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Computer software refers to ___
options: Physical computer parts|Programs and instructions that tell the hardware what to do|Cables and connectors|Computer furniture
answer: Programs and instructions that tell the hardware what to do
rubric: Software is the set of programs, instructions and data that operate on hardware.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The acronym GUI stands for ___
options: General User Input|Graphical User Interface|General Utility Installation|Graphics Unit Integration
rubric: A GUI uses icons, windows and menus — making computers accessible without knowing commands.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is an example of a smart device?
options: A wooden ruler|A blackboard|A smartphone with internet access|A printed book
rubric: Smart devices (smartphones, smart TVs) connect to the internet and run applications.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is an INPUT device?
options: Monitor|Printer|Keyboard|Speaker
rubric: Input devices send data INTO the computer — keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is an OUTPUT device?
options: Mouse|Keyboard|Scanner|Printer
rubric: Output devices receive data FROM the computer — monitor, printer, speaker, projector.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: RAM (Random Access Memory) is ___
options: Permanent storage for files|Temporary memory used by the CPU to store running programs and data|A type of hard drive|A graphics card
answer: Temporary memory used by the CPU to store running programs and data
rubric: RAM is volatile (temporary) memory — it stores data currently in use and clears on shutdown.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: ROM (Read-Only Memory) is ___
options: Memory that can be freely written and deleted|Permanent memory that stores the computer's startup instructions (BIOS)|The same as RAM|A storage device
answer: Permanent memory that stores the computer's startup instructions (BIOS)
rubric: ROM is non-volatile — it stores firmware like BIOS that runs when the computer boots.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A hard disk drive (HDD) is used for ___
options: Processing data|Temporary storage|Permanent mass storage of data and programs|Displaying images
answer: Permanent mass storage of data and programs
rubric: HDDs use magnetic platters to store operating systems, applications and data permanently.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The monitor is an example of a ___
options: Storage device|Processing device|Input device|Output device
rubric: The monitor displays the computer's visual output — it is an output device.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A scanner is used to ___
options: Print documents|Convert physical documents and images into digital format|Store data|Connect to the internet
answer: Convert physical documents and images into digital format
rubric: A scanner digitises physical documents, photos and objects into digital files.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The mouse controls the ___
options: Keyboard|Printer|Cursor (pointer) on the screen|Internet connection
rubric: The mouse moves the on-screen cursor and is used to click, drag and interact with a GUI.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A USB flash drive (pen drive/thumb drive) is ___
options: An input device only|A portable storage device that plugs into a USB port|An output device only|A processing unit
answer: A portable storage device that plugs into a USB port
rubric: USB flash drives are portable solid-state storage devices — small and removable.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The CPU speed is measured in ___
options: Gigabytes (GB)|Megapixels|Gigahertz (GHz)|Decibels
rubric: CPU speed (clock rate) is measured in Hertz — modern processors run at GHz (billions of cycles/second).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A projector is an example of a ___
options: Input device|Storage device|Output device|Processing unit
rubric: A projector displays computer output on a screen or wall — it is an output device.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A webcam is used to ___
options: Print images|Capture live video and images for input into a computer|Store large files|Connect to printers
answer: Capture live video and images for input into a computer
rubric: A webcam is a digital camera that inputs live video into the computer — used for video calls.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The motherboard of a computer ___
options: Stores the operating system|Is the main circuit board connecting all components|Only manages the hard drive|Produces sound
answer: Is the main circuit board connecting all components
rubric: The motherboard is the primary PCB — it connects and allows communication between CPU, RAM and peripherals.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A touchscreen is a device that is both ___
options: Input and storage|Output and storage|Input and output simultaneously|Processing and storage
rubric: A touchscreen displays visual output AND accepts touch input — it is both input and output.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which storage medium holds the MOST data?
options: Floppy disk|CD-ROM|USB flash drive (16 GB)|External hard drive (1 TB)
rubric: A 1 TB external HDD holds far more than CDs (~700 MB), floppies (~1.44 MB) or typical flash drives.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A microphone is an example of a ___
options: Processing device|Output device|Storage device|Input device
rubric: A microphone captures sound and converts it to digital input for the computer.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Pixels on a monitor refer to ___
options: The screen's brightness|Tiny dots that make up the screen image — more pixels means higher resolution|The screen's weight|Connection ports
answer: Tiny dots that make up the screen image — more pixels means higher resolution
rubric: Pixels (picture elements) are the smallest display units — resolution is measured in pixels (e.g. 1920×1080).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A Solid State Drive (SSD) is faster than a hard disk drive (HDD) because ___
options: It is bigger|It uses magnetic disks|It has no moving parts — using flash memory chips|It needs no power
answer: It has no moving parts — using flash memory chips
rubric: SSDs use NAND flash memory — no mechanical parts mean faster access speeds and greater durability.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) is used to ___
options: Speed up the CPU|Provide battery backup power to protect against power cuts|Cool the computer|Connect to Wi-Fi
answer: Provide battery backup power to protect against power cuts
rubric: A UPS supplies emergency power — protecting computers from sudden power loss and data corruption.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A graphics card (GPU) is responsible for ___
options: Processing email|Managing internet connections|Rendering images and video to the monitor|Storing files
answer: Rendering images and video to the monitor
rubric: The GPU processes and renders graphics — essential for gaming, video editing and 3D applications.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: System software refers to ___
options: Games and office tools|Software that manages the computer hardware and provides a platform for applications — e.g. the operating system|Only antivirus programs|Spreadsheet programs
answer: Software that manages the computer hardware and provides a platform for applications — e.g. the operating system
rubric: System software (OS, device drivers, utilities) manages hardware and supports application software.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Application software is designed to ___
options: Manage computer hardware|Help users perform specific tasks like writing documents or editing photos|Run the computer's startup|Manage memory only
answer: Help users perform specific tasks like writing documents or editing photos
rubric: Application software (word processors, browsers, games) runs on top of the OS for end-user tasks.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Microsoft Word is an example of ___
options: System software|A utility program|An application software (word processor)|An operating system
rubric: Microsoft Word is application software — a word processor for creating and editing text documents.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Freeware software is ___
options: Software that must be paid for|Software that is free to use and distribute|Only system software|Illegal software
answer: Software that is free to use and distribute
rubric: Freeware is software distributed at no cost — users may use and share it freely.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Open-source software is software whose ___
options: Source code is kept secret|Source code is publicly available and may be modified by users|Source is always free|Licence is always expensive
answer: Source code is publicly available and may be modified by users
rubric: Open-source software (e.g. Linux, Firefox) shares its source code — allowing community development.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A software license gives the user ___
options: Ownership of the software|Permission to use the software under specific conditions set by the developer|The right to sell the software|Access to the source code
answer: Permission to use the software under specific conditions set by the developer
rubric: A software licence is a legal agreement defining how software may be used, copied and distributed.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A computer virus is a type of ___
options: Hardware failure|Malicious software (malware) that replicates and damages files or systems|Network cable|Printer error
answer: Malicious software (malware) that replicates and damages files or systems
rubric: A computer virus is malware that attaches to programs, replicates and damages the system.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Antivirus software is used to ___
options: Speed up the CPU|Detect and remove malware from a computer|Create documents|Browse the internet
answer: Detect and remove malware from a computer
rubric: Antivirus software scans for, detects and removes malicious programs (viruses, spyware, etc.).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of these is an example of presentation software?
options: Microsoft Word|Microsoft Excel|Microsoft PowerPoint|Google Chrome
rubric: Microsoft PowerPoint is presentation software — used to create slideshows.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A web browser is used to ___
options: Write documents|Access and navigate the World Wide Web|Create spreadsheets|Edit photos
answer: Access and navigate the World Wide Web
rubric: A web browser (Chrome, Firefox, Edge) is used to retrieve and display web pages.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Installing a software update is important because updates ___
options: Make the computer slower|Use more storage|Fix bugs improve features and patch security vulnerabilities|Change the hardware
answer: Fix bugs improve features and patch security vulnerabilities
rubric: Software updates address known bugs, add features and close security holes exploited by hackers.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A file extension tells you ___
options: The file's size|The type and format of the file (e.g. .docx is a Word document)|The file's creation date|The file's owner
answer: The type and format of the file (e.g. .docx is a Word document)
rubric: File extensions (.pdf, .jpg, .mp3) indicate the file type and which program opens it.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: PDF stands for ___
options: Portable Document Format|Personal Data File|Printed Digital Form|Primary Data Format
rubric: PDF is a file format that preserves document formatting across different platforms and devices.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Compressing a file means ___
options: Deleting it|Reducing its size to save storage space|Making it larger|Encrypting it
answer: Reducing its size to save storage space
rubric: File compression (zip, rar) reduces file size — useful for storage and faster file transfer.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A utility program is a type of software that ___
options: Creates documents|Manages and maintains the computer system (e.g. disk cleaner antivirus)|Plays games|Browses the web
answer: Manages and maintains the computer system (e.g. disk cleaner antivirus)
rubric: Utility programs (disk cleaner, defragmenter, antivirus) perform system maintenance tasks.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Shareware differs from freeware because shareware ___
options: Is completely free|Is illegal|Allows a trial period but requires payment for continued use|Has no limitations
answer: Allows a trial period but requires payment for continued use
rubric: Shareware is try-before-you-buy — a limited trial version that must be purchased for full features.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is a mobile operating system?
options: Microsoft Word|Windows 11|Android|PowerPoint
rubric: Android (Google) is a mobile OS for smartphones and tablets — iOS (Apple) is another example.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Software piracy means ___
options: Selling pirate-themed games|Using copying or distributing software illegally without a valid licence|Writing bad software|Deleting software
answer: Using copying or distributing software illegally without a valid licence
rubric: Software piracy is the unauthorised copying, distribution or use of copyrighted software.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The recycle bin on a Windows computer ___
options: Permanently deletes files immediately|Temporarily stores deleted files allowing recovery before final deletion|Stores downloaded files|Organises documents
answer: Temporarily stores deleted files allowing recovery before final deletion
rubric: The Recycle Bin holds deleted files — they can be restored until the bin is emptied.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A backup is ___
options: Deleting old files|A copy of important data stored separately in case the original is lost or damaged|An update|An antivirus scan
answer: A copy of important data stored separately in case the original is lost or damaged
rubric: Regular backups protect against data loss from hardware failure, theft, virus or accidents.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An operating system (OS) is ___
options: A word processing program|The software that manages computer hardware and provides services for all other software|A spreadsheet|A browser
answer: The software that manages computer hardware and provides services for all other software
rubric: The OS (Windows, macOS, Linux) is the master control program managing all computer resources.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is a popular desktop operating system?
options: Android|iOS|Microsoft Windows|Snapchat
rubric: Windows (Microsoft) is the most widely used desktop OS globally.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The desktop in Windows is ___
options: A physical desk|The main screen displayed after logging in where icons shortcuts and the taskbar appear|A type of folder|A computer program
answer: The main screen displayed after logging in where icons shortcuts and the taskbar appear
rubric: The Windows desktop is the home screen — showing icons, the taskbar and the start menu.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A folder (directory) on a computer is used to ___
options: Run programs|Organise and store files|Connect to the internet|Display images
rubric: Folders are virtual containers that organise files — like a filing cabinet for digital documents.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: To copy a file in Windows you can use the keyboard shortcut ___
options: Ctrl+X|Ctrl+V|Ctrl+C|Ctrl+Z
rubric: Ctrl+C copies selected content or files to the clipboard in Windows.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: To paste a copied file or text in Windows you press ___
options: Ctrl+C|Ctrl+P|Ctrl+V|Ctrl+S
rubric: Ctrl+V pastes clipboard content at the cursor location or selected folder.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The taskbar in Windows usually contains ___
options: Only the date|The Start menu open applications and the system tray with clock and notifications|Only the desktop|Games
answer: The Start menu open applications and the system tray with clock and notifications
rubric: The Windows taskbar provides quick access to the Start menu, running apps and system notifications.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Ctrl+Z in most applications is the shortcut for ___
options: Save|Copy|Paste|Undo
rubric: Ctrl+Z undoes the last action — a critical keyboard shortcut across most applications.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Multi-tasking in computing means ___
options: A computer doing only one task|The OS running multiple applications or processes at the same time|A printer printing many pages|Using many keyboards
answer: The OS running multiple applications or processes at the same time
rubric: Modern OSes allow simultaneous execution of multiple programs through multi-tasking.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A file path describes ___
options: A file's size|The exact location of a file in the computer's folder structure|The file's content|The date a file was made
answer: The exact location of a file in the computer's folder structure
rubric: A file path (e.g. C:\Users\Documents\report.docx) shows the route from root to the file.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Ctrl+S is used to ___
options: Open a new file|Close a program|Save the current file|Search for a file
rubric: Ctrl+S is the universal keyboard shortcut to save the current file in most applications.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The Control Panel in Windows is used to ___
options: Write documents|Manage system settings — hardware software users and security|Browse the internet|Play music
answer: Manage system settings — hardware software users and security
rubric: The Control Panel provides a centralised interface for configuring Windows system settings.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Shutting down a computer properly is important because it ___
options: Saves electricity only|Ensures all files are saved changes are applied safely and hardware is powered off correctly|Makes the computer faster|Deletes temporary files only
answer: Ensures all files are saved changes are applied safely and hardware is powered off correctly
rubric: Proper shutdown completes processes, writes pending changes and prevents file corruption.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Pressing Delete on a selected file in Windows ___
options: Permanently deletes it immediately|Moves it to the Recycle Bin|Copies it|Renames it
answer: Moves it to the Recycle Bin
rubric: In Windows, pressing Delete moves a file to the Recycle Bin — not immediately permanent deletion.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A user account on a computer ___
options: Connects the computer to the internet|Identifies a person and controls their access rights and personalisation settings|Stores the OS|Runs the printer
answer: Identifies a person and controls their access rights and personalisation settings
rubric: User accounts give individual login credentials, customised settings and access permissions.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which Windows tool is used to search for files and folders?
options: Notepad|File Explorer (Windows Explorer)|Microsoft Word|Control Panel
rubric: File Explorer (or Windows Explorer) is Windows' file management tool for navigating and searching files.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The command prompt in Windows is a ___
options: Graphical interface|Text-based interface for entering operating system commands directly|Type of printer|Network tool only
answer: Text-based interface for entering operating system commands directly
rubric: The command prompt (cmd) allows users to type text commands to control the OS — a CLI interface.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Logging off a computer differs from shutting down because ___
options: They are the same|Logging off ends the user session but leaves the computer running|Logging off deletes files|Logging off turns off the monitor only
answer: Logging off ends the user session but leaves the computer running
rubric: Log off ends the current user's session (keeping the OS running); Shut Down powers the machine off.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A printer driver is ___
options: The person operating the printer|Software that allows the OS to communicate with the printer|A printer's power cable|A type of ink
answer: Software that allows the OS to communicate with the printer
rubric: Drivers are software bridges — a printer driver translates OS commands into signals the printer understands.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Hibernation on a laptop ___
options: Shuts down completely|Saves the current session state to disk and powers off — restoring everything on startup|Locks the screen|Closes all files
answer: Saves the current session state to disk and powers off — restoring everything on startup
rubric: Hibernate saves RAM to disk and powers off — on restart, all open applications and files are restored.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Word processing software is primarily used to ___
options: Edit photos|Create and edit text documents|Browse the internet|Manage finances
rubric: Word processors (MS Word, Google Docs) are used to create, format and edit text documents.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A cursor in a word processor is ___
options: A type of font|The blinking vertical line showing where typed text will appear|A menu bar|A save button
answer: The blinking vertical line showing where typed text will appear
rubric: The cursor (insertion point) indicates where the next character typed will be inserted.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Bold text is used in documents to ___
options: Make text smaller|Emphasise important words or headings by making them thicker and darker|Change the font colour|Underline text
answer: Emphasise important words or headings by making them thicker and darker
rubric: Bold formatting (Ctrl+B) makes text heavier — used for emphasis and headings.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The Find and Replace function in a word processor allows you to ___
options: Change the font|Search for a word and replace it with another throughout the document|Save a document|Print a document
answer: Search for a word and replace it with another throughout the document
rubric: Find & Replace (Ctrl+H) locates a specific word/phrase and replaces it — saving editing time.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Spell check in a word processor ___
options: Changes the font|Translates the document|Identifies misspelled words and suggests corrections|Formats the page
answer: Identifies misspelled words and suggests corrections
rubric: Spell check flags words not in the dictionary and suggests correct spellings.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Page orientation in a word processor can be set to ___
options: Colour or black and white|Portrait (vertical) or landscape (horizontal)|A4 or A3 only|Single or double sided
rubric: Page orientation: Portrait (tall, default) or Landscape (wide) — set in page layout settings.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which keyboard shortcut is used to print a document?
options: Ctrl+P|Ctrl+S|Ctrl+O|Ctrl+N
rubric: Ctrl+P opens the Print dialogue — the standard shortcut across most applications.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Indentation in a document refers to ___
options: The size of the font|Spacing between lines|The space between text and the page margin (pushing text inward)|The document header
answer: The space between text and the page margin (pushing text inward)
rubric: Indentation creates space between text and the margin — used for paragraphs and nested lists.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A header in a document appears ___
options: At the bottom of every page|Only on the last page|At the top of every page|In the middle of the document
answer: At the top of every page
rubric: A header is text at the top margin of every page — typically containing title, author or page number.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The font size in a document refers to ___
options: The weight of the letters|The height of the characters measured in points|The colour of the letters|The type of font
answer: The height of the characters measured in points
rubric: Font size is measured in points (pt) — 12pt is common for body text; 72pt ≈ 1 inch high.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Mail merge is a feature used to ___
options: Send emails|Create personalised letters for many recipients by merging a document with a data list|Merge two computers|Print in colour
answer: Create personalised letters for many recipients by merging a document with a data list
rubric: Mail merge inserts personalised data (names, addresses) from a database into a document template.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The default file extension for Microsoft Word 2016+ documents is ___
options: .doc|.pdf|.txt|.docx
rubric: Microsoft Word 2007 and later uses the .docx format (Office Open XML).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Text alignment in word processing includes all of the following EXCEPT ___
options: Left|Centre|Right|Diagonal
rubric: Text alignment options: Left, Centre, Right and Justify — there is no diagonal alignment.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The ruler in a word processor is used to ___
options: Measure paper physically|Set margins tabs and indents visually|Change the font|Save the document
answer: Set margins tabs and indents visually
rubric: The on-screen ruler lets you visually set page margins, tab stops and paragraph indents.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Superscript text appears ___
options: Below the normal line of text|Above the normal line of text in a smaller size|In bold|In italics
answer: Above the normal line of text in a smaller size
rubric: Superscript (e.g. x²) places text above the baseline — used for exponents and footnotes.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A table in a word processor is used to ___
options: Draw pictures|Organise information in rows and columns|Create charts|Write headings only
answer: Organise information in rows and columns
rubric: Tables organise data into rows and columns — useful for timetables, comparisons and lists.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Ctrl+A in a word processor ___
options: Saves the document|Adds a new page|Selects all text and objects in the document|Closes the document
answer: Selects all text and objects in the document
rubric: Ctrl+A selects all content — useful before formatting or deleting the entire document.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Word wrap means ___
options: Text falls off the screen|Text automatically moves to the next line when it reaches the margin — no manual Enter needed|Wrapping text around images only|Changing the margin
answer: Text automatically moves to the next line when it reaches the margin — no manual Enter needed
rubric: Word wrap automatically breaks lines at the margin — a fundamental word processing feature.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Formatting marks (non-printing characters) in a word processor show ___
options: Page borders|Hidden characters like spaces paragraph marks and tabs — useful for layout checking|Grammar errors|Spelling mistakes
answer: Hidden characters like spaces paragraph marks and tabs — useful for layout checking
rubric: Toggling formatting marks (¶) reveals spaces, tabs and paragraphs — helping with precise layout.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The word count feature in a word processor tells you ___
options: The number of pages|The number of words characters and paragraphs in a document|The number of fonts used|The date of creation
answer: The number of words characters and paragraphs in a document
rubric: Word Count shows total words, characters, paragraphs and pages — essential for essay requirements.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A spreadsheet is used mainly to ___
options: Write essays|Organise calculate and analyse numerical data in rows and columns|Browse the internet|Design posters
answer: Organise calculate and analyse numerical data in rows and columns
rubric: Spreadsheets (MS Excel, Google Sheets) organise data in grids — used for calculations and analysis.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: In a spreadsheet a cell is ___
options: The entire sheet|The intersection of a row and a column (e.g. cell A1 B3)|A chart|A formula
answer: The intersection of a row and a column (e.g. cell A1 B3)
rubric: A cell is the basic unit of a spreadsheet — identified by its column letter and row number (e.g. B3).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: In Excel the formula =SUM(A1:A5) adds ___
options: Only cells A1 and A5|All values from cell A1 to A5 inclusive|The largest value|Only cell A5
answer: All values from cell A1 to A5 inclusive
rubric: =SUM(A1:A5) adds A1+A2+A3+A4+A5 — the colon means a range.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: All formulas in a spreadsheet begin with ___
options: A number|A letter|An equals sign (=)|A hash (#)
rubric: In Excel and most spreadsheets, formulas always start with = to tell the program to calculate.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A chart in a spreadsheet is used to ___
options: Enter text|Visually represent data in graphical form (bar pie line chart etc.)|Connect to the internet|Print only
answer: Visually represent data in graphical form (bar pie line chart etc.)
rubric: Charts convert spreadsheet data into visual graphs — making trends and comparisons easy to see.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which formula calculates the average of cells B1 to B10 in Excel?
options: =SUM(B1:B10)|=MAX(B1:B10)|=AVERAGE(B1:B10)|=COUNT(B1:B10)
rubric: The AVERAGE function returns the arithmetic mean of a range — =AVERAGE(B1:B10) averages 10 cells.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Sorting data in a spreadsheet means ___
options: Deleting unwanted rows|Arranging data in ascending or descending order|Adding formulas|Merging cells
answer: Arranging data in ascending or descending order
rubric: Sort arranges records alphabetically (A–Z or Z–A) or numerically (low–high or high–low).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A database is best described as ___
options: A single spreadsheet|An organised collection of structured data that can be easily accessed managed and updated|A word processing document|A web page
answer: An organised collection of structured data that can be easily accessed managed and updated
rubric: A database stores related data in an organised structure — enabling efficient retrieval and management.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: In a database a record is ___
options: A heading row|A complete set of related fields for one entry (e.g. one student's full details)|A single piece of data|A table name
answer: A complete set of related fields for one entry (e.g. one student's full details)
rubric: A record is one complete row in a database table — all data about a single entity.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A field in a database is ___
options: A whole row of data|A whole database|A single category of information (e.g. Name Age or Email)|A table
answer: A single category of information (e.g. Name Age or Email)
rubric: A field is one attribute column in a database table — e.g. 'DateOfBirth' holds one type of data.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The =MAX() function in a spreadsheet returns ___
options: The average|The sum|The smallest value|The largest value in a range
answer: The largest value in a range
rubric: MAX() finds the highest number in a specified range — e.g. =MAX(C1:C10).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Filtering data in a spreadsheet allows you to ___
options: Delete data|Display only the rows that meet specific criteria|Add new columns|Print selected rows
answer: Display only the rows that meet specific criteria
rubric: Filtering temporarily hides rows that do not match the criteria — showing only relevant records.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The default file extension for Microsoft Excel workbooks is ___
options: .docx|.pptx|.xlsx|.pdf
rubric: Microsoft Excel 2007+ uses .xlsx as its default file format.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Rows in a spreadsheet are identified by ___
options: Letters (A B C…)|Numbers (1 2 3…)|Symbols|Colours
rubric: Rows are numbered (1, 2, 3…) and columns are lettered (A, B, C…) in standard spreadsheets.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Columns in a spreadsheet are identified by ___
options: Numbers|Colours|Letters (A B C…)|Symbols
rubric: Columns use letters (A–Z, then AA, AB, etc.) in Excel and most spreadsheet software.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A primary key in a database table is ___
options: The most important field|A unique identifier for each record (e.g. Student ID)|The first column|The largest value
answer: A unique identifier for each record (e.g. Student ID)
rubric: A primary key uniquely identifies each record — no two rows can have the same primary key value.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Relative cell references in a spreadsheet (like A1) ___
options: Stay fixed when a formula is copied|Change relative to the formula's new position when copied|Delete the cell|Always refer to row 1
answer: Change relative to the formula's new position when copied
rubric: Relative references adjust automatically when formulas are copied to new cells.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A pivot table in a spreadsheet is used to ___
options: Change the theme|Summarise and analyse large datasets interactively|Edit text|Print labels
answer: Summarise and analyse large datasets interactively
rubric: Pivot tables quickly summarise, group and analyse large data sets without complex formulas.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: =COUNT(A1:A10) in Excel counts ___
options: The sum of A1 to A10|Only text cells|The number of cells containing numeric values in A1 to A10|The largest value
answer: The number of cells containing numeric values in A1 to A10
rubric: COUNT counts how many cells in a range contain numbers — not text or blank cells.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Conditional formatting in a spreadsheet ___
options: Prints in colour only|Automatically formats cells based on their values (e.g. red for values below zero)|Changes all fonts|Is used to merge cells
answer: Automatically formats cells based on their values (e.g. red for values below zero)
rubric: Conditional formatting applies visual rules (colour, bold) based on cell content — highlighting patterns.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The internet is ___
options: A single website|A global network of interconnected computers sharing information|A type of computer|A software program
answer: A global network of interconnected computers sharing information
rubric: The internet is the worldwide network connecting billions of devices and enabling data exchange.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The World Wide Web (WWW) is ___
options: The same as the internet|A system of interlinked web pages and sites accessed via the internet|A type of computer|An email service
answer: A system of interlinked web pages and sites accessed via the internet
rubric: The Web is a service that runs ON the internet — a collection of interconnected hypertext pages.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is ___
options: A type of computer virus|The web address used to locate a specific page on the internet|A wireless network|An email attachment
answer: The web address used to locate a specific page on the internet
rubric: A URL (e.g. https://www.edu.ng) is the address identifying the location of a web resource.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: HTTPS in a web address means the website uses ___
options: HTTP protocol only|A secure (encrypted) connection — the 'S' stands for Secure|A slow connection|An old protocol
answer: A secure (encrypted) connection — the 'S' stands for Secure
rubric: HTTPS (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure) encrypts communication — essential for safe online transactions.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Wi-Fi allows computers to ___
options: Print documents|Connect to a network wirelessly using radio waves|Store more data|Run faster
answer: Connect to a network wirelessly using radio waves
rubric: Wi-Fi uses radio frequency signals to provide wireless network/internet access.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A search engine is a website that ___
options: Sends emails|Stores files|Helps users find information on the internet by indexing web pages|Designs websites
answer: Helps users find information on the internet by indexing web pages
rubric: Search engines (Google, Bing) crawl and index the web — returning ranked results for search queries.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: ISP stands for ___
options: Internet Software Program|Internet Service Provider (a company that provides internet access)|International System Protocol|Internet Speed Performance
answer: Internet Service Provider (a company that provides internet access)
rubric: An ISP (e.g. MTN, Airtel, Spectranet) provides internet connectivity to homes and businesses.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Email is short for ___
options: Easy Mail|Electronic Mail|External Mail|Enhanced Mail
rubric: Email = Electronic Mail — digital messages sent and received over the internet.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The CC field in an email stands for ___
options: Confidential Copy|Carbon Copy (sends a copy to additional recipients)|Cancelled Copy|Computer Copy
rubric: CC (Carbon Copy) sends a visible copy of the email to additional recipients.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An email attachment is ___
options: A virus|The email subject line|A file (document image etc.) included with the email message|The email signature
answer: A file (document image etc.) included with the email message
rubric: Attachments are files (documents, photos, spreadsheets) sent along with an email message.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Phishing is a cybercrime where ___
options: Hackers physically steal computers|Criminals send fake emails or websites to trick users into revealing passwords or personal info|Viruses are spread through USB drives|Spam is sent
answer: Criminals send fake emails or websites to trick users into revealing passwords or personal info
rubric: Phishing uses deceptive messages mimicking trusted sources to steal credentials and financial data.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Social media platforms are primarily used for ___
options: Official government communication only|Sharing content connecting with people and communicating online|Writing academic papers|Managing databases
answer: Sharing content connecting with people and communicating online
rubric: Social media (Facebook, Instagram, X/Twitter) enables content sharing and online social interaction.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Downloading means ___
options: Sending a file from your computer to the internet|Receiving a file from the internet to your device|Deleting a file|Compressing a file
answer: Receiving a file from the internet to your device
rubric: Downloading transfers data FROM the internet/network TO your local device.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Uploading means ___
options: Deleting a file from the internet|Sending a file FROM your device TO a server or the internet|Printing a file|Saving a file locally
answer: Sending a file FROM your device TO a server or the internet
rubric: Uploading transfers data FROM your device TO a server, cloud or the internet.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Cloud storage allows you to ___
options: Store files only on a USB drive|Store files on remote internet servers accessible from any device anywhere|Increase computer RAM|Speed up the processor
answer: Store files on remote internet servers accessible from any device anywhere
rubric: Cloud storage (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) keeps files on remote servers — accessible via internet.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Spam emails are ___
options: Important official messages|Unsolicited bulk messages often advertising or carrying malware|Personal emails from friends|Work emails
answer: Unsolicited bulk messages often advertising or carrying malware
rubric: Spam is unwanted, unsolicited mass email — often advertising, scams or phishing attempts.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Cyberbullying refers to ___
options: Physical fighting at school|Using digital technology to harass threaten or humiliate others online|Technical software bugs|Network problems
answer: Using digital technology to harass threaten or humiliate others online
rubric: Cyberbullying uses online platforms (social media, messaging) to intimidate or harm others.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A strong password should ___
options: Be your date of birth|Be a simple word|Be a mix of upper and lower case letters numbers and symbols of at least 8 characters|Be shared with friends
answer: Be a mix of upper and lower case letters numbers and symbols of at least 8 characters
rubric: Strong passwords are long, complex and unique — mixing character types makes them hard to crack.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Video conferencing tools like Zoom or Microsoft Teams allow ___
options: Only text messaging|Real-time face-to-face video and audio communication between multiple users remotely|Only file sharing|Only email
answer: Real-time face-to-face video and audio communication between multiple users remotely
rubric: Video conferencing enables real-time visual and audio meetings regardless of location.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is an example of an e-commerce activity?
options: Reading a news article|Watching a YouTube video|Buying goods or services online (e.g. ordering from Jumia or Konga)|Playing an offline game
answer: Buying goods or services online (e.g. ordering from Jumia or Konga)
rubric: E-commerce is commercial transactions conducted electronically — buying/selling online.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A firewall in computing is ___
options: A physical wall in a data centre|Software or hardware that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic to prevent unauthorised access|An antivirus program|A password manager
answer: Software or hardware that monitors and controls incoming and outgoing network traffic to prevent unauthorised access
rubric: Firewalls enforce access control rules — blocking malicious traffic while allowing legitimate communication.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Two-factor authentication (2FA) improves security by ___
options: Requiring two computers|Requiring a second verification step (e.g. a code sent to your phone) in addition to your password|Doubling the password length|Using two email accounts
answer: Requiring a second verification step (e.g. a code sent to your phone) in addition to your password
rubric: 2FA adds an extra identity verification layer — even if a password is stolen, the account stays protected.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Ransomware is malware that ___
options: Speeds up the computer|Encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to restore access|Improves internet speed|Removes all viruses
answer: Encrypts a victim's files and demands payment to restore access
rubric: Ransomware locks or encrypts files and demands a ransom — organisations and individuals are targets.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Spyware is software that ___
options: Protects your computer|Secretly collects your personal information and sends it to a third party without consent|Organises your files|Speeds up your browser
answer: Secretly collects your personal information and sends it to a third party without consent
rubric: Spyware runs covertly — recording keystrokes, browsing habits and personal data.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Identity theft online occurs when ___
options: Someone deletes your files|A criminal steals your personal information to impersonate you and commit fraud|Your computer crashes|A website is blocked
answer: A criminal steals your personal information to impersonate you and commit fraud
rubric: Online identity theft uses stolen personal data (name, ID, financial info) to commit fraud.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: You should NOT share your password with ___
options: Your parent in an emergency|Your IT teacher when troubleshooting|Anyone else — passwords are private|The school admin only
rubric: Passwords are personal — sharing them puts your accounts at risk of unauthorised access.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A Trojan horse in computing is ___
options: A horse-themed game|Malware disguised as legitimate software — once installed it causes harm|An antivirus tool|A network protocol
answer: Malware disguised as legitimate software — once installed it causes harm
rubric: Trojan horses appear useful but contain malicious code — installed unwittingly by the user.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Updating software and operating systems regularly helps to ___
options: Slow down the computer|Patch security vulnerabilities that could be exploited by hackers|Use more memory|Delete old files
answer: Patch security vulnerabilities that could be exploited by hackers
rubric: Regular updates fix security flaws — unpatched software is a prime entry point for cyberattacks.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) is used to ___
options: Store files|Encrypt internet traffic and protect privacy when browsing online|Print documents|Speed up computer games
answer: Encrypt internet traffic and protect privacy when browsing online
rubric: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel — masking the user's IP and securing data in transit.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: You receive an email asking for your bank details to claim a prize. This is most likely ___
options: A genuine promotion|A phishing scam — you should delete it and report it|A message from your bank|An official government notice
answer: A phishing scam — you should delete it and report it
rubric: Unsolicited emails requesting personal or financial details are classic phishing attempts — never respond.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Data privacy means ___
options: Sharing all personal data freely|The right to control how your personal information is collected used and shared|Deleting all online accounts|Using the internet without a password
answer: The right to control how your personal information is collected used and shared
rubric: Data privacy gives individuals control over their personal information online.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attack ___
options: Steals passwords|Sends spam emails|Overwhelms a server with huge volumes of traffic making it unavailable to legitimate users|Installs spyware
answer: Overwhelms a server with huge volumes of traffic making it unavailable to legitimate users
rubric: DDoS floods a server with requests from multiple sources — crashing or degrading the service.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of the following is the SAFEST online practice?
options: Using the same password everywhere|Clicking all links in emails|Downloading programs from unknown websites|Using unique strong passwords and avoiding suspicious links
answer: Using unique strong passwords and avoiding suspicious links
rubric: Safe online habits: unique strong passwords, scepticism of links and verified downloads.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The padlock icon in a web browser address bar means ___
options: The site is blocked|The connection is encrypted (HTTPS) and relatively secure|The site is free|The site is government-owned
answer: The connection is encrypted (HTTPS) and relatively secure
rubric: A padlock (🔒) indicates the site uses SSL/TLS encryption — data is transmitted securely.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Screen time management for young people is important because excessive screen time can ___
options: Improve eyesight|Lead to eye strain poor posture sleep disruption and reduced physical activity|Increase intelligence|Improve fitness
answer: Lead to eye strain poor posture sleep disruption and reduced physical activity
rubric: Excessive screen time is linked to physical and mental health issues — balance is recommended.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: What should you do if you are cyberbullied?
options: Bully back online|Keep it secret|Tell a trusted adult and block the bully|Delete all social media accounts permanently
answer: Tell a trusted adult and block the bully
rubric: Victims of cyberbullying should report it to a trusted adult, block the bully and keep evidence.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Copyright law protects ___
options: Only physical property|Original creative works (text music images software etc.) from being used without the creator's permission|Public domain content|Facts and ideas
answer: Original creative works (text music images software etc.) from being used without the creator's permission
rubric: Copyright law grants creators exclusive rights to their work — unauthorised use is infringement.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Logging out of your account on a shared computer is important because it ___
options: Speeds up the computer|Prevents other users from accessing your personal account and data|Saves battery|Deletes your files
answer: Prevents other users from accessing your personal account and data
rubric: Always log out on shared devices — leaving an account open allows others to misuse it.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An ethical hacker (white-hat hacker) ___
options: Steals data for personal gain|Is hired to find security weaknesses in systems with the owner's permission|Spreads viruses|Sells stolen passwords
answer: Is hired to find security weaknesses in systems with the owner's permission
rubric: Ethical hackers (penetration testers) probe systems legally to find and fix vulnerabilities.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which of these is a good habit for protecting your data online?
options: Sharing personal info on public posts|Using public Wi-Fi for banking|Regularly backing up your files and using antivirus software|Never updating passwords
answer: Regularly backing up your files and using antivirus software
rubric: Regular backups and antivirus protection are essential data safety habits.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Digital citizenship refers to ___
options: Citizenship of a tech company|Using technology responsibly safely and ethically in society|Programming skills|Hardware knowledge
answer: Using technology responsibly safely and ethically in society
rubric: Digital citizenship covers responsible, respectful and safe use of technology in everyday life.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Netiquette means ___
options: Computer networking|Acceptable and polite behaviour when communicating online|A type of antivirus|Fast internet speed
answer: Acceptable and polite behaviour when communicating online
rubric: Netiquette (internet etiquette) includes respectful online communication — no insults, caps-lock shouting, etc.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Fake news online refers to ___
options: Old news stories|False or misleading information presented as true news|News from foreign countries|News that is not interesting
answer: False or misleading information presented as true news
rubric: Fake news is intentionally misleading content designed to deceive — a serious challenge in the digital age.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Before sharing information online you should ___
options: Share immediately to be first|Verify it is accurate from a reliable source|Post it on all platforms|Ignore the source
answer: Verify it is accurate from a reliable source
rubric: Critical digital literacy requires verifying information from credible sources before sharing.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Screen addiction refers to ___
options: Using the computer at work|An unhealthy compulsive need to use digital devices that interferes with daily life|Watching TV occasionally|Using the internet for research
answer: An unhealthy compulsive need to use digital devices that interferes with daily life
rubric: Digital/screen addiction is excessive device use that negatively impacts health, relationships and school.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The digital divide refers to ___
options: A broken computer screen|The gap between people who have access to digital technology and those who do not|Different software versions|Fast and slow internet
answer: The gap between people who have access to digital technology and those who do not
rubric: The digital divide is the inequality between those with and without access to digital tools and internet.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Intellectual property online includes ___
options: Only government documents|Creative works owned by their creator — music images text software — protected by copyright|Public domain works only|Free-to-use images only
answer: Creative works owned by their creator — music images text software — protected by copyright
rubric: Intellectual property (IP) law protects creative works — using them without permission is infringement.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Plagiarism in digital work means ___
options: Creating original content|Citing all sources correctly|Using someone else's work as your own without credit|Sharing licensed content
answer: Using someone else's work as your own without credit
rubric: Plagiarism — copying others' work without attribution — is dishonest and violates copyright.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Sharing another person's private photos online without consent is ___
options: Acceptable if they are a celebrity|Harmless fun|Illegal and a serious violation of privacy — called non-consensual image sharing|A form of digital backup
answer: Illegal and a serious violation of privacy — called non-consensual image sharing
rubric: Non-consensual sharing of private images violates privacy laws and causes serious harm.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: ICT contributes to sustainable development by ___
options: Increasing electricity consumption only|Enabling e-learning remote health services smart farming and reducing paper use|Making everyone rich|Replacing all workers
answer: Enabling e-learning remote health services smart farming and reducing paper use
rubric: ICT tools support education, healthcare, agriculture and environmental sustainability.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The right to access information online in Nigeria is supported by ___

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: E-government services in Nigeria allow citizens to ___
options: Only pay taxes offline|Access government services online — like applying for NIN BVN or checking results|Vote in elections only|Drive without a licence
answer: Access government services online — like applying for NIN BVN or checking results
rubric: E-government platforms (NIMC, JAMB portal, tax portals) bring government services online.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A digital footprint is ___
options: A computer mouse trackpad|The trail of data left by a person's online activity — websites visited posts made accounts created|A type of virus|A printer mark
answer: The trail of data left by a person's online activity — websites visited posts made accounts created
rubric: A digital footprint is the permanent online record of a person's internet activity.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: ICT skills are important for future careers because ___
options: Only IT companies need them|Most modern jobs and industries require digital literacy and computer skills|They replace education|They are optional everywhere
answer: Most modern jobs and industries require digital literacy and computer skills
rubric: Digital literacy is a core 21st-century skill — required across nearly all professions.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Which organisation regulates ICT and internet services in Nigeria?
options: NAFDAC|NCC (Nigerian Communications Commission)|INEC|CBN
rubric: The NCC regulates telecommunications and internet services in Nigeria.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An algorithm is ___
options: A type of computer|A step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem or completing a task|A programming language|A type of virus
answer: A step-by-step set of instructions for solving a problem or completing a task
rubric: An algorithm is a finite, ordered sequence of instructions for solving a problem — the basis of programming.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Coding (programming) means ___
options: Typing text in a document|Writing instructions in a programming language that a computer can follow|Designing a poster|Using a spreadsheet
answer: Writing instructions in a programming language that a computer can follow
rubric: Coding involves writing source code in a language (Python, Scratch, JavaScript) to create programs.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Scratch is a programming language designed for ___
options: Professional software engineers only|Young learners — using drag-and-drop visual coding blocks|Hacking|Database management
answer: Young learners — using drag-and-drop visual coding blocks
rubric: Scratch (MIT) is a visual, block-based programming environment designed to teach coding to beginners.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A program is ___
options: A TV schedule|A set of instructions written in a programming language that a computer executes|A school timetable|A type of hardware
answer: A set of instructions written in a programming language that a computer executes
rubric: A program is a complete set of coded instructions that directs a computer to perform tasks.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A variable in programming is ___
options: A type of loop|A fixed value that never changes|A named storage location holding a value that can change during a program|A type of screen
answer: A named storage location holding a value that can change during a program
rubric: Variables store data values (numbers, text) that can be read and modified by a program.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: In programming a loop is used to ___
options: Skip instructions|Repeat a block of instructions multiple times|Connect to the internet|Save a file
answer: Repeat a block of instructions multiple times
rubric: Loops (for, while) repeat code — avoiding repeated identical lines and automating repetitive tasks.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An 'if' statement in programming is used for ___
options: Repeating code|Making decisions — executing code only when a condition is true|Storing data|Printing output
answer: Making decisions — executing code only when a condition is true
rubric: If-statements add conditional logic — they branch program flow based on whether a condition is true.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A flowchart is a diagram that shows ___
options: Computer hardware connections|The logical sequence of steps in an algorithm or program using shapes and arrows|Database tables|Network connections
answer: The logical sequence of steps in an algorithm or program using shapes and arrows
rubric: Flowcharts use standardised symbols (ovals, diamonds, rectangles, arrows) to visualise algorithm logic.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Debugging in programming means ___
options: Writing new code|Testing a program for speed|Finding and fixing errors (bugs) in a program|Saving a file
answer: Finding and fixing errors (bugs) in a program
rubric: Debugging is the process of identifying, analysing and correcting errors in code.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A bug in programming is ___
options: A type of computer virus|An error or flaw in a program that causes incorrect or unexpected behaviour|A hardware failure|A missing file
answer: An error or flaw in a program that causes incorrect or unexpected behaviour
rubric: A bug is a coding mistake that produces unintended results — debugging is the process of fixing bugs.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: HTML is mainly used for ___
options: Database management|Designing printed documents|Creating the structure and content of web pages|Programming games
answer: Creating the structure and content of web pages
rubric: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) defines web page structure using tags — the foundation of the web.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Pseudocode is ___
options: A type of virus|Actual code that runs on a computer|An informal high-level description of an algorithm using plain English before writing real code|A database query
answer: An informal high-level description of an algorithm using plain English before writing real code
rubric: Pseudocode bridges planning and coding — using plain language to describe logic without formal syntax.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An input in a program receives data from ___
options: Only the keyboard|The user or another source (keyboard file sensor)|Only stored files|Only the CPU
answer: The user or another source (keyboard file sensor)
rubric: Program input is any data from the user or an external source — keyboard, files, sensors, etc.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: An output in a program ___
options: Takes in data|Processes data internally|Displays or sends results to the user or another system|Stores data only
answer: Displays or sends results to the user or another system
rubric: Program output returns results — to a screen (display), file, printer or other system.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: The three basic control structures in programming are ___
options: Input Process Output|Sequence Selection (if) and Iteration (loop)|Save Open Close|Start Stop Pause
rubric: All programs are built from: Sequence (order), Selection (decision) and Iteration (repetition).

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Python is a popular programming language known for ___
options: Being the oldest language|Only running on Apple computers|Being easy to read write and learn — widely used in AI web development and science|Only making games
answer: Being easy to read write and learn — widely used in AI web development and science
rubric: Python is renowned for its readable syntax — one of the most widely used and versatile languages.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A syntax error in programming occurs when ___
options: The program runs too slowly|Code is written that violates the grammar rules of the programming language|The internet is slow|A virus attacks
answer: Code is written that violates the grammar rules of the programming language
rubric: Syntax errors are grammar mistakes in code — e.g. missing brackets or misspelled keywords.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: A function (or procedure) in programming is ___
options: A type of loop only|A named reusable block of code that performs a specific task|A database table|A file format
answer: A named reusable block of code that performs a specific task
rubric: Functions encapsulate reusable logic — called by name to avoid repeating the same code.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: In Scratch the 'when green flag clicked' block ___

rubric: In Scratch, the green flag is the run button — 'when green flag clicked' starts the script.

subject: Digital Technologies
stem: Computational thinking skills include ___
options: Only mathematics|Decomposition pattern recognition abstraction and algorithm design|Only coding|Only database design
answer: Decomposition pattern recognition abstraction and algorithm design
rubric: Computational thinking: break problems down (decompose), find patterns, abstract key details, design algorithms.
